findings.title: Memory past_context reaches only researchers + PM, not the four analysts, trader, or risk debaters
findings.whats_missing: propagation.create_initial_state injects past_context into AgentState, but only bull_researcher.py (L17-22), bear_researcher.py (L17-22), and portfolio_manager.py (L36-41) read state['past_context']. The market/news/sentiment/fundamentals analysts, the trader, and all three risk debaters never read it. The lessons from prior decisions therefore never shape the evidence-gathering or the trade proposal — only the debate and final synthesis. This is a major reason memory has little measurable learning effect.
findings.end_goal: Every agent whose reasoning benefits from prior outcomes (at minimum the analysts and trader) optionally receives a compact past_context block, gated by token budget, so prior lessons influence what evidence is gathered and how the trade is sized — not just the closing synthesis.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/agents/utils/agent_states.py:75 defines past_context; only consumed in bull_researcher.py:17, bear_researcher.py:17, managers/portfolio_manager.py:36; absent from analysts/*, trader/trader.py, risk_mgmt/*

findings.title: Pending forecasts only resolve when the same ticker is re-run, leaving the ledger near-100% unresolved
findings.whats_missing: _resolve_pending_entries (trading_graph.py:278-316) filters get_pending_entries() to e['ticker'] == ticker, so a forecast for AAPL is only ever scored when AAPL is run again. The docstring even admits 'only same-ticker entries are resolved per run.' With a rotating universe this means almost nothing resolves (matches the reported 4582 forecasts / 0 resolved). The reflection→learning loop is effectively dead.
findings.end_goal: A standalone resolver sweeps ALL pending entries whose holding window has elapsed (independent of which ticker is being traded today), fetches returns, writes reflections, and backfills the ledger, so resolved-rate trends toward 100% and the reflection corpus becomes usable.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/graph/trading_graph.py:288 `pending = [e for e in self.memory_log.get_pending_entries() if e['ticker'] == ticker]`; docstring L285-287 acknowledges the trade-off

findings.title: parse_rating fallback grabs the first rating-like word in prose, mislabeling decisions
findings.whats_missing: The second pass in parse_rating (rating.py:42-47) returns the first 5-tier word found anywhere in the text. Tested live: 'We should overweight tech and Sell this name' returns 'Overweight' even though the decision is Sell; 'Credit rating: AAA. Recommendation: Sell' makes the label regex capture 'AAA' first. The label regex `rating.*?[:\-]...` (L25) is per-line and stops at the first separator, so incidental uses of 'rating'/'overweight'/'buy' in prose can dominate. The PM render path mitigates this (always emits `**Rating**: X`), but parse_rating also runs on free-text fallback output and on the memory-log final_trade_decision, where misfires silently mislabel stored entries.
findings.end_goal: parse_rating anchors on an explicit, render-emitted label (e.g. a line that is exactly `**Rating**:`/`**Recommendation**:`/`**Action**:`), prefers the LAST such label, and only falls back to whole-text word scan as a last resort — with unit tests for the adversarial prose cases above.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/agents/utils/rating.py:25,42-48; verified misfires via live regex eval on 'We should overweight tech and Sell this name' -> Overweight

findings.title: get_sentiment_context tool and the 'social' ToolNode are dead wiring after the sentiment redesign
findings.whats_missing: create_sentiment_analyst pre-fetches news+StockTwits+Reddit and does NOT bind_tools, and should_continue_social always routes straight to cleanup (conditional_logic.py:22-30). Yet trading_graph._create_tool_nodes still builds a 'social' ToolNode with get_news + get_sentiment_context (L182-188), and get_sentiment_context is exported/registered but no agent can ever call it. This is unreachable code that implies a capability that doesn't run.
findings.end_goal: Either remove the unused 'social' ToolNode and get_sentiment_context from the agent path, or actually route the sentiment analyst's vendor sentiment through get_sentiment_context so the registered vendor chain is used. No registered tool should be unreachable.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/graph/trading_graph.py:182-188 builds social ToolNode; conditional_logic.py:22-30 routes social straight to clear; news_data_tools.py:65-78 defines get_sentiment_context with no caller

findings.title: Tool-calling analysts silently emit empty report strings when the last message still has tool_calls
findings.whats_missing: In market/news/fundamentals analysts the report is only set when len(result.tool_calls)==0 (e.g. market_analyst.py:89-94). If the model ends a turn still requesting tools and the graph hits the recursion limit, or returns content alongside tool_calls, the report field stays '' and is written to state with no warning. Downstream researchers/PM then reason over a blank market_report/news_report/fundamentals_report, and the saved packet silently lacks that section — a correctness and observability gap that can flip a decision.
findings.end_goal: Each analyst guarantees a non-empty report (or an explicit '<no report produced: reason>' marker) before returning, logs a warning when content is empty after tool exhaustion, and the packet schema validates that required report sections are present.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/agents/analysts/market_analyst.py:87-95; news_analyst.py:73-81; fundamentals_analyst.py:59-67 all share the `if len(result.tool_calls)==0: report=result.content` pattern with empty default

findings.title: No self-critique / verification node exists anywhere in the agent pipeline
findings.whats_missing: The pipeline goes analysts -> bull/bear -> RM -> trader -> risk -> PM with no node that adversarially checks the final decision for hallucinated figures, internal contradictions, or unsupported claims against the source reports. The market-readiness goal explicitly calls for 'self-checking' research, but the only retrospective check is the post-hoc Reflector after the outcome is known.
findings.end_goal: A self-critique node runs before the PM finalizes (or gates it), re-reading the analyst reports and flagging any number/claim in the thesis not grounded in the evidence blocks, forcing a revise-or-justify pass. Failures are surfaced in the packet and can downgrade conviction.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/graph/setup.py:87-216 graph wiring has no critique node; reflection.py only runs after outcome is known

findings.title: Macro, options-flow, and insider signals are bolted onto existing analysts rather than dedicated analysts
findings.whats_missing: get_macro_context is an optional tool shared by market+news analysts, get_insider_transactions is one tool on the news analyst, and there is no options/positioning analyst at all. The audit brief calls out a dedicated macro/options/insider analyst as a gap. Macro regime and insider/options positioning are first-class trading signals that currently get diluted inside general-purpose prompts and may never be called.
findings.end_goal: Dedicated, optionally-selectable analyst lanes for (a) macro/rates regime, (b) insider transactions + ownership changes, and (c) options flow / positioning, each with its own prompt, tools, and report section, selectable via selected_analysts so a run can deepen the dimensions that matter for a given ticker.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/agents/analysts/ only has market/news/sentiment/fundamentals; macro is a shared tool (market_analyst.py:24-28, news_analyst.py:25-30); insider is one news tool; no options analyst exists

findings.title: Structured-output free-text fallback returns response.content which can be a non-string list (Anthropic)
findings.whats_missing: invoke_structured_or_freetext returns plain_llm.invoke(prompt).content directly (structured.py:73-74). For Anthropic and some providers, message content is a list of content blocks, not a str. RM/Trader/PM then store a list into investment_plan/trader_investment_plan/final_trade_decision, which is later string-formatted into other prompts and parsed by parse_rating (which calls .splitlines()). A list has no splitlines() — this can crash or stringify oddly precisely on the fallback path that fires when a weak/edge provider is in use.
findings.end_goal: The fallback normalizes content to a clean string (joining text blocks) before returning, with a unit test covering list-shaped content, so downstream rendering and parse_rating never receive a non-str.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/agents/utils/structured.py:73-74 `response = plain_llm.invoke(prompt); return response.content` with no str coercion

findings.title: Debate/risk 'rounds' comments are wrong and max_debate_rounds semantics are off-by-one
findings.whats_missing: should_continue_debate checks count >= 2*max_debate_rounds with comment '# 3 rounds of back-and-forth between 2 agents' (conditional_logic.py:51-53). With default max_debate_rounds=1 the bull and bear each speak exactly once (count reaches 2), which is one exchange, not three rounds. Same in should_continue_risk_analysis (L59-69): comment says '3 rounds' but each of the 3 debaters speaks once. The comments misdescribe behavior and the multiplier makes the config knob non-obvious.
findings.end_goal: Comments accurately describe the loop, and the round math is documented (or refactored) so max_debate_rounds=N yields N full bull/bear exchanges as a reader would expect.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/graph/conditional_logic.py:51-53 and 61-63 comments vs. actual single-pass behavior

findings.title: Bear researcher prompt hardcodes 'stock' despite asset_type/crypto support
findings.whats_missing: bear_researcher.py computes target_label ('stock'/'asset') but the prompt body still says 'macroeconomic threats that could hinder the stock's performance' (L33) with a literal 'stock'. For crypto runs the bull prompt is fully asset-neutral but the bear prompt leaks 'stock', producing inconsistent framing between the two debaters on crypto.
findings.end_goal: Bear prompt uses target_label consistently everywhere (matching bull_researcher), so crypto vs stock framing is symmetric across both debaters.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/agents/researchers/bear_researcher.py:33 literal "the stock's performance" while L16 computes target_label

findings.title: Researcher/risk prompts still label the sentiment report as 'Social media sentiment report'
findings.whats_missing: The sentiment analyst was redesigned to aggregate news+StockTwits+Reddit (sentiment_analyst.py module docstring), but bull/bear/aggressive/conservative/neutral prompts all still inject it as 'Social media sentiment report' / 'Social Media Sentiment Report' (bull_researcher.py:41, bear:43, aggressive_debator.py:27, etc.). The label undersells the report (it includes institutional news framing) and is inconsistent with the renamed agent.
findings.end_goal: All downstream prompts label it 'Sentiment report (news + StockTwits + Reddit)' or simply 'Sentiment report', matching the redesigned multi-source analyst.
findings.evidence: bull_researcher.py:41, bear_researcher.py:43, risk_mgmt/aggressive_debator.py:27, conservative_debator.py:27, neutral_debator.py:27 all say 'Social media'/'Social Media'

findings.title: Risk debaters and bull/bear researchers produce only free prose with no structured signal extraction
findings.whats_missing: Only RM/Trader/PM use schemas. The bull/bear and the 3 risk debaters return raw response.content concatenated into history strings. There is no structured capture of each side's conviction, key claims, or which risks were raised — so the PM/RM must re-derive everything from prose, and there is no machine-readable record of what each debater argued for later analysis or calibration.
findings.end_goal: Debaters optionally emit a small structured payload (stance, top-3 claims, confidence) alongside prose, stored in the packet, enabling later calibration of which debate arguments correlated with good outcomes.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/agents/researchers/bull_researcher.py:49-51 and risk_mgmt/*_debator.py return only f'...: {response.content}' with no schema; schemas.py only covers RM/Trader/PM

findings.title: 5-tier rating scale text is duplicated in RM and PM prompts and again in schema field descriptions
findings.whats_missing: The Buy/Overweight/Hold/Underweight/Sell scale with descriptions is hand-written in research_manager.py:32-39 and again in portfolio_manager.py:49-54, and a third near-copy lives in the ResearchPlan/PortfolioDecision field descriptions (schemas.py:68-88,178-205). The three copies can drift (e.g. RM says 'recommend taking or growing the position' for Buy; PM says 'enter or add to position'). RATINGS_5_TIER in rating.py is the canonical list but the prose descriptions aren't centralized.
findings.end_goal: A single shared constant/helper renders the rating-scale block, consumed by both manager prompts and referenced from the schema, so the wording can never drift across the three agents.
findings.evidence: research_manager.py:32-39, portfolio_manager.py:49-54, schemas.py:68-88 contain three independent copies of the scale

findings.title: Trader emits 3-tier Buy/Hold/Sell while RM/PM use 5-tier, with no reconciliation of Overweight/Underweight
findings.whats_missing: TraderAction is 3-tier (schemas.py:40-51) but the RM hands the trader a 5-tier recommendation and the PM re-expands to 5-tier afterward. An RM 'Overweight' collapses to the trader's 'Buy' and a separate 'sizing' string, then the PM independently re-rates. There is no explicit mapping documented, so Overweight/Underweight conviction can silently disappear at the trader and be re-invented at the PM, weakening sizing fidelity.
findings.end_goal: A documented, tested mapping between the 5-tier recommendation, the trader's 3-tier action + sizing, and the PM's 5-tier rating, so conviction strength is preserved end-to-end rather than lossily round-tripped.
findings.evidence: schemas.py:40-51 TraderAction (3-tier) vs PortfolioRating (5-tier) L30-37; trader.py consumes 5-tier investment_plan but outputs 3-tier

findings.title: Prefetch analysts hardcode magic numbers (14d window, [:6] indicators, 7000-char truncation, look_back 20/30/5)
findings.whats_missing: create_prefetched_market_analyst hardcodes a 14-day price window, indicator_names[:6], look_back 20, and get_macro_context(...,30,5) (market_analyst.py:114-133). _truncate_block hardcodes max_chars=7000 in three separate files (news_analyst.py:86, fundamentals_analyst.py:72, and again as a private copy). sentiment uses limit=30 and _seven_days_back. These are scattered, undocumented, and duplicated rather than config-driven.
findings.end_goal: These windows/limits/truncation sizes live in config (or a single shared constants module) with names and defaults, and _truncate_block is defined once and imported, so overnight context budgets are tunable and consistent.
findings.evidence: market_analyst.py:113-133; news_analyst.py:86-90 and fundamentals_analyst.py:72-76 each redefine _truncate_block with max_chars=7000; sentiment_analyst.py:35,58

findings.title: Tool-calling and prefetch analyst variants give materially different instructions for the same lane
findings.whats_missing: For each lane there are two prompts that diverge: e.g. the tool-calling market analyst asks for 'up to 8 indicators' and a 'very detailed and nuanced report', while the prefetch variant fixes 6 indicators and asks for a 'concise' report with a fixed 6-point structure. The two variants produce reports of different depth/shape depending only on whether the lane is tool-free, making runs non-comparable and the saved packets inconsistent.
findings.end_goal: The tool and prefetch variants share a single canonical report contract (same required sections, same depth guidance), differing only in how data is acquired, so packets are comparable regardless of execution mode.
findings.evidence: market_analyst.py:30-59 (tool) vs 137-159 (prefetch); same divergence in news_analyst.py and fundamentals_analyst.py

findings.title: Sentiment analyst ignores asset_type for crypto and never receives past_context
findings.whats_missing: create_sentiment_analyst builds instrument_context with asset_type but its body prompt is stock-centric (Reddit subs r/stocks/r/investing, StockTwits cashtag) and does not adapt source selection for crypto; like all analysts it gets no past_context. For crypto tickers the prompt still references equity-flavored sources without acknowledging they may be sparse.
findings.end_goal: The sentiment analyst adapts its source framing and caveats by asset_type (and optionally crypto-specific communities), and can reference prior sentiment-divergence lessons via past_context.
findings.evidence: sentiment_analyst.py:47-52 reads asset_type only for instrument_context; system message L111-164 is equity-flavored with fixed subreddits

findings.title: Memory-log tag parsing is brittle to '|' or newlines in ticker/decision and to rating words containing separators
findings.whats_missing: Entries are stored as `[date | ticker | rating | pending]` and parsed by splitting on '|' (memory.py:264, 141, 193). A ticker or rating containing a '|' (or a decision whose first line happens to start with '[' and end with ']') would corrupt _parse_entry / update_with_outcome field indexing. parse_rating can also yield arbitrary capitalized words if the heuristic misfires, which then become the stored 'rating' field with no validation against RATINGS_5_TIER.
findings.end_goal: Tag fields are escaped or stored as structured JSON front-matter, the parsed rating is validated against RATINGS_5_TIER (falling back to Hold), and _parse_entry tolerates decision bodies that look like tags — with tests for pipe/newline injection.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/agents/utils/memory.py:43-47 writes tag; :264 `fields = tag_line[1:-1].split('|')`; rating stored without RATINGS_5_TIER validation

findings.title: get_insider_transactions takes only a ticker with no date window, risking stale/forward-looking data
findings.whats_missing: get_insider_transactions(ticker) has no curr_date/as-of parameter (news_data_tools.py:81-93), unlike every other tool. In a backtest/walk-forward at a past trade_date it may return insider data dated AFTER the simulated date, leaking lookahead into the news analyst's thesis — directly relevant to the weak walk-forward calibration.
findings.end_goal: The insider tool accepts an as-of date and filters out transactions after it, so historical/walk-forward runs are point-in-time correct and free of lookahead.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/agents/utils/news_data_tools.py:81-93 signature has no date arg; all other tools thread curr_date

findings.title: get_indicators swallows only ValueError and returns error strings inline as if they were data
findings.whats_missing: get_indicators catches only ValueError and appends str(e) into the results list joined with real indicator output (technical_indicators_tools.py:31-35). Non-ValueError exceptions propagate (could stall a tool loop), and caught errors are concatenated as if they were indicator data, so the LLM may treat an error message as an indicator reading. There's no logging.
findings.end_goal: Errors are caught broadly, logged, and clearly demarcated (e.g. '<indicator X unavailable: reason>') so the model never confuses an error string for data, and the tool never raises mid-loop.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/agents/utils/technical_indicators_tools.py:30-35 `except ValueError as e: results.append(str(e))`

findings.title: agent_utils helpers lack focused tests and the file has trailing dead whitespace
findings.whats_missing: build_instrument_context and get_language_instruction (agent_utils.py:38-67) and the dedupe logic in create_msg_delete (L69-92) carry subtle behavior (exchange-suffix preservation, English short-circuit, duplicate RemoveMessage guard) but I see no dedicated unit test asserting these. The file also ends with stray blank lines L94-96.
findings.end_goal: Unit tests cover get_language_instruction English short-circuit, build_instrument_context crypto vs stock + suffix hint, and create_msg_delete dedup of overlapping/empty ids; trailing whitespace removed.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/agents/utils/agent_utils.py:38-92; trailing blank lines at 94-96; no test file targets these helpers directly

findings.title: Structured-output fallback silently doubles LLM cost with no counter/metric
findings.whats_missing: When structured_llm.invoke fails, invoke_structured_or_freetext logs a warning then calls plain_llm.invoke — a second full LLM call (structured.py:63-74). There is no counter or metric tracking how often fallback fires per agent/provider, so a provider that always fails structured output (doubling cost and latency every run) is invisible except in log noise.
findings.end_goal: Fallback frequency is counted per agent and surfaced in run observability so a chronically-failing structured provider is detected and the operator can switch models.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/agents/utils/structured.py:63-74 logs warning but emits no metric/counter

findings.title: Tool-calling analysts rely solely on the global recursion_limit with no per-analyst tool-call cap
findings.whats_missing: Tool-calling analysts loop analyst<->tools until the model stops calling tools or the global recursion_limit (100) trips (propagation.py:14, setup.py:118-123). A repetitive local model can burn many tool calls in one lane, and the empty-report bug (above) then triggers. There is no per-lane tool-call budget or repetition guard.
findings.end_goal: Each tool-calling analyst enforces a max tool-call count (config-driven) after which it is forced to summarize from data already gathered, preventing a single lane from exhausting the budget and yielding an empty report.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/graph/propagation.py:14 max_recur_limit=100; setup.py:118-123 unbounded analyst<->tools loop

findings.title: Crypto runs still invoke the fundamentals analyst even though fundamentals are unavailable
findings.whats_missing: For asset_type='crypto', the fundamentals analyst and its tools still run and the bull/bear merely add a label that fundamentals 'may be unavailable' (bull_researcher.py:23-27). This wastes an LLM call and tool fetches that route_to_vendor likely returns empty/error for crypto, and produces a low-value or fabricated-risk report section.
findings.end_goal: Crypto runs skip or replace the equity-fundamentals lane (e.g. with on-chain/tokenomics) so no run pays for a structurally empty fundamentals report.
findings.evidence: setup.py:68-72 always wires fundamentals for selected_analysts; bull_researcher.py:23-27 only relabels rather than skipping

findings.title: Reflector re-reads the entire final decision but extracts no structured lesson tags for calibration
findings.whats_missing: reflect_on_final_decision produces 2-4 sentences of free prose (reflection.py:14-57). There is no structured extraction of (which analyst was right/wrong, which signal mattered, direction-correct boolean) — so the reflection corpus can't be aggregated to answer 'which analyst/signal has historically added alpha', which is exactly what walk-forward calibration (scored 4/10) needs.
findings.end_goal: Reflection emits both prose and a small structured record (direction_correct, decisive_signal, analyst_credit) so the ledger can compute per-analyst hit rates and feed calibration/promotion.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/graph/reflection.py:20-29 prompt requests only prose; no structured field captured

findings.title: get_language_instruction reads config on every call with no caching and only a string-equality English check
findings.whats_missing: get_language_instruction calls get_config() on every invocation for every agent (agent_utils.py:47-51) and only short-circuits when the language string equals 'english' (case-insensitive). A config value like 'en' or 'English (US)' would append a redundant instruction; the repeated config reads are minor but happen per-agent-per-run.
findings.end_goal: Normalize the language value against a known set, cache the resolved instruction per run, and document accepted values, so non-English instructions only append when genuinely needed.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/agents/utils/agent_utils.py:47-51

findings.title: Deprecated social_media_analyst shim emits a DeprecationWarning on import even though the package imports it
findings.whats_missing: social_media_analyst.py raises a module-level DeprecationWarning at import (L18-23) and create_social_media_analyst also warns (sentiment_analyst.py:179-186), yet agents/__init__.py still imports create_social_media_analyst into the public namespace (__init__.py:7-10,41). Any import of the agents package may surface the warning, and the alias is kept 'for back-compat' for a single-user system with only 2 commits of history — likely unnecessary surface area.
findings.end_goal: Decide whether back-compat is needed for this private repo; if not, remove the shim module, the alias, and its __init__ export to cut dead deprecation surface. If kept, stop importing it eagerly in __init__.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/agents/analysts/social_media_analyst.py:18-23; agents/__init__.py:7-10,41; sentiment_analyst.py:170-186

findings.title: Market analyst embeds a ~25-line indicator dictionary in the system prompt on every run
findings.whats_missing: The tool-calling market analyst hardcodes the full indicator catalog with usage tips inline in the system message (market_analyst.py:31-55), spending a large fixed token block every single run even though the model only selects up to 8. This is the largest static prompt in the layer and is re-sent every market lane.
findings.end_goal: The indicator catalog lives in a compact reference the model can consult on demand (or a trimmed list), reducing fixed prompt tokens per run while preserving selection guidance.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/agents/market_analyst.py:31-55 inlines the full indicator dictionary (~1.5k tokens) in the system prompt

findings.title: Analyst stop-signal 'FINAL TRANSACTION PROPOSAL: **BUY/HOLD/SELL**' is instructed but analysts have no decision authority
findings.whats_missing: Every tool-calling analyst's wrapper system prompt instructs it to prefix with 'FINAL TRANSACTION PROPOSAL: **BUY/HOLD/SELL**' to stop the team (market_analyst.py:69-70, news/fundamentals same), but analysts are evidence-gatherers with no mandate to issue a transaction proposal. This is legacy collaborative-agent boilerplate that can pressure an analyst into prematurely emitting a BUY/HOLD/SELL it shouldn't, and the trader render preserves the same line (schemas.py:159) creating two sources of the signal.
findings.end_goal: Analyst wrapper prompts drop the transaction-proposal stop-signal (analysts only produce reports); the FINAL TRANSACTION PROPOSAL line is owned solely by the trader/PM, eliminating premature analyst directional calls.
findings.evidence: market_analyst.py:69-70, news_analyst.py:56-57, fundamentals_analyst.py:41-42 all instruct the stop-signal in evidence-gathering analysts

findings.title: get_YFin_data_online uses ticker.history() with default auto_adjust, silently dropping 'Adj Close'
findings.whats_missing: y_finance.py:24 calls ticker.history(start, end) without specifying auto_adjust. Modern yfinance defaults auto_adjust=True, which removes the 'Adj Close' column and adjusts OHLC in place. Line 37 then iterates numeric_columns including 'Adj Close' which will never be present, so the analyst-facing CSV has adjusted prices but no explicit adjusted-close column, and the column list is misleading. The cached path (stockstats_utils.load_ohlcv) explicitly sets auto_adjust=True, so the online price path and the indicator price path use different adjustment semantics for the same symbol.
findings.end_goal: Both price entry points (online CSV and cached OHLCV) declare auto_adjust explicitly and identically, document whether prices are split/dividend-adjusted, and either emit a real 'Adj Close' column or drop it from the expected-column list so headers never reference a column that cannot exist.
findings.evidence: y_finance.py:24,37; stockstats_utils.py:79-86 (auto_adjust=True only in cached path)
findings.recommended_change: Pass auto_adjust explicitly in get_YFin_data_online to match load_ohlcv, and reconcile the numeric_columns list with the actual returned columns.

findings.title: OHLCV cache filename embeds today's date, so a new file is written every calendar day and the previous day's cache is never reused
findings.whats_missing: load_ohlcv builds the cache filename as f"{symbol}-YFin-data-{start_str}-{end_str}.csv" where start_str/end_str are derived from pd.Timestamp.today(). Both shift every day, so each new calendar day produces a brand-new cache filename and re-downloads 15 years of history per symbol, while orphaning yesterday's CSVs (unbounded disk growth, no eviction). During an overnight batch across many symbols this defeats the cache and multiplies yfinance rate-limit exposure.
findings.end_goal: Cache keyed on symbol (and adjustment mode) with an explicit TTL / freshness check (e.g. mtime-based staleness like the official cache uses), reusing the existing file and only appending/refreshing the tail, plus pruning of superseded cache files so disk usage stays bounded.
findings.evidence: stockstats_utils.py:64-88 (today_date drives start_str/end_str in the filename); contrast with _official_common cache TTL logic at _official_common.py:972-1041

findings.title: alpha_vantage get_news/get_global_news/get_insider_transactions return raw dict/JSON into a string-rendering router
findings.whats_missing: alpha_vantage_news.get_news/get_global_news/get_insider_transactions and alpha_vantage_fundamentals.get_balance_sheet/get_cashflow/get_income_statement return either a dict (parsed JSON) or the raw API string from _make_api_request, not an analyst-rendered string. interface.VENDOR_METHODS registers get_alpha_vantage_news etc. alongside string-returning yfinance/marketaux adapters, and _merge_vendor_results does str(result) on a Python dict, dumping a repr like "{'feed': [...]}" into the merged analyst context. _is_empty_vendor_result also treats a non-empty dict as 'not empty', so a dict that only contains an AV error/Information note will be passed through as if it were valid evidence.
findings.end_goal: Every vendor implementation registered in VENDOR_METHODS returns the same analyst-string contract (or all go through a structured packet renderer like decision_vendor_adapters._render_packet), AV news/fundamentals are rendered to readable text, and error/Information payloads are classified as empty so the fallback chain advances instead of emitting a raw dict repr.
findings.evidence: alpha_vantage_news.py:24,53,72 (returns _make_api_request result directly); alpha_vantage_fundamentals.py:36,42,48,54; interface.py:277,284,287 + _merge_vendor_results str() at interface.py:401; _is_empty_vendor_result dict branch at interface.py:367-370

findings.title: Alpha Vantage news time_to truncates the end date to 00:00, excluding the final day's intraday news
findings.whats_missing: format_datetime_for_api converts a YYYY-mm-dd end_date to YYYYMMDDT0000 (midnight at the start of that day). For get_news the time_to is therefore the start of end_date, so any article published during end_date itself (00:01 onward) is excluded from the window. The yfinance news path deliberately adds +1 day to end_date for inclusivity (yfinance_news.py:89), so the two news providers have inconsistent window semantics.
findings.end_goal: AV news end-of-window maps to 23:59 of end_date (or end_date+1 at 00:00) so the requested final day is fully included, matching the inclusive window used by the yfinance and packet-based news adapters.
findings.evidence: alpha_vantage_common.py:27-28 (strftime '%Y%m%dT0000'); alpha_vantage_news.py:21; contrast yfinance_news.py:89 (end_dt + relativedelta(days=1))

findings.title: yf_retry can return None (implicit) when retries are exhausted without re-raising on the final loop iteration
findings.whats_missing: yf_retry loops range(max_retries+1); on a YFRateLimitError it only re-raises in the else branch (attempt == max_retries). The control flow is correct for rate-limit errors, but because the function has no return/raise after the loop, any future edit that changes the branch condition would let it fall through and return None. Callers like get_YFin_data_online do data.empty on the result and get_fundamentals does 'if not info' — a None would raise an opaque AttributeError rather than a clear data-unavailable message. There is no defensive final raise/return guarding the post-loop path.
findings.end_goal: yf_retry has an explicit terminal raise after the loop (or restructured try/except) so it can never implicitly return None, and callers receive a typed RateLimit/data-unavailable signal instead of an AttributeError downstream.
findings.evidence: stockstats_utils.py:18-34 (no return/raise after for-loop)

findings.title: Inconsistent freshness/source/confidence typing across providers; string-CSV paths carry no provenance at all
findings.whats_missing: The official providers (tiingo, eodhd, fmp, finnhub, massive, alpaca_market_data) return SourceEvidencePacket with quality, as_of, freshness, source_refs. The yfinance/alpha_vantage/stockstats string-returning paths (get_YFin_data_online, get_stockstats_indicator, AV stock/indicator) return bare CSV/text with only a '# Data retrieved on' header and no machine-readable as_of, source, quality, or staleness field. Quality strings are also hand-assigned inconsistently (tiingo='medium', massive='medium', yfinance options/short-interest='low', alpaca='high') with no shared rubric, so a downstream consumer cannot uniformly rank or down-weight evidence by source confidence.
findings.end_goal: A single shared confidence/freshness contract (source name, as_of timestamp, staleness flag, quality tier from one documented rubric) attached to every market/price/fundamental result regardless of whether the underlying provider is string-based or packet-based, enabling the router and agents to rank and discount sources consistently.
findings.evidence: y_finance.py:46-48 (header-only provenance) vs tiingo.py:57-68 / massive.py:68-79 (full packet); quality literals scattered: tiingo.py:64 'medium', alpaca_market_data.py:79 'high', yfinance_options.py:224 'low'

findings.title: record_connector_health writes connector-health.json to disk on every HTTP attempt (and every retry)
findings.whats_missing: record_connector_health(..., write=True) is the default and is called on every attempt inside _request_json/_request_text_response — including each transient retry and each cache hit — and each call does write_connector_health() which json.dumps the entire snapshot and rewrites results/_context/connector-health.json. During an overnight run with many symbols x many providers x retries this is thousands of full-file rewrites, adding latency and disk churn on the hot path, and is not concurrency-safe (no lock; analyst_concurrency could interleave writes).
findings.end_goal: Health stats accumulate in memory and are flushed to disk on a debounce/interval or at end-of-batch (write=False on the per-attempt hot path), with an atomic write (temp file + rename) to avoid torn JSON under concurrency.
findings.evidence: _official_common.py:189 (write default True), 213-214, 373-380, 432-438 (write=True per attempt), 160-172 (full-file rewrite)

findings.title: Alpha Vantage error responses become plain strings that may not be classified as empty/transient, breaking fallback
findings.whats_missing: _make_api_request only raises AlphaVantageRateLimitError when the JSON 'Information' field mentions 'rate limit' or 'api key'. Other AV error shapes ('Error Message', 'Note', empty {} from OVERVIEW for an unknown symbol, or premium-endpoint messages) are returned as a dict or raw string. get_indicator and get_stock then return strings like 'Error retrieving ... data' or 'Error: No data returned', which _is_empty_vendor_result catches only if they start with the exact hardcoded prefixes ('error ', 'error:', 'no data found', ...). Messages like 'Error: 'time' column not found' or an AV 'Note' string slip through as valid evidence and stop the fallback chain.
findings.end_goal: A single AV response classifier maps all known AV error shapes ('Error Message', 'Note', 'Information', empty payloads) to either AlphaVantageRateLimitError (transient) or a normalized empty/error result that _is_empty_vendor_result reliably detects, so the router degrades to the next vendor instead of surfacing an AV error string.
findings.evidence: alpha_vantage_common.py:78-84 (only Information/rate-limit detected); alpha_vantage_indicator.py:143,150,169,210; interface.py:354-366 (hardcoded failure_prefixes)

findings.title: _is_empty_vendor_result relies on brittle hardcoded English message prefixes
findings.whats_missing: Empty/failed-vendor detection is a hardcoded tuple of lowercase English prefixes. Any new adapter that phrases a no-data message differently ('No records', 'Symbol not found', 'Empty response', non-English when output_language changes) will be treated as valid evidence and short-circuit the fallback chain. There is no shared sentinel/exception contract for 'this vendor produced nothing usable'.
findings.end_goal: Vendor adapters signal no-data via a typed result (raise a NoVendorDataError or return a sentinel) rather than free-text the router must pattern-match, with the prefix list retained only as a backstop.
findings.evidence: interface.py:354-366 (failure_prefixes tuple)

findings.title: No unit tests for tiingo, eodhd, fmp, finnhub, alpha_vantage indicator/stock/news, yfinance_news, alpaca_market_data adapters
findings.whats_missing: test_official_dataflows.py imports many modules but the assigned price/fundamental adapters have thin or no direct behavioral tests: there is no test for alpha_vantage_indicator column-mapping/date-window logic, alpha_vantage_stock outputsize selection, fmp transcript extraction (fetch_fmp_latest_earning_call_transcript sort logic), eodhd symbol/.suffix handling, finnhub endpoint validation, tiingo daily-prices->CSV mapping, yfinance_news nested 'content' parsing and date filtering, or alpaca_market_data header/env resolution. Only stockstats load_ohlcv, options, and short-interest have focused tests. Regressions in column mapping or date filtering (high look-ahead risk) would pass CI silently.
findings.end_goal: Each provider adapter has table-driven unit tests with fixture payloads covering happy path, empty payload, error payload, NaN handling, and look-ahead/date-window edges, so provider parity and date-filter correctness are guarded.
findings.evidence: tests/ listing shows no test_alpha_vantage*, test_fmp*, test_finnhub*, test_tiingo*, test_eodhd*, test_yfinance_news*, test_alpaca_market_data*; test_official_dataflows.py:5-38 imports modules without per-adapter assertions

findings.title: Indicator NaN/early-window values surfaced as the literal string 'N/A' or raw stockstats NaN with no warm-up handling
findings.whats_missing: _get_stock_stats_bulk maps NaN indicator values to the string 'N/A', which is indistinguishable from 'N/A: Not a trading day'. For a 200-SMA on a short cache window the first 199 rows are NaN warm-up, but the rendered window may present 'N/A' as if it were a holiday gap rather than insufficient-history. StockstatsUtils.get_stock_stats returns the raw numpy value (possibly nan) with no NaN guard, so a single-date indicator lookup can return a bare 'nan' string into the agent prompt.
findings.end_goal: Distinct, explicit markers for (a) non-trading day, (b) indicator warm-up / insufficient history, and (c) genuine missing data, with all numpy NaN coerced to a clear sentinel before it reaches an agent prompt.
findings.evidence: y_finance.py:216-219 (NaN -> 'N/A'), 157-158 ('N/A: Not a trading day'); stockstats_utils.py:131-133 (returns raw value, no NaN check)

findings.title: Alpha Vantage stock outputsize heuristic can return too-short 'compact' data for multi-month windows
findings.whats_missing: get_stock chooses outputsize='compact' when (today - start_date).days < 100. 'compact' returns the latest 100 calendar-data-points (trading days), which is ~140 calendar days. If start_date is, e.g., 95 days ago but the requested window needs the full ~95 trading days, compact (latest 100 *trading* days ~5 calendar months) usually suffices, but the inverse edge — a start_date 99 days ago on a holiday-heavy stretch — risks the requested start being absent; and the threshold compares calendar days against a trading-day-count limit. No assertion verifies the returned data actually covers start_date.
findings.end_goal: outputsize chosen against trading-day count (or simply always 'full' for any window older than ~3 months) with a post-fetch check that the earliest returned date <= start_date, falling back to 'full' if coverage is short.
findings.evidence: alpha_vantage_stock.py:27-30

findings.title: _filter_csv_by_date_range returns its error message as if it were CSV data on parse failure
findings.whats_missing: On any exception (e.g., AV returned a JSON error rather than CSV, or a non-date first column), _filter_csv_by_date_range returns the string 'Error filtering Alpha Vantage CSV data by date range: ...'. get_stock returns that directly. _is_empty_vendor_result will catch it only because it starts with 'error ' lowercased — but the message starts with 'Error filtering' which lowercases to 'error filtering', matching the 'error ' prefix, so it is caught; however the dependency on that exact prefix is fragile and the function conflates 'no data' with 'parse failure'.
findings.end_goal: Date-range filtering raises a typed error (or returns empty) on parse failure rather than returning a human message in the data channel, so the router classifies it deterministically rather than via prefix luck.
findings.evidence: alpha_vantage_common.py:122-126; interface.py:354-366

findings.title: Global-news yfinance Search uses a broad try/except that masks per-query failures and a fragile dedupe-by-title
findings.whats_missing: get_global_news_yfinance wraps the entire multi-query loop in one try/except Exception; a failure on the first query aborts all remaining queries and returns 'Error fetching global news'. Dedupe is by exact title string, so near-duplicate headlines from different publishers are not merged, and articles with empty/None titles are dropped from dedupe but can still be appended (title '' check). The look-ahead guard only runs in the nested 'content' branch, not the flat branch.
findings.end_goal: Per-query try/except so one failing query does not lose the others, normalized dedupe (lowercased/trimmed/fuzzy), and a uniform look-ahead (pub_date <= curr_date) guard applied to both flat and nested article shapes.
findings.evidence: yfinance_news.py:137-200 (single outer try), 154-157 (title-exact dedupe), 184-188 (flat branch lacks look-ahead guard)

findings.title: FMP adapter pins the /stable base but mixes endpoint families that historically differ between /stable and /api/v3
findings.whats_missing: BASE_URL='https://financialmodelingprep.com/stable' and ALLOWED_ENDPOINT_PREFIXES lists both new-style ('quote-short','news/stock','earning-call-transcript') and statement endpoints. FMP's stable vs legacy v3 APIs have diverged in path shape and required params (e.g., transcript params, symbol vs path-style). There is no version pin/test asserting these routes resolve under /stable, so a silent FMP API migration would 404 every fundamentals/news/transcript call with only a generic OfficialDataError, and the earnings-transcript gap (a known weak area) would stay unresolved.
findings.end_goal: Documented FMP API version, a contract/smoke test (mocked) per FMP route confirming the path family and required params under the chosen base, and explicit handling/logging that distinguishes 'endpoint moved/forbidden by plan' from a transient failure.
findings.evidence: fmp.py:19-35 (base + prefixes), 205-213 (transcript params), repo note: earnings-transcript evidence gaps is a known weak area

findings.title: validate_official_path rejects any path containing '?' so callers must pass params separately, but date values are interpolated into the path unescaped
findings.whats_missing: fetch_massive_daily_prices interpolates start_date/end_date directly into the route string ('v2/aggs/ticker/{symbol}/range/1/day/{start_date}/{end_date}') which then passes through validate_official_path. The validator allows only [A-Za-z0-9_./-], so a malformed date with ':' or '+' (e.g., an ISO datetime) raises 'not a safe relative API path' rather than a clear 'invalid date' message; conversely there is no positive validation that start_date/end_date are real YYYY-MM-DD values before interpolation. Same pattern for grouped_daily {date}.
findings.end_goal: Date inputs validated against YYYY-MM-DD (and start<=end) before interpolation, with a clear date-format error, so callers get an actionable message and the path validator is a backstop rather than the primary date check.
findings.evidence: massive.py:131 (date interpolation), 153; _official_common.py:717-735 (validate_official_path char set)

findings.title: Stock-data fallback chain lacks finnhub/eodhd/tiingo-intraday parity; fundamentals/news have far deeper chains than prices
findings.whats_missing: get_stock_data chain is only yfinance,tiingo,massive,alpha_vantage (4), while get_fundamentals has 6 and get_news has 10. finnhub and eodhd both offer daily OHLCV but are not wired as get_stock_data fallbacks, and there is no intraday/minute-bar route at all. If yfinance is rate-limited and the keyed price providers are unconfigured, price coverage collapses faster than news/fundamentals coverage.
findings.end_goal: Price (get_stock_data) fallback breadth comparable to news/fundamentals, including finnhub/eodhd daily candles and at least one intraday provider, all returning the shared CSV/packet contract, so an overnight run does not lose price data when one vendor degrades.
findings.evidence: default_config.py:155 (4-vendor price chain) vs :160-161 (6/10-vendor chains); finnhub.py/eodhd.py have no OHLCV fetcher despite both supporting candles

findings.title: No dividend/split corporate-actions feed and no forward earnings-calendar data type
findings.whats_missing: The dataflow layer exposes OHLCV, indicators, fundamentals, news, sentiment, options, short-interest, and macro — but no dedicated corporate-actions (dividends, splits, special dividends) feed and no forward earnings/economic-event calendar. Without a calendar, the system cannot reliably avoid holding into an earnings print or position around a known catalyst, and adjusted-vs-unadjusted price discrepancies (see auto_adjust finding) cannot be reconciled against actual split dates.
findings.end_goal: First-class corporate-actions and earnings-calendar adapters (yfinance .dividends/.splits/.calendar, FMP/EODHD calendars) feeding the trader/risk layer so positions are catalyst-aware and price adjustments are auditable against real action dates.
findings.evidence: interface.py TOOLS_CATEGORIES (no corporate_actions or earnings_calendar category); y_finance.py has no dividends/splits accessor

findings.title: No analyst-estimates / estimate-revisions / price-target data type for event-underreaction theses
findings.whats_missing: The research pipeline values guidance/Q&A (transcripts) but has no structured analyst-estimate, estimate-revision (up/down trend), or consensus price-target feed, which FMP, finnhub (stock/recommendation, stock/price-target), and EODHD all provide. Estimate-revision momentum is one of the strongest documented post-event drift signals and would directly support the bull/bear debate.
findings.end_goal: An analyst-estimates/revisions adapter (finnhub recommendation+price-target, FMP analyst-estimates) returning the shared evidence contract, surfaced to the fundamentals analyst as a distinct, downrankable evidence type.
findings.evidence: fmp.py ALLOWED_ENDPOINT_PREFIXES has key-metrics/ratios but no analyst-estimates; finnhub.py prefixes lack 'stock/recommendation','stock/price-target','stock/earnings'

findings.title: alpaca_market_data only reads ALPACA_PAPER_* keys, with no live-data-key fallback and no SIP/feed selection
findings.whats_missing: fetch_alpaca_latest_trades hardcodes ALPACA_PAPER_API_KEY/SECRET via _headers. There is no fallback to a dedicated market-data key, and no 'feed' parameter (iex vs sip), so on a free/paper key the default IEX feed returns sparse trades and the function gives a misleadingly thin quote with no indication the feed is limited. The Windows-registry env read (_read_windows_user_env) is a useful Windows-only path but is undocumented and untested.
findings.end_goal: Market-data credentials resolved independently of paper trading keys, an explicit feed parameter with a documented default and a limitation note in the packet when IEX is used, and a test covering the env-resolution precedence including the Windows-registry branch.
findings.evidence: alpaca_market_data.py:51-53 (paper keys only), 18 (no feed param), 21-31 (untested winreg path)

findings.title: yfinance options and short-interest adapters tag as_of=now and never reconcile against a curr_date, so they can leak future data into backtests
findings.whats_missing: Both adapters set as_of = now_iso() and fetch live Yahoo data with no curr_date parameter, so when invoked in a historical/backtest context they surface present-day options chains and present-day short interest as if they were available on the simulated date — a look-ahead leak. The dateShortInterest field is captured but never compared to a simulation date, and there is no staleness flag if Yahoo's short-interest date is months old.
findings.end_goal: These supplemental adapters accept curr_date and either refuse (return a blocked/stale packet) when no point-in-time data is available or clearly flag the data as present-day-only and excluded from historical evaluation, with staleness computed from dateShortInterest vs the requested as_of.
findings.evidence: yfinance_options.py:110-115,179 (as_of=now, no curr_date); yfinance_short_interest.py:74,107,113 (as_of=now, dateShortInterest captured but unused for look-ahead)

findings.title: filter_financials_by_date assumes all statement columns are dates and silently drops columns that fail to parse
findings.whats_missing: filter_financials_by_date builds mask = pd.to_datetime(data.columns, errors='coerce') <= cutoff. Columns that are not parseable dates coerce to NaT, and NaT <= cutoff is False, so any non-date column (e.g., a 'TTM' column yfinance sometimes includes, or a label column) is dropped without warning. Conversely a real fiscal-period column with an unusual format could be coerced to NaT and lost, removing legitimate historical data.
findings.end_goal: Column filtering that explicitly identifies the date columns (and preserves known non-date columns like 'TTM' or labels per policy), logging when a column is dropped because it could not be parsed, so look-ahead filtering never silently discards valid data.
findings.evidence: stockstats_utils.py:98-109

findings.title: get_fundamentals reads deprecated yfinance 'pegRatio' key; several info fields silently None across yfinance versions
findings.whats_missing: y_finance.get_fundamentals reads info.get('pegRatio'), which recent yfinance renamed to 'trailingPegRatio'; the old key returns None and the line is dropped (fields with None are skipped at line 295), so PEG silently disappears with no warning. dividendYield units also changed (fraction vs percent) across yfinance versions and there is no normalization, so the reported dividend yield can be off by 100x depending on the installed version.
findings.end_goal: Field accessors that try both old/new yfinance key names, normalize known unit changes (dividendYield, margins), and emit an explicit 'not available' note when a core ratio is missing rather than silently omitting the line.
findings.evidence: y_finance.py:269 (pegRatio), 273 (dividendYield), 294-296 (None fields dropped silently)

findings.title: Technical-indicator description/parameter tables are duplicated verbatim between y_finance and alpha_vantage_indicator
findings.whats_missing: The best_ind_params dict in y_finance.py (lines 61-132) and indicator_descriptions in alpha_vantage_indicator.py (lines 47-60) are near-identical blocks of the same indicator prose, plus the supported-indicator sets differ (y_finance includes 'mfi'; AV omits 'mfi' and treats 'vwma' as unsupported). Drift between the two means an indicator supported on yfinance silently 404s when routed to alpha_vantage, with inconsistent descriptions.
findings.end_goal: A single canonical indicator registry (name -> description, params, which providers support it) imported by both the yfinance and alpha_vantage indicator paths, so supported-set and prose never drift and routing can skip a provider that cannot compute a requested indicator.
findings.evidence: y_finance.py:61-132 vs alpha_vantage_indicator.py:32-60; 'mfi' only in y_finance, 'vwma' unsupported in AV (alpha_vantage_indicator.py:133-136)

findings.title: Indicator bulk lookup uses string startswith date matching, fragile to time-suffixed or non-midnight dates
findings.whats_missing: get_stock_stats and _get_stock_stats_bulk convert Date to strftime('%Y-%m-%d') and match with str.startswith(curr_date_str). If the cache ever stores intraday timestamps or a localized date, startswith matching is brittle; and building a per-date dict then looping day-by-day with relativedelta(days=1) over the whole look_back window is O(window) Python-level work per indicator call rather than a vectorized pandas reindex.
findings.end_goal: Date matching on a proper datetime index (exact normalized-day comparison), and the window built via a single vectorized pandas slice/reindex rather than a day-by-day Python loop.
findings.evidence: stockstats_utils.py:125-129; y_finance.py:202-219 (dict build), 148-166 (day-by-day loop)

findings.title: Per-provider rate limiting is reactive (retry/circuit) only; no proactive token-bucket or shared budget across an overnight batch
findings.whats_missing: Rate limiting is entirely reactive: yf_retry backs off on 429, _request_json backs off + opens a circuit after N failures. There is no proactive throttle (token bucket / min-interval) per provider, so an overnight batch over many symbols can burst into yfinance/AV free-tier limits (AV free = 25 req/day, 5/min) before the circuit opens, wasting the daily budget on the first few symbols. AV's 25/day cap is not modeled at all, so the chain will exhaust it silently mid-run.
findings.end_goal: A per-provider proactive limiter (configurable requests/min and requests/day) shared across the batch, with AV's daily cap modeled so the router preemptively routes around a depleted free tier instead of burning the budget and then falling back.
findings.evidence: stockstats_utils.py:18-34 (reactive only); _official_common.py:363-382 (reactive backoff); no requests/min or requests/day config in default_config.py news/data section

findings.title: Optional providers hardcode quality and never set a staleness flag relative to requested window
findings.whats_missing: tiingo/eodhd/fmp/finnhub/massive all pass quality='medium' (or 'low') as a constant and rely on extract_payload_timestamp to set as_of, but never compute stale=True when the latest payload timestamp is older than the requested end_date/window. A request for fresh quotes that returns a multi-day-old bar is packaged with stale=False, so downstream freshness gating cannot tell a current quote from a stale one.
findings.end_goal: Each adapter computes staleness by comparing the extracted as_of against the requested window/now and sets the freshness.stale flag accordingly, so freshness gating is data-driven rather than always false.
findings.evidence: tiingo.py:57-68 (quality constant, no stale calc); eodhd.py:49-60; massive.py:68-79; finnhub.py:54-65; evidence_packet stale default at _official_common.py:831,835

findings.title: route_to_vendor redeclares fallback_errors after the merge branch (dead/shadowed local) and duplicates the fallback loop
findings.whats_missing: route_to_vendor defines fallback_errors and a full vendor loop inside the merge_policy branch (lines 427-455), then defines fallback_errors and an almost-identical loop again for the non-merge path (457-475). The two loops duplicate the empty/transient handling logic; a fix to one (e.g., adding a new transient type or logging) must be made twice and can drift. The first fallback_errors is unreachable once merge_policy is truthy and returns/raises, so the second declaration shadows it.
findings.end_goal: A single shared helper that iterates the vendor chain and yields (vendor, result) or accumulated errors, called by both the merge and first-success paths, eliminating the duplicated loop and the shadowed local.
findings.evidence: interface.py:425-475 (two near-duplicate loops, fallback_errors declared twice)

findings.title: No single source of truth documenting which env API keys each provider needs and which are required vs optional
findings.whats_missing: Required keys are scattered across modules: ALPHA_VANTAGE_API_KEY (ValueError, not OfficialDataError, so it is NOT in TRANSIENT_VENDOR_EXCEPTIONS and would abort the chain rather than fall back), TIINGO_API_KEY (required=True), FMP_API_KEY (required), FINNHUB_API_KEY (required), EODHD_API_TOKEN/KEY, MASSIVE_API_KEY/POLYGON_API_KEY, ALPACA_PAPER_*. There is no doc/table mapping provider->env var->required?->free-tier limits, and the AV missing-key path raises a bare ValueError that the router does not treat as transient, so a missing AV key crashes routing instead of skipping AV.
findings.end_goal: A documented provider/key matrix (env var, required vs optional, free-tier limits, how missing-key degrades) plus making missing-key errors a uniform typed exception that the router classifies as 'skip this vendor' so an unconfigured optional provider degrades gracefully.
findings.evidence: alpha_vantage_common.py:14-17 (raises ValueError); interface.py:210-216 (TRANSIENT_VENDOR_EXCEPTIONS excludes ValueError); env requirements spread across tiingo.py:31, fmp.py:39, finnhub.py:29, massive.py:35-39

findings.title: Missing ALPHA_VANTAGE_API_KEY raises ValueError which the router treats as a hard error, aborting the whole fallback chain
findings.whats_missing: get_api_key raises ValueError('ALPHA_VANTAGE_API_KEY environment variable is not set'). _make_api_request does not catch it, so it propagates out of get_alpha_vantage_* into route_to_vendor. TRANSIENT_VENDOR_EXCEPTIONS does not include ValueError, and the router explicitly preserves non-transient errors (test_route_to_vendor_preserves_non_transient_errors). Therefore, if alpha_vantage is anywhere in a fallback chain and the key is unset, the FIRST time AV is reached the entire route_to_vendor raises ValueError and the remaining vendors are never tried — a missing optional key breaks the whole method.
findings.end_goal: A missing/optional provider key is a typed, router-recognized 'vendor unavailable' condition that causes the chain to skip that vendor and continue, never aborting routing; required-key validation only hard-fails when that provider is the sole configured route.
findings.evidence: alpha_vantage_common.py:12-17; interface.py:210-216, 443,470 (only TRANSIENT_VENDOR_EXCEPTIONS are swallowed); test_dataflows_interface.py:131-146 confirms non-transient errors propagate

findings.title: Tiingo IEX (intraday) endpoint is allow-listed but has no adapter; dead allowance with no intraday wiring
findings.whats_missing: ALLOWED_ENDPOINT_PREFIXES includes 'iex' (Tiingo's IEX intraday/real-time quotes) but there is no fetch_tiingo_iex_* function and nothing in decision_vendor_adapters or interface routes to it. The allowance exists with no consumer, so the intraday capability is half-built — either a leftover or an unfinished feature.
findings.end_goal: Either remove the unused 'iex' allowance or finish the intraday adapter (fetch_tiingo_iex_quote / intraday bars) and wire it into a new intraday data category, so the allow-list reflects actual capability.
findings.evidence: tiingo.py:23-27 ('iex' allowed) vs tiingo.py:71-145 (only daily/metadata/news adapters); decision_vendor_adapters.py imports only fetch_tiingo_daily_prices, fetch_tiingo_news

findings.title: No cross-source price/quote reconciliation despite multiple OHLCV providers being available
findings.whats_missing: The router uses first-success for get_stock_data, so only one price source is consulted and there is no agreement check between yfinance/tiingo/massive/AV. A bad split-adjustment or a single-vendor data glitch (e.g., a 10x spike) flows straight into indicators and the trade thesis with no detection. Given the auto_adjust inconsistency above, the same symbol can yield different adjusted prices from different vendors with no flag.
findings.end_goal: An optional reconciliation mode for price/quote that samples 2+ providers and flags/quarantines a symbol-day when last-close or returns disagree beyond a tolerance, surfacing a data-quality warning into the analyst context and the connector-health snapshot.
findings.evidence: interface.py:457-475 (first-success only for non-mergeable get_stock_data); default_config.py:155 (4 price vendors available but only first is used)

findings.title: _official_common.py (1057 lines) bundles HTTP retry, circuit breaker, health, redaction, caching, and packet construction in one module
findings.whats_missing: A single 1057-line module owns six distinct concerns (timeouts/retry, circuit breaker state, connector-health metrics + disk IO, secret redaction/sanitization, evidence-cache read/write, and evidence-packet/blocked-packet construction). This couples unrelated subsystems (e.g., the cache layer calls record_connector_health which writes disk), makes the per-request-disk-write coupling hard to see, and complicates testing each concern in isolation.
findings.end_goal: Split into focused modules (http_client, circuit_breaker, connector_health, redaction, evidence_cache, evidence_packet) with explicit interfaces, so the disk-write coupling and concurrency concerns are isolated and unit-testable.
findings.evidence: _official_common.py spans 1057 lines covering retry (316-448), circuit (217-246), health+disk (105-214), redaction (81-89,701-714), cache (910-1057), packets (818-908)

findings.title: Circuit-breaker and connector-health state is process-local; lost between overnight job invocations
findings.whats_missing: _CONNECTOR_CIRCUITS and _CONNECTOR_HEALTH are module-level dicts, reset on every process start. An overnight pipeline that spawns separate processes (per symbol or per stage) starts each with a closed circuit and zero history, so a provider that was rate-limited/down in one process is hammered again from scratch in the next, and the written connector-health.json is the only cross-process signal (and it is never read back to seed the circuit). The cooldown (60s) is also far shorter than typical free-tier daily resets.
findings.end_goal: Circuit/health state seeded from the persisted connector-health.json (or a small state file) at startup so a tripped provider stays avoided across process boundaries within a run, with cooldowns configurable per provider to match real reset windows (e.g., AV daily).
findings.evidence: _official_common.py:66-67 (module-level dicts), 31 (60s cooldown constant), no read-back of connector-health.json into circuit state

findings.title: News merge dedupe is line-exact and global, can both fail to merge near-duplicates and drop legitimately repeated lines
findings.whats_missing: _dedupe_text_lines keys on lowercased/whitespace-collapsed full lines across all merged sources. A blank-but-meaningful structural line, or a common boilerplate line like 'Execution authority: none', is deduped after the first source, and two genuinely different articles that share a normalized title line get one silently dropped. Conversely two near-identical headlines with different punctuation are NOT deduped. There is no per-article semantic dedupe.
findings.end_goal: Article-level dedupe (by URL/normalized title) rather than global line-exact dedupe, preserving structural/boilerplate lines per section and merging near-duplicate headlines, so the merged context neither drops distinct evidence nor repeats the same story.
findings.evidence: interface.py:380-414 (line-level global dedupe in _dedupe_text_lines/_merge_vendor_results)

findings.title: fetch_fmp_latest_earning_call_transcript sorts candidates by raw string date plus (year,quarter) tuple, risking wrong 'latest' selection
findings.whats_missing: dated_candidates is a list of (sort_date_str, year, quarter) sorted reverse=True. sort_date is a raw string that may be empty ('') for some rows; an empty string sorts below any real date, but because the tuple's first element is the string and ties fall through to (year, quarter), a row with a present date but lower year could outrank a row with an empty date but higher year. The primary sort key should be (year, quarter), not the free-text date. This is the live path for the known earnings-transcript gap, so a wrong 'latest' quarter would feed stale guidance into the thesis.
findings.end_goal: Latest-transcript selection sorts primarily by (year, quarter) (and secondarily by a parsed date), never by a possibly-empty string first, so the most recent fiscal quarter is always chosen.
findings.evidence: fmp.py:266-277 (sort by (sort_date, year, quarter) with sort_date possibly '')

findings.title: News date filtering strips tzinfo and compares naive local-ish dates against UTC-published timestamps
findings.whats_missing: get_news_yfinance parses pub_date from ISO (UTC-aware), then does pub_date.replace(tzinfo=None) and compares against start_dt/end_dt parsed naively from YYYY-MM-DD. Dropping the tzinfo without converting to a target zone means an article published at 23:30 UTC on end_date could be off-by-a-day relative to a user expecting local-time boundaries, and the +1 day fudge (end_dt + 1 day) over-includes to compensate. There is no consistent timezone policy across the price (tz_localize(None)) and news paths.
findings.end_goal: A single documented timezone policy (e.g., all comparisons in UTC) applied to news publish-time filtering and price index normalization, converting (not just stripping) tzinfo, so date-window boundaries are exact and consistent across data types.
findings.evidence: yfinance_news.py:88-89 (replace(tzinfo=None) + +1 day fudge), 177; y_finance.py:33-34 (tz_localize(None))

findings.title: Earnings-transcript fallback tries fragile YouTube-scrape path before FMP, guaranteeing the known gap
findings.whats_missing: In config/research_provider_fallbacks.json the earnings_transcripts list orders youtube_transcript (cost_tier local_unlimited, priority 20) ahead of fmp (free_limited, priority 30). Cost-tier ordering ranks local_unlimited above free_limited, so the orchestrator always attempts YouTube first. The YouTube path (tradingagents/research/youtube_transcript.py) scrapes news.google-style YouTube search HTML with a regex for videoId then shells out to `docker mcp tools call youtube_transcript__get_transcript`, which is exactly the lane that times out. FMP (a clean JSON transcript API) only runs after YouTube fails, and FMP_API_KEY is not set, so every run collapses to the gap packet.
findings.end_goal: FMP (reliable structured transcript API) is the primary earnings_transcripts route when its key is present, with YouTube transcript demoted to a clearly-secondary best-effort fallback (or behind a feature flag), so a configured FMP key yields real transcript evidence and the YouTube timeout no longer dominates the path.
findings.evidence: config/research_provider_fallbacks.json:82-88; tradingagents/research/provider_fallbacks.py:_candidate_sort_key (cost tier rank before priority); tradingagents/research/youtube_transcript.py:69-155
findings.recommended_change: Reorder so fmp has lower/earlier effective rank than youtube_transcript for earnings_transcripts, or special-case earnings_transcripts to prefer keyed structured vendors first.

findings.title: FMP earnings-transcript endpoints exist but FMP_API_KEY path is the only real transcript source and is commented out by default
findings.whats_missing: fmp.py implements earning-call-transcript / -dates / -latest endpoints and fetch_fmp_latest_earning_call_transcript, and the orchestrator wires fmp for earnings_transcripts, but .env.example ships FMP_API_KEY commented out (line 95) and nothing tells the operator FMP is THE structured transcript provider. There is no runbook note that without FMP_API_KEY the only transcript route is the flaky YouTube scrape.
findings.end_goal: Operator-facing docs/.env.example clearly state FMP_API_KEY is the recommended earnings-transcript provider, with the free-tier transcript limits noted, so the transcript gap is closed by adding one documented key rather than relying on YouTube scraping.
findings.evidence: .env.example:95 (#FMP_API_KEY=); tradingagents/dataflows/fmp.py:192-283; tradingagents/research/provider_orchestrator.py:967-976

findings.title: YouTube transcript discovery relies on undocumented HTML regex with no rate limit, retry, or circuit breaker
findings.whats_missing: _discover_youtube_video_urls scrapes YouTube search HTML with a single regex `"videoId":"([A-Za-z0-9_-]{11})"` (youtube_transcript.py:147). It does not go through _official_common's get_text (no retry/backoff, no circuit breaker, no connector-health recording, no Retry-After). It is also one IP-blockable request per ticker with a hardcoded desktop UA, and the earnings-relevance check only scans the first 5000 chars. When YouTube changes markup or rate-limits, every ticker silently degrades to the gap packet with no connector-health signal.
findings.end_goal: Transcript discovery routes through the shared hardened HTTP layer (retry, circuit breaker, connector-health, sanitized errors) or is removed in favor of a real transcript vendor, so YouTube failures are observable in connector-health and don't quietly disable the whole earnings lane.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/research/youtube_transcript.py:123-155 (raw session.get, no record_connector_health), 171-173 (5000-char relevance cap)

findings.title: Nearly all news/macro adapter files are git-untracked (working-tree only)
findings.whats_missing: `git status --porcelain` shows _official_common.py, fmp.py, marketaux.py, newsapi.py, google_news.py, alpaca_news.py, scrapingbee.py, sec.py, bea.py, bls.py, eia.py, fred.py, treasury_fiscal.py, finnhub.py, eodhd.py, tiingo.py, massive.py, decision_vendor_adapters.py, integration_registry.py and the entire tradingagents/research/ directory as untracked (??). The core data-acquisition layer for this audit area exists only in the working tree and is not under version control; a single `git clean` or fresh checkout loses all of it. The two-commit history means none of this is recoverable.
findings.end_goal: All adapter and research-orchestration modules are committed on a real branch with meaningful history, so the news/macro/social dataflow layer is reproducible, reviewable, and not at risk of accidental loss.
findings.evidence: git status --porcelain tradingagents/dataflows/ tradingagents/research/ (?? on _official_common.py, fmp.py, sec.py, bea.py, bls.py, eia.py, fred.py, treasury_fiscal.py, newsapi.py, marketaux.py, scrapingbee.py, etc.)

findings.title: Registry marks MARKETAUX_API_KEY required while code accepts MARKETAUX_API_TOKEN, so health report lies
findings.whats_missing: marketaux.py _api_token() prefers MARKETAUX_API_TOKEN, then falls back to MARKETAUX_API_KEY (required=True). But integration_registry.py lists required_env_vars=[MARKETAUX_API_KEY] only. An operator who sets only MARKETAUX_API_TOKEN will work at runtime but the registry health report flags marketaux as skipped_missing_env (and lists MARKETAUX_API_KEY in missing_required_env_vars). The eodhd adapter has the mirror problem: code accepts EODHD_API_TOKEN or EODHD_API_KEY but .env.example only documents EODHD_API_TOKEN and the registry requires EODHD_API_TOKEN, so a key-only operator is misreported.
findings.end_goal: Registry required_env_vars semantics express 'any one of' for token/key alternatives (e.g. a required-group concept) so health status matches the adapter's actual resolution logic for marketaux and eodhd.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/dataflows/marketaux.py:25-30; tradingagents/dataflows/integration_registry.py:320-330 and 116-126; tradingagents/dataflows/eodhd.py:21-26

findings.title: Registry report shows only env presence; never reports live connector health/circuit state
findings.whats_missing: build_integration_registry_report only computes status from env-var presence (env_ready / skipped_missing_env / available_without_env / requires_runtime_check). It has no link to results/_context/connector-health.json (calls, errors, rate_limit_count, circuit_state) that _official_common maintains. A source with a valid key but an open circuit, repeated 429s, or 100% error rate still reports 'env_ready'. There is also no per-source freshness or last-success surfaced. The two systems are never joined.
findings.end_goal: Registry health report (or a combined health view) merges env-presence with live connector-health (circuit_state, recent error/rate-limit counts, last_success) so 'is this source actually working tonight' is answerable from one artifact.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/dataflows/integration_registry.py:580-665 (status from env only); _official_common.py:149-214 (separate connector-health file)

findings.title: No semantic cross-provider news/social dedup; only exact-line matching
findings.whats_missing: The only dedup is interface.py _dedupe_text_lines (exact normalized-line set match) for MERGEABLE_METHODS. The provider_orchestrator dedups nothing across providers (max_packets_per_need=1 just stops at the first source). When google_news, newsapi, marketaux, finnhub, fmp, alpaca_news, eodhd all surface the same wire story, there is no canonical-URL normalization, title near-dup detection, or article-id dedup. This wastes tokens and lets one syndicated story masquerade as multiple independent sources, inflating apparent corroboration.
findings.end_goal: A shared news-normalization step (canonical URL, normalized title, published-at clustering) dedups stories across providers and tags syndicated vs independent coverage, so the analyst sees distinct stories and corroboration counts are honest.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/dataflows/interface.py:380-389 (exact-line dedup); tradingagents/research/provider_orchestrator.py:1062-1121 (no cross-source merge)

findings.title: Several configured fallback routes (benzinga, firecrawl, docker_fetch, massive_options, social MCPs) have no orchestrator handler
findings.whats_missing: config lists benzinga (earnings_transcripts), firecrawl/docker_fetch (crawler_research), facebook/instagram/linkedin (social_sentiment), massive_options (options_iv_flow), social_watchlist (social_sentiment). _fetcher_for_candidate in provider_orchestrator.py has no branch for any of these, so they always become status 'unsupported_in_local_orchestrator' and are skipped. The config implies capability the code does not have; for earnings_transcripts this removes benzinga as a real backstop behind YouTube/FMP.
findings.end_goal: Either implement fetchers for the configured routes or remove the dead entries so the fallback config reflects what the orchestrator can actually execute, and unsupported-route counts go to zero for shipped needs.
findings.evidence: config/research_provider_fallbacks.json:78-100; tradingagents/research/provider_orchestrator.py:846-977 (no benzinga/firecrawl/docker_fetch/massive_options/social-mcp branches), 808-817 (_unsupported_attempt)

findings.title: macro_official fallback group is defined but no orchestrator path requests or fetches fred/bls/bea/eia/treasury per-run
findings.whats_missing: config defines a macro_official fallback list (fred, bls, bea, eia, treasury_fiscal, google_news_rss), and decision_vendor_adapters exposes get_fred/bls/bea/eia/treasury context, but DEFAULT_TICKER_EVIDENCE_NEEDS (provider_orchestrator.py:72-80) does not include macro_official and _fetcher_for_candidate has no fred/bls/bea/eia/treasury branch. So the orchestrator never pulls official macro context as a first-class evidence need; it is only reachable through the separate decision_vendor_adapters string API. Macro regime (rates, CPI, GDP, oil) is therefore not part of the standard per-run evidence bundle.
findings.end_goal: A macro/regime evidence need is fetched once per run through the same cached, health-tracked orchestrator path (fred/bls/bea/eia/treasury), so every overnight research run carries fresh official macro context with provenance, not just ad-hoc analyst calls.
findings.evidence: config/research_provider_fallbacks.json:57-65 (macro_official); tradingagents/research/provider_orchestrator.py:72-80 (needs list omits macro_official), 846-977 (no macro fetchers)

findings.title: record_connector_health rewrites the full health JSON on every single HTTP call
findings.whats_missing: record_connector_health(write=True) is the default and is called on every attempt, success, retry, and circuit event, and each call does write_connector_health() which json.dumps + writes results/_context/connector-health.json synchronously (lines 180-214). A run touching many providers x many tickers x retries does thousands of full-file rewrites, adding latency and disk churn and risking partial writes under concurrency.
findings.end_goal: Health is batched/flushed periodically or at end-of-run (or written atomically and throttled), so connector-health persistence is not O(requests) full-file rewrites.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/dataflows/_official_common.py:180-214 (write default True, write_connector_health per call), 160-172

findings.title: Reddit single 403 breaks the loop and abandons all remaining subreddits for the ticker
findings.whats_missing: In fetch_reddit_posts, a 403 on one subreddit returns None which triggers `break`, abandoning all later subreddits (reddit.py:158-165). Reddit 403s are often per-query/transient, not a global block, so one noisy subreddit kills coverage of stocks/investing. There is also no per-host rate-limit accounting beyond a fixed 0.4s sleep, and no record_connector_health on the 403 path (only logger.warning), so the block is invisible in health.
findings.end_goal: A 403 on one subreddit is recorded to connector-health and skips just that subreddit (continue), continuing to query the rest, so transient blocks don't zero out Reddit coverage and the block is observable.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/dataflows/reddit.py:62-67 (403 returns None), 154-165 (break on None), 64 (warning only, no health record on 403)

findings.title: StockTwits fetch has no rate-limit handling and no per-symbol pacing despite a strict public quota
