findings.whats_missing: StockTwits' public stream is ~200 req/hour/IP, but fetch_stocktwits_messages issues one un-paced request per symbol with no awareness of the limit; on 429 it relies only on _official_common backoff (max 3 attempts) and then returns a generic '<stocktwits unavailable>' placeholder. Across a watchlist this can burn the hourly budget early and silently lose social signal for later tickers with no surfaced rate-limit reason.
findings.end_goal: StockTwits requests are budgeted/paced against the documented public quota with rate-limit state surfaced in connector-health, so a watchlist run degrades predictably rather than randomly losing later tickers.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/dataflows/stocktwits.py:72-106 (single request, generic placeholder, no pacing)

findings.title: get_social_sentiment_context concatenates StockTwits and Reddit with no merged sentiment or dedup, double-counting noise
findings.whats_missing: get_social_sentiment_context just stacks the StockTwits and Reddit text blocks (decision_vendor_adapters.py:523-531). StockTwits already returns its own user-labeled bull/bear summary, Reddit returns raw posts; there is no unified sentiment score, no overlap handling, and no weighting by the source_quality 'low' trust. The analyst gets two unnormalized blobs and must reconcile sentiment itself.
findings.end_goal: Social sentiment is normalized into one scored, deduped, trust-weighted block (e.g. net bull/bear with volume and source attribution), so social signal is consistent and its low trust is reflected, not just pasted text.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/dataflows/decision_vendor_adapters.py:497-531

findings.title: Source-quality registry lacks profiles for stocktwits-style alt providers actually used (alphainsider, youtube_transcript, twitter present but alphainsider missing)
findings.whats_missing: SOURCE_TRUST_PROFILES has no entry for alphainsider (strategy marketplace, used in paper_tournament) or youtube_transcript or several gap sources; they fall through to the default 'unknown' / 24h profile. So evidence from these sources is silently rated unknown quality with a generic TTL rather than an intentional trust/role/ttl, weakening route ordering and freshness decisions for them.
findings.end_goal: Every source that can emit an evidence packet (alphainsider, youtube_transcript, and any gap/alt source) has an explicit SourceTrustProfile with deliberate base_quality, ttl, role, and allowed_effects, so quality scoring is never accidentally 'unknown'.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/research/source_quality.py:74-299 (no alphainsider/youtube_transcript entries); used in tradingagents/brokers/paper_tournament.py and research/alphainsider.py

findings.title: AlphaInsider adapter wraps get_json/post_json but re-implements its own non-hardened JSON shape checks and a fake response wrapper
findings.whats_missing: alphainsider.py builds a _JsonPayload shim to feed dict into _response_payload (a .json()-style wrapper), duplicating response handling that _official_common already does, and the Authorization header carries the raw JWT through get_json/post_json (header values are not redacted by safe_source_ref, which only sanitizes params/url). request_hash/safe ref are not used so there is no request fingerprint or evidence packet for AlphaInsider responses; results are bare lists/dicts outside the SourceEvidencePacket provenance model used by every other source in this area.
findings.end_goal: AlphaInsider returns SourceEvidencePacket-shaped evidence with provenance/fingerprint like other adapters, reuses the shared response/error handling, and confirms the JWT in the Authorization header is never echoed into logs or packets.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/research/alphainsider.py:44-114 (_JsonPayload shim, no evidence_packet/request_hash), 92-98 (raw JWT Authorization header)

findings.title: Only alpaca_news reads Windows HKCU Environment; other keyed sources won't see user-scoped Windows env vars
findings.whats_missing: alpaca_news.py has _read_windows_user_env (winreg HKCU\Environment) so it can find ALPACA keys set as Windows user env vars. The shared env_value() in _official_common.py (used by fmp/finnhub/eodhd/fred/bea/eia/newsapi/marketaux/scrapingbee) only calls os.getenv. On Windows (this is a win32 host), a key set via setx into HKCU but not present in the current process env is found for Alpaca but NOT for FMP/FRED/etc., producing inconsistent 'missing key' behavior across providers on the same machine.
findings.end_goal: Env resolution is consistent across all adapters (shared helper handles the Windows user-env fallback once), so a key set the same way is visible to every provider, eliminating provider-specific phantom 'missing key' failures.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/dataflows/alpaca_news.py:25-45 (_read_windows_user_env); tradingagents/dataflows/_official_common.py:656-663 (env_value os.getenv only)

findings.title: ScrapingBee sends Python-capitalized booleans (True/False) instead of lowercase, likely ignored by the API
findings.whats_missing: scrapingbee.py _bool_param returns str(bool(value)) => 'True'/'False' (capitalized), unlike marketaux/_bool_param which lowercases. ScrapingBee's render_js/block_ads params expect lowercase 'true'/'false'; 'True'/'False' is likely treated as falsy/invalid, so render_js and block_ads are silently not applied, degrading JS-rendered page fetches in the paid fallback.
findings.end_goal: Boolean query params are lowercase 'true'/'false' so render_js/block_ads behave as intended on the paid crawler fallback.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/dataflows/scrapingbee.py:60-61 (_bool_param returns capitalized) vs marketaux.py:40-41 (lowercased)

findings.title: fetch_fmp_latest_earning_call_transcript makes two billable FMP calls and ignores transcript-dates pagination
findings.whats_missing: fetch_fmp_latest_earning_call_transcript first calls earning-call-transcript-dates then earning-call-transcript (two API calls per ticker against a free-limited quota), and sorts dated_candidates by a string sort_date that may be empty, so 'latest' can be wrong when date fields are missing/non-ISO. On free tier this doubles consumption and can pick a stale quarter.
findings.end_goal: Latest-transcript selection uses (year, quarter) numeric ordering (not string date) and minimizes billable calls (e.g. prefer earning-call-transcript-latest endpoint when available), so it reliably returns the newest transcript at one call where possible.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/dataflows/fmp.py:253-283 (two calls, string sort_date), ALLOWED_ENDPOINT_PREFIXES includes earning-call-transcript-latest but it is unused

findings.title: NewsAPI from/to dates are not clamped to the free-tier 30-day window, causing avoidable 426 failures
findings.whats_missing: fetch_newsapi_everything passes from_date/to_date straight through (newsapi.py:85-88). NewsAPI's free Developer tier rejects 'from' dates older than ~30 days with HTTP 426. Callers requesting longer windows get a hard error (surfaced as a blocked packet) rather than an automatically clamped request, so legitimate recent news is lost on a fixable boundary.
findings.end_goal: NewsAPI requests clamp 'from' to the free-tier max window (configurable) so a too-wide window degrades to the allowed range instead of failing outright.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/dataflows/newsapi.py:64-97 (no window clamp)

findings.title: Integration registry omits youtube_transcript, twitter, crawlee, firecrawl and the composio social routes that the fallback config relies on
findings.whats_missing: DEFAULT_INTEGRATIONS lists composio, but not youtube_transcript (docker MCP), twitter (docker MCP), crawlee, firecrawl, docker_fetch, or the facebook/instagram/linkedin composio sub-routes that research_provider_fallbacks.json references. The registry is meant to describe 'what each integration is allowed to do', yet the active research routes for social_sentiment, crawler_research, and earnings_transcripts are partly invisible in it, so the no-secret capability inventory is incomplete.
findings.end_goal: Every route referenced by the provider fallback config has a corresponding registry entry (category, route, authorities, fallback_behavior, runtime_check_required), so the registry is a complete, authoritative capability map.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/dataflows/integration_registry.py:18-557 (no youtube_transcript/twitter/crawlee/firecrawl entries); config/research_provider_fallbacks.json:66-101 references them

findings.title: Macro adapters lack the as-of point-in-time filtering that decision_vendor_adapters applies only to equity sources
findings.whats_missing: _packet_filtered_as_of (decision_vendor_adapters.py) is applied to SEC/FMP/EODHD equity fundamentals to drop rows after curr_date, but get_fred/bls/bea/eia/treasury context build packets without running them through _packet_filtered_as_of. FRED/BLS/BEA series can be revised and contain observations dated up to today; in a backtest/walk-forward at curr_date this leaks post-as-of macro data into the analyst, a subtle lookahead bias that directly undermines the walk-forward calibration weak area.
findings.end_goal: All macro context fetchers enforce the same point-in-time as-of filtering (and ideally use vintage/realtime endpoints where the source supports them, e.g. FRED realtime_start/end), so walk-forward runs never see macro values that did not exist at curr_date.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/dataflows/decision_vendor_adapters.py:390-484 (macro getters skip _packet_filtered_as_of) vs 226-276 (equity getters use it)

findings.title: Untracked adapters have uneven test coverage; several news/macro fetchers lack dedicated tests
findings.whats_missing: Tests exist for official dataflows, decision_vendor_adapters, reddit, alphainsider, youtube_transcript, and the orchestrator, but there is no dedicated test asserting the earnings_transcripts fallback ORDER (the actual bug), no test that marketaux/eodhd token-vs-key registry status matches the adapter, no test for scrapingbee bool-param formatting, and no test that macro adapters apply as-of filtering. The highest-risk behaviors (route ordering, key-name parity, point-in-time) are unguarded.
findings.end_goal: Targeted tests pin the earnings-transcript route order (FMP before YouTube when keyed), token/key registry parity for marketaux/eodhd, scrapingbee lowercase booleans, and macro as-of filtering, so these regressions can't recur silently.
findings.evidence: tests present: test_official_dataflows.py, test_decision_vendor_adapters.py, test_reddit_dataflow.py, test_youtube_transcript_bridge.py, test_research_provider_orchestrator.py; none assert fallback ordering or token/key parity (config/research_provider_fallbacks.json:82-88)

findings.title: Add structured earnings-transcript provider(s) beyond FMP/YouTube (Quartr / API Ninjas / Tiingo fundamentals) to close the transcript gap durably
findings.whats_missing: The only structured transcript source is FMP; YouTube is a scrape. There is no second structured transcript vendor wired (benzinga is referenced but unimplemented). A single-provider dependency on FMP free tier (with strict transcript limits) is fragile for the stated 'deep, self-checking' goal.
findings.end_goal: At least one additional structured transcript/IR source (e.g. Quartr, API Ninjas earnings transcript, or company-IR crawler returning the transcript PDF/HTML) is wired as a real fallback so earnings_transcripts has redundant non-scrape coverage and the gap is genuinely closed.
findings.evidence: config/research_provider_fallbacks.json:82-88 (only fmp + youtube + unimplemented benzinga); tradingagents/dataflows/fmp.py:192-283

findings.title: Add high-signal macro/alt-data sources missing from the registry (ECB/IMF, NewYorkFed/Treasury yield curve, NOAA/EIA weather, USPTO, OpenFIGI, GDELT)
findings.whats_missing: Current macro is fred/bls/bea/eia/treasury_fiscal. Notably absent for a market-ready research system: NY Fed / Treasury par-yield curve (rates regime), FRED is keyed-only with no FOMC calendar source, ECB SDW / IMF for global macro, GDELT or RSS-based event detection for breaking macro/geopolitical events, USPTO/OpenAlex for innovation signals, OpenFIGI for symbology normalization, and a free congressional-trading / insider source (e.g. SEC Form 4 is in SEC but not surfaced as an evidence need). No commodities curve beyond EIA WTI.
findings.end_goal: A prioritized set of free/official macro and alt-data sources (yield curve, FOMC calendar, GDELT event stream, Form 4 insider, OpenFIGI symbology) is added as registry entries + adapters with source-quality profiles, broadening regime and event coverage for overnight research.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/dataflows/integration_registry.py:44-354 (macro set limited to fred/bls/bea/eia/treasury); config/research_provider_fallbacks.json:57-65 (macro_official list)

findings.title: Confirm api_token never reaches evidence packets: marketaux/eodhd put api_token in params used by request_hash and safe_source_ref
findings.whats_missing: marketaux/newsapi/eodhd/fmp/fred/bea/eia all inject the credential into the params dict that is then passed to safe_source_ref and request_hash. safe_source_ref and request_hash DO strip SECRET_PARAM_NAMES (api_token, apikey, apiKey lowercased, UserID? -> 'userid' is in the set, but BEA uses 'UserID' which lowercases to 'userid' = covered; FRED uses 'api_key' = covered). This appears safe, but EIA uses 'api_key' (covered) and BEA 'UserID'->'userid' (covered); however there is no test asserting the redaction holds for each provider's exact param name, so a future param rename (e.g. 'token' vs 'access_token') could leak into source_refs/fingerprints.
findings.end_goal: A parametrized test asserts that for every keyed adapter the resulting packet.source_refs and input_hashes contain no credential substring, locking redaction against future param-name drift.
findings.evidence: _official_common.py:34-52 (SECRET_PARAM_NAMES), 666-698 (safe_source_ref/request_hash strip by name); bea.py:26 (UserID), fred.py:30 (api_key), marketaux.py:65 (api_token)

findings.title: Google News RSS items keep google redirect links and unresolved publisher; no canonical-source extraction
findings.whats_missing: _parse_rss stores item link (a news.google.com redirect URL) and a 'source' field from <source>, but does not resolve to the canonical publisher URL or decode the Google redirect. Downstream dedup/credibility scoring can't see the true publisher domain, and the link is not directly fetchable evidence. The published date filter also drops items with unparseable pubDate (returns False) which can silently exclude valid recent items.
findings.end_goal: Google News items expose the resolved canonical publisher URL and domain (for dedup and credibility), and undated items are handled deliberately rather than always excluded.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/dataflows/google_news.py:85-114 (raw redirect link kept), 53-66 (undated items excluded)

findings.title: ScrapingBee maintains its own DEFAULT_ALLOWED_DOMAINS separate from crawler_policy, risking divergence
findings.whats_missing: scrapingbee.py hardcodes DEFAULT_ALLOWED_DOMAINS (18 domains) and also calls research.crawler_policy.domain_allowed against that local list. The crawler (crawlee) likely has its own allowlist; two allowlists for the same 'what may we fetch' policy can drift, so a domain approved for crawlee but absent here is silently blocked on the paid fallback (and vice versa).
findings.end_goal: A single shared crawl/research domain allowlist is the source of truth for both crawlee and scrapingbee, so the fetch policy can't diverge between primary and fallback crawlers.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/dataflows/scrapingbee.py:26-44 (local allowlist) + 77 (domain_allowed against it); research/crawler_policy.py (separate policy)

findings.title: BLS/EIA keyless behavior not surfaced; silent low-rate path can fail mid-run without operator signal
findings.whats_missing: bls.py resolves BLS_API_KEY with required=False and proceeds keyless (registry fallback_behavior 'continue_without_key_at_lower_rate') — but the keyless BLS tier is ~25 queries/day and there is no counter or warning when running keyless. eia.py requires EIA_API_KEY (required=True) so it hard-fails without a key even though registry lists fallback 'skip_source_and_use_fallbacks'. The keyless-vs-keyed behavior and its daily ceiling are not reported anywhere, so a run can quietly exhaust the BLS free tier.
findings.end_goal: Keyless BLS runs emit a clear 'running at reduced daily quota' signal in connector-health, and the EIA required-key behavior matches its registry fallback semantics, so operators know when a macro source is running degraded or hard-blocked.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/dataflows/bls.py:26-33 (keyless ok, no quota note); tradingagents/dataflows/eia.py:37 (required=True) vs integration_registry.py:91-102 (skip_source_and_use_fallbacks)

findings.title: alpaca_news hardcodes ALPACA_PAPER_* keys; a live-only credential setup loses Alpaca news
findings.whats_missing: _headers requires ALPACA_PAPER_API_KEY/SECRET specifically (alpaca_news.py:54-57). The news/market-data endpoint works with either paper or live data credentials, but if an operator only configured live keys, Alpaca news hard-fails with 'ALPACA_PAPER_API_KEY is missing' even though valid Alpaca data credentials exist.
findings.end_goal: Alpaca news resolves whichever Alpaca data credential is present (paper preferred, live as fallback) so the news source isn't lost on a live-only credential configuration.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/dataflows/alpaca_news.py:48-57 (paper keys only)

findings.title: autonomous_uncapped removes account dollar ceiling AND per-name cap with no default backstop
findings.whats_missing: In autonomous_uncapped mode _risk_cap_issues() returns empty immediately (live_gate.py:319-320) so per_name_cap_usd is never checked, and the account_max_capital_at_risk_usd check is explicitly skipped (live_gate.py:532 `live_budget_mode != autonomous_uncapped`). The only remaining account ceiling is account_hard_ceiling_usd, which is Optional/None by default (risk_envelope.py:25) and commented out in the example config (risk_envelope.example.yaml:25). Meanwhile cli/main.py _dynamic_live_cap_for_budget_mode sets the live cap to (current exposure + full broker buying_power) in uncapped mode (cli/main.py:443-452), and choose_autonomous_live_buy_notional can size a single buy up to 50% of that available notional (candidates.py:183-198). Net: in uncapped mode a single autonomous buy can be a large fraction of the entire account with only broker buying-power as the limit.
findings.end_goal: autonomous_uncapped should still enforce a mandatory, non-optional account-level dollar ceiling and a per-name ceiling (even if larger than the tiny-live tranche). account_hard_ceiling_usd (or an equivalent) should be REQUIRED whenever live_budget_mode=autonomous_uncapped, with load_risk_envelope failing closed if uncapped is selected without a hard ceiling. Per-name cap should apply in every mode.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/policy/live_gate.py:319-320,529-560; tradingagents/policy/risk_envelope.py:25; config/risk_envelope.example.yaml:21-25; cli/main.py:443-452; tradingagents/brokers/supervisor/candidates.py:169-198

findings.title: Order rate limit is default-inert and has a check/record time-of-use gap
findings.whats_missing: (1) The rate limit only enforces when BOTH max_live_orders_per_window and live_order_window_minutes are set (live_gate.py:564-568), and both are commented out by default (risk_envelope.example.yaml:28-30) — so out of the box there is NO submit-time rate cap, which is exactly gap (2). (2) Even when enabled, the gate evaluates the rolling count at decision time (validate_supervisor_live_submit_allowed) but record_live_order_submission only happens AFTER each successful submit in the loop, recorded with decision.generated_at rather than the real submit clock (cli/main.py:10526-10531). Two near-simultaneous runs both pass the gate before either records, so the window cap can be exceeded. (3) record_live_order_submission does a non-atomic read-modify-write of the JSON ledger with no lock (order_rate_limit.py:72-88); concurrent runs can lose records and undercount. (4) The single-writer execution lock is acquired AFTER the gate has already evaluated the rate limit, not before, so the lock does not protect the rate-limit check itself.
findings.end_goal: A live order rate limit should be ON by default with a sane window, enforced atomically under the single-writer lock so the count-check and the record happen as one critical section, using real submit time. Concurrent runs must not be able to jointly exceed the window cap.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/policy/order_rate_limit.py:72-109; tradingagents/policy/live_gate.py:562-578; cli/main.py:10489-10531; config/risk_envelope.example.yaml:27-30

findings.title: Buy-side live orders have no mandatory human/evidence review; only sells require loss_exit_review
findings.whats_missing: _final_submit_loss_gate_issues only fires for sell actions (live_gate.py:269-313 `if not _is_sell_action(action): continue`). Buys are gated only by promotion state booleans, risk caps, circuit breakers, and broker buying power — there is no equivalent mandatory evidence packet (thesis, freshness, anti-chase, source_packet_ids) required before a live BUY submits. This is gap (3). For an 'autonomous overnight' system the buy side is where new money risk is created.
findings.end_goal: Live buys should require their own mandatory pre-submit evidence packet (entry thesis, freshness window, anti-chase/anti-FOMO check, sizing justification, source packet ids), validated at final submit the same way loss_exit_review is for sells, and fail closed if missing/stale.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/policy/live_gate.py:260-313 (sell-only loop); tradingagents/brokers/supervisor/hourly.py:328-360 (autonomous buy action built with no review evidence)

findings.title: Dead-man and freeze are re-checked once before the submit loop, not before each submit_order call
findings.whats_missing: acquire_tiny_live_operational_guard re-validates live control (freeze + dead-man) once, but only when control_state_path is passed and only before the per-action loop (tiny_live.py:151-165). The actual submit loop then iterates and calls live_client.submit_order for each action with no per-iteration freeze/dead-man re-check (cli/main.py:10501-10531). If the dead-man expires or an operator freezes mid-batch (multi-order batch), later orders in the same batch still submit. This is gap (4): the re-check is at guard eval, not at each submit_order().
findings.end_goal: Immediately before each individual live submit_order() call, re-load live_control and re-confirm not-frozen and dead-man-fresh; abort the remaining batch the moment either trips. The check should be cheap and inside the loop.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/execution/tiny_live.py:151-165; cli/main.py:10501-10531

findings.title: Legacy execute_order_pairs mirror path bypasses the tiny-live operational guard and rate-limit ledger entirely
findings.whats_missing: The paper/live mirror command calls validate_supervisor_live_submit_allowed then execute_order_pairs(..., live_guard_approved=True) directly (cli/main.py:8590-8634). This path never calls acquire_tiny_live_operational_guard, so it gets NO single-writer lock, NO broker clock-skew guard, NO is_open/calendar session check, NO live-state reconciliation, and NO per-submit dead-man re-check. It also never calls record_live_order_submission, so any live legs it submits are invisible to the rate-limit window ledger. (Note: it passes execution_mode='live_now' which the unified gate rejects at live_gate.py:466, so today it is effectively always blocked — but the path still exists as a latent live-submit route whose guard coverage is far weaker than the supervisor path.)
findings.end_goal: Either delete the legacy execute_order_pairs live-mirror command, or route it through the identical tiny-live operational guard + rate-limit recording the supervisor path uses, so every live-submit route has identical safety coverage. No live-capable code path should exist that skips lock/clock/session/reconcile/dead-man/rate-limit.
findings.evidence: cli/main.py:8590-8634; tradingagents/brokers/alpaca.py:735-809 (execute_order_pairs has no lock/clock/reconcile); grep shows record_live_order_submission only at cli/main.py:10527

findings.title: live_guard_approved is a trusted boolean with no binding token tying gate result to submit
findings.whats_missing: execute_order_pairs takes live_guard_approved: bool and trusts it (alpaca.py:740,746). Callers hardcode live_guard_approved=True (cli/main.py:8633). There is no signed/structured approval object binding the specific order set, account, and time window that the gate actually evaluated to the submit call — nothing re-validates inside execute_order_pairs that the same orders were the ones approved. A future refactor that calls execute_order_pairs without first calling the gate would silently submit live. This is gap (6).
findings.end_goal: Replace the bare boolean with a structured, single-use approval token returned by the gate that encodes the exact order fingerprints, account, exposure ceiling, and an expiry; execute_order_pairs must re-validate the token against the orders it is about to submit and refuse if they differ or the token is expired.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/brokers/alpaca.py:735-757; cli/main.py:8629-8634

findings.title: Promotion and risk state are static JSON files never auto-downgraded when a downstream gate breaks
findings.whats_missing: _promotion_issues reads boolean flags (stage, live_enabled, ci_green, shadow_confirmed, benchmark/cost/recent_alpha/capacity gates) from a hand-written promotion_state.json (live_gate.py:97-131). build_promotion_state/write_promotion_state only write what evaluate_sleeve_promotion was handed; nothing recomputes or revokes live_enabled when walk-forward calibration degrades, when the agent-intelligence ledger shows 0 resolved forecasts, or when a CI run goes red. So a sleeve can stay tiny_live_eligible/live_enabled=true even after its edge evidence collapses. This is gap (7), and it is amplified by the known weak calibration (0.3143 directional accuracy, negative action-relative return).
findings.end_goal: Promotion state should be derived/recomputed from live calibration, CI status, and resolved-forecast evidence on every run, and auto-downgrade live_enabled to false (fail closed) the moment any upstream gate (calibration guard, CI, drawdown halt, resolved-forecast floor) breaks, with the downgrade reason recorded in the packet.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/policy/live_gate.py:97-131; tradingagents/policy/promotion.py:53-126 (no recompute/revoke trigger); known calibration 0.3143 / -1.66 per audit brief

findings.title: Mirror rollback only cancels paper when LIVE fails, not the reverse, and rollback is best-effort
findings.whats_missing: execute_order_pairs submits paper first, then live; if live fails it best-effort cancels the paper leg (_rollback_paper_leg, alpaca.py:701-732). But: (a) it cannot rollback a paper order that already FILLED (cancel only works on open orders) — a filled paper leg with no live leg is left as a silent imbalance flagged only in a text note; (b) there is no rollback in the other direction because paper is always first, but if paper SUCCEEDS and then the process crashes before live submit, there is no recovery record; (c) the rollback note is appended to report.failed text rather than producing a structured reconciliation action. This is gap (5) only partially closed.
findings.end_goal: Mirror submission should be transactional with structured outcomes: on any leg failure, emit a machine-readable imbalance/reconciliation record (not just a string), detect filled-vs-open and escalate filled-leg imbalances explicitly, and persist an idempotent recovery marker so a crash between legs is detected and reconciled on the next run.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/brokers/alpaca.py:701-809

findings.title: alpaca_supervisor.py plus the cli submit block are oversized and tangle policy/evidence/submit/render
findings.whats_missing: alpaca_supervisor.py is 724 lines mixing symbol extraction, NON_SYMBOL stopword lists, portfolio snapshotting, client_order_id minting, gate wiring, and ~50 re-exports. Worse, the single most safety-critical code — the live submit loop with gate calls, operational guard, rate-limit recording, idempotency-conflict reconciliation, and lock release — lives inline in cli/main.py spanning roughly lines 10363-10618 inside an already enormous CLI function. This makes the money-movement logic hard to unit test in isolation and easy to break. The audit brief explicitly calls for splitting into policy/evidence/packet/render/guard/CLI.
findings.end_goal: Extract the live submit orchestration into a dedicated, independently unit-testable module (e.g. brokers/supervisor/submit.py) with a single submit_live_actions(...) entrypoint, and split alpaca_supervisor.py into policy/evidence/packet/render/guard/CLI submodules. The CLI command should be a thin caller.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/brokers/alpaca_supervisor.py (724 lines, _NON_SYMBOL_WORDS 156-243); cli/main.py:10363-10618 (inline submit loop)

findings.title: Execution lock is released without owner verification in the submit finally block
findings.whats_missing: release_execution_lock supports an owner check (lock.py:62-73) but the cli submit path calls release_execution_lock(lock_path) with no owner (cli/main.py:10600-10601). If a stale-lock takeover occurred (acquire_execution_lock unlinks locks older than stale_after_seconds, lock.py:43-55), this process could unlink a lock now owned by a different writer. Also the stale-lock takeover uses st_mtime which on Windows/NFS can be unreliable, and recursion on takeover (lock.py:51) could loop if unlink races.
findings.end_goal: Always release with the acquiring owner id and verify ownership before unlinking; make stale-lock takeover record and log the displaced owner, and bound the recursive retry. Lock content (pid/owner/created_at) should be validated, not just mtime.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/execution/lock.py:25-73; cli/main.py:10484-10601

findings.title: client_order_id is sha1[:10] truncated to 48 chars; collision/idempotency risk
findings.whats_missing: supervisor_live_client_order_id builds an id from a sha1 digest truncated to 10 hex chars then truncates the whole string to 48 chars (alpaca_supervisor.py:499-508). _client_order_id and build_tiny_live_order_payload also slice to [:48] (alpaca.py:569,612). If two distinct actions in the same local day/sleeve/symbol/side hash-collide on the 10-char prefix, or if the 48-char truncation drops the distinguishing digest, two different intents could map to the same broker idempotency key — the duplicate-id path would then treat a genuinely different order as 'already exists'. The classify path keys off broker error text only.
findings.end_goal: Use a sufficiently long, collision-resistant client_order_id (full short digest within Alpaca's 128-char limit, not truncated below the digest), and assert uniqueness of generated ids within a batch before submit.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/brokers/alpaca_supervisor.py:499-508; tradingagents/brokers/alpaca.py:568-569,612-622

findings.title: Loss-exit review staleness window is a hardcoded 6h magic number with no config
findings.whats_missing: _loss_exit_review_issues hardcodes datetime.timedelta(hours=6) for review staleness (live_gate.py:255) and the same 6h appears in write_live_control_state default dead_man (live_control.py:72). These are unexplained magic numbers, not in the risk envelope, so the freshness/dead-man horizon cannot be tuned without code edits and the two 6h values are not obviously linked.
findings.end_goal: Promote the review freshness window and the dead-man default horizon to named, documented risk-envelope/config values with explicit defaults, and reference a single source of truth so they cannot silently diverge.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/policy/live_gate.py:255; tradingagents/policy/live_control.py:72

findings.title: Risk envelope uses a hand-rolled line YAML parser that silently mishandles nesting/lists
findings.whats_missing: _parse_simple_yaml splits each line on the first ':' and strips quotes (risk_envelope.py:51-61). It silently ignores any nested mapping, list, multi-line value, or anchor, and a duplicate key silently wins last. A misformatted but plausible-looking envelope (e.g. an indented block someone adds) could be parsed in a way that drops a cap field, and since only REQUIRED fields are validated, optional safety fields (account_hard_ceiling_usd, rate-limit fields) could be dropped with no error. For a file that controls live money limits, silent partial parsing is risky.
findings.end_goal: Parse the risk envelope with a real YAML parser (it already depends on yaml elsewhere), reject unknown/duplicate keys, and fail closed on any structural surprise rather than silently producing a partial envelope.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/policy/risk_envelope.py:51-61,98-161

findings.title: Submit loop breaks on the first broker error leaving a partially-submitted batch
findings.whats_missing: The per-action submit loop does `break` on the first exception (cli/main.py:10598). If action 1 of 3 submits successfully and action 2 raises, the loop stops and the run is marked blocked, but action 1's live order is already live and actions 3 is silently skipped. There is no explicit per-action accounting that a partial batch occurred beyond the submitted[] list, and no automatic cancel/reconcile of the already-submitted leg. Combined with no per-submit dead-man recheck, a mid-batch failure leaves indeterminate live state.
findings.end_goal: On a mid-batch submit failure, explicitly record which orders submitted vs skipped, surface a partial-batch reconciliation requirement, and decide deliberately whether to cancel the already-submitted legs — never leave a silent partial fill with the remainder skipped.

findings.title: Live reconciliation matches only position qty, not cost basis / side / avg entry
findings.whats_missing: reconcile_live_state compares only position quantity within a 1e-6 tolerance (reconcile.py:39-77). It does not compare cost basis, average entry price, or market value, and it cannot detect a position that has the right qty but a wildly different basis (e.g., from an unexpected fill price). It also treats expected-open-order presence purely by client_order_id set membership, so an order that exists but mutated (price/qty changed at broker) is 'matched'.
findings.end_goal: Reconciliation should compare qty AND cost basis/avg-entry within tolerance and verify each expected open order's key fields against the broker (using compare_alpaca_order_to_intent, which already exists), not just presence of the id, before allowing a new submit.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/execution/reconcile.py:39-77; compare helper exists at tradingagents/brokers/alpaca.py:237-285

findings.title: _is_live_order_action treats missing order_type/action as non-live, risking gate bypass
findings.whats_missing: _is_live_order_action returns False when order_type is in {'none',''} or action in {'hold','hold_cash',''} (live_gate.py:74-82). An action that is genuinely a live order but constructed with a missing/blank order_type (e.g. a future caller that forgets to set it) would be classified as not-a-live-action and the entire gate would early-return allowed=True (live_gate.py:404-406). The gate's safety therefore depends on every caller populating order_type correctly; a malformed live action silently skips ALL checks.
findings.end_goal: Fail closed: if account=='live' and the action is not an explicit hold, a missing/blank order_type should be treated as an INVALID live action that blocks (not as a non-live action that bypasses the gate).
findings.evidence: tradingagents/policy/live_gate.py:74-82,404-406

findings.title: Broker buying-power check ignores already-open live orders' reserved notional
findings.whats_missing: _broker_buying_power_issues compares projected_buy_notional against live_buying_power as reported (live_gate.py:368-386), and total_buy_notional only accumulates the CURRENT batch's buys (live_gate.py:463,512). It does not subtract notional already reserved by existing open (unfilled) live buy orders. Two sequential runs within the same window could each see full buying power and each pass, over-committing the account. current_live_exposure is passed for the account-max check but not folded into the broker buying-power check.
findings.end_goal: Buying-power validation should use buying power net of open-order reservations (broker non-marginable buying power or explicitly subtract open live buy notional), so concurrent/sequential runs cannot double-spend the same buying power.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/policy/live_gate.py:368-386,463-512

findings.title: Live control / rate-limit / promotion state files have no documented bootstrap and live_control absence blocks
findings.whats_missing: The gate reads results/policy/live_control.json, promotion_state.json, and live_order_rate_state.json by path (live_gate.py:393-395). load_live_control_state returns a blocking issue if the file is missing (live_control.py:36-37), which is correct fail-closed behavior, but there is no documented, tested bootstrap that creates a valid live_control.json with a fresh dead-man before an armed live run, and write_promotion_state requires a human to assemble SleevePromotionDecision objects by hand. The 'overnight autonomous' goal needs these files produced/refreshed automatically with evidence, or live is silently always-blocked (or, worse, armed by a stale hand-edited file).
findings.end_goal: Provide and test an automated bootstrap/refresh that writes live_control.json (fresh dead-man, not frozen) and a derived promotion_state.json each armed run, with the dead-man horizon and promotion evidence recomputed from current calibration — never relying on a hand-maintained JSON to authorize live money.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/policy/live_gate.py:389-395; tradingagents/policy/live_control.py:30-60; tradingagents/policy/promotion.py:107-126

findings.title: One-time Tuesday 2026-05-26 LiveExecutionPolicy and validators are stale/dead code in the live module
findings.whats_missing: LiveExecutionPolicy, TUESDAY_LIVE_RUN_ID='20260526-tuesday', validate_live_entry_allowed, and validate_live_management_action hardcode a specific past one-time live window (alpaca.py:46,89-106,418-477). Today's date is well past that window. These functions are not referenced by the current supervisor submit path (which uses the unified gate) yet they live in the core money-movement module and could be invoked by mistake or mislead a reader about how live entry is actually gated.
findings.end_goal: Remove the orphaned one-time Tuesday policy/validators (or move to an archived/tests-only location) so the live module contains only the active gating logic, and confirm no caller depends on them.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/brokers/alpaca.py:46,89-106,418-477; grep shows no submit-path callers

findings.title: Circuit-breaker daily-loss/drawdown derived only from equity-vs-last_equity, no intraday tracking
findings.whats_missing: _account_circuit_breaker_values computes daily_loss as max(0, last_equity - equity) and drawdown as that over last_equity (cli/main.py:462-482). This is a single point-in-time snapshot using broker last_equity; it does not track the intraday high-water mark, realized vs unrealized split, or losses already taken and recovered. A loss that breached daily_loss_halt_usd intraday but partially recovered by snapshot time would not trip the breaker, and the breaker only blocks buys (live_gate.py:344), not sells/holds. For an autonomous system this under-reports drawdown.
findings.end_goal: Track an intraday high-water mark and cumulative realized+unrealized daily loss persisted across hourly runs, and trip the daily-loss/drawdown halt on the worst intraday value, not just the latest snapshot delta.
findings.evidence: cli/main.py:462-482; tradingagents/policy/live_gate.py:337-365

findings.title: sizing helpers use builtin sum() over Decimals starting at int 0
findings.whats_missing: live_exposure_from_positions and total_unrealized_pl use Python builtin sum(...) over Decimal generators (sizing.py:18-26). sum() starts from int 0, so an empty sequence returns int 0 (not Decimal('0')), and mixing can yield subtle type inconsistencies downstream where Decimal is expected (e.g. comparisons/quantize). Type hints say the functions operate on Decimals but the start value is int.
findings.end_goal: Sum with an explicit Decimal('0') start (or use math.fsum-equivalent for Decimal) so these money helpers always return Decimal, including for empty inputs, and add a unit test for the empty-positions case.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/brokers/supervisor/sizing.py:18-26

findings.title: No test asserts autonomous_uncapped is still bounded by an account ceiling
findings.whats_missing: test_live_gate.py exercises rate limit and caps, but given the uncapped-mode early returns (live_gate.py:319,532) there is no test proving that an uncapped run with a huge notional is blocked by account_hard_ceiling_usd when configured, nor a test proving uncapped without a hard ceiling is rejected at config load. The most dangerous mode is the least covered.
findings.end_goal: Add tests: (a) uncapped + account_hard_ceiling_usd set => oversized buy blocked; (b) uncapped + no hard ceiling => either config load fails closed or gate blocks; (c) per-name ceiling still enforced in uncapped mode.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/policy/live_gate.py:316-334,529-560; tests/test_live_gate.py (no uncapped-ceiling assertion found)

findings.title: Rate-limit ledger records decision.generated_at, skewing the rolling window
findings.whats_missing: record_live_order_submission is called with now=decision.generated_at (cli/main.py:10530), which is the hourly decision build time, not the wall-clock instant the order actually hit the broker. The rolling-window count then measures spacing of decision timestamps, not real submissions, slightly distorting the rate window and making forensic timelines inaccurate.
findings.end_goal: Record the actual submit wall-clock time (datetime.now(UTC) at the moment of the successful submit_order), keeping decision.generated_at as separate metadata.
findings.evidence: cli/main.py:10526-10531; tradingagents/policy/order_rate_limit.py:72-88

findings.title: market_verification and reconciliation packet writers use non-atomic write_text
findings.whats_missing: write_market_verification_packet writes markdown/json with plain Path.write_text (market_verification.py:97-101), unlike the policy modules that use atomic_write_text. A crash mid-write leaves a truncated evidence packet. The reconciliation module is read-only (good) but the evidence packets it feeds are persisted via these non-atomic writers elsewhere.
findings.end_goal: Route all evidence/packet writes through the existing atomic_write_text helper so a crash never leaves a partially written audit packet.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/market_verification.py:97-101; tradingagents/policy/io.py:18-41 (atomic helper exists)

findings.title: alpaca_reconciliation is hardcoded to a single incident symbol (ORCL)
findings.whats_missing: The whole module is framed around DEFAULT_ORCL_SYMBOL='ORCL' and 'ORCL incident evidence' (alpaca_reconciliation.py:1,14,40-110). The core reconciliation logic is symbol-generic (it takes symbol=) but the naming, docstrings, and default bind it to one past incident, making it unclear it can/should reconcile any symbol and leaving incident-specific dead framing in a safety-adjacent module.
findings.end_goal: Generalize and rename to a symbol-agnostic post-submit reconciliation tool (symbol required, no ORCL default), so it is a reusable part of the standing reconcile-before-submit safety loop rather than a one-incident artifact.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/brokers/alpaca_reconciliation.py:1,14,40,66-72

findings.title: Money-movement hardening lives in a 108-file uncommitted WIP branch with 2-commit history
findings.whats_missing: All of the submit-path hardening (order_rate_limit module, account_hard_ceiling, tiny_live operational guard wiring) sits on branch wip/submit-path-hardening-2026-06-05 with 108 changed files / +25557 / -4016 vs main, 213 dirty entries (107 untracked), and only 2 commits total in history (git log). The safety-critical changes are unreviewed, unmerged, and at risk of loss; there is no atomic, reviewable commit boundary around the live-money guards.
findings.end_goal: Land the submit-path safety work as a series of small, reviewed, tested commits onto a tracked branch (not a giant WIP blob), with the live-gate/rate-limit/operational-guard changes isolated so they can be audited and reverted independently, and the working tree returned to clean.
findings.evidence: git status: 213 entries / 107 untracked; git diff --stat main: 108 files, +25557/-4016; git log: only 2 commits

findings.title: No documented one-command freeze/kill-switch wired to the dead-man control file
findings.whats_missing: write_live_control_state can set frozen=true (live_control.py:63-84) and the gate honors it, but there is no surfaced, documented operator command/runbook to instantly freeze live trading or shorten the dead-man, and the freeze is only re-checked once per submit batch (see deadman-not-rechecked-per-submit). For an autonomous overnight system, the human override path is the most important safety control and it is not first-class.
findings.end_goal: Provide a single documented kill-switch command that atomically writes frozen=true with reason and a near-immediate dead-man, verified by a test, and ensure every live submit path re-reads it immediately before each order.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/policy/live_control.py:46-84; cli/main.py:10474 (single control_state path wired, no kill command surfaced)

findings.title: select_research_model_route picks Mac/Windows Ollama without a health probe, so an unreachable default Mac URL is reported 'selected'
findings.whats_missing: In select_research_model_route (model_routing.py:637-654) the Windows and Mac routes are evaluated with select_windows_local_model_route(env=...) / select_mac_ollama_model_route(env=...) but WITHOUT passing endpoint_health. When endpoint_health is None those functions skip the reachability/tags checks and return status='selected' for any configured URL. select_mac_ollama_model_route also defaults the endpoint to DEFAULT_MAC_OLLAMA_URL (the Tailscale host known to be blocked by timeout), so this path will report the dead Mac lane as the selected research route and downstream callers may route real research work to a host that never responds. The parallel-routes path (select_parallel_research_model_routes) correctly threads route_health, but the single-route selector does not.
findings.end_goal: select_research_model_route should require/accept a route_health map and treat a local lane as 'selected' only after a reachability + required-model probe passes; with no health evidence it should fail closed to deterministic helpers rather than optimistically selecting a possibly-dead endpoint (especially the quarantined Mac default).
findings.evidence: tradingagents/research/model_routing.py:637-654 (no endpoint_health passed); :360-369 (Mac default endpoint = blocked Tailscale host); :448-469 (selected when endpoint_health is None)
findings.recommended_change: Thread endpoint_health into both local-route calls in select_research_model_route, or have the selector probe before selecting; never select the Mac default URL without a passing tags probe.

findings.title: YouTube earnings-transcript bridge has no gap/blocked-packet classification; it always raises on any failure
findings.whats_missing: fetch_youtube_earnings_transcript_packet (youtube_transcript.py:194-285) raises OfficialDataError for every non-success: no video candidates, MCP timeout, transcript too short, and 'did not look like an earnings call'. There is no structured gap classification distinguishing a transient failure (timeout/network) from a structural gap (no earnings video exists) from a content-quality rejection (found a video but it is not an earnings call). twitter_mcp.py returns a graceful _blocked_twitter_packet (quality='unknown', blocked=True, stale=True) on 401/403/429 so the orchestrator can record a downranked gap; youtube_transcript does not, so the orchestrator only sees a thrown error and the open item 'transcript gap classification' is unmet.
findings.end_goal: On unrecoverable-but-expected outcomes (no candidates / not-an-earnings-call / too-short) the bridge should emit a structured blocked/gap SourceEvidencePacket with a gap_category (e.g. transcript_not_found vs transcript_wrong_content vs transcript_transient_timeout), quality='unknown', blocked=True, and suggested fallback routes (FMP transcript, company IR), mirroring twitter_mcp and the RESEARCH_GAP_EVIDENCE_NEEDS pattern, so the calibration/source-quality layer can downrank rather than lose the signal.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/research/youtube_transcript.py:222-285; contrast tradingagents/research/twitter_mcp.py:98-149,175-182
findings.recommended_change: Add a _blocked_youtube_packet helper and classify failure modes; return it instead of raising for structural/content gaps, keep raising only for truly unexpected errors.

findings.title: MiroFish advisory valid_window/expires_after is surfaced but never compared to current date; expired advisory still reports final_handoff_available
findings.whats_missing: build_mirofish_handoff_status records advisory_valid_window and advisory_expires_after from staleness (mirofish_handoff.py:1185-1193) and _final_handoff_available (line 997-1006) only checks for DRAFT/NOT-FINAL markers and a report-id match. Nothing compares expires_after/valid_window against datetime.now, so once the MiroFish advisory window lapses the packet still reports status='final_handoff_available' and feeds attention symbols / forecast symbols / selection biases into morning research as if current. The report-33 highlight even hardcodes valid_window '2026-06-04 through roughly 2026-06-13' (line 611) and selection biases in Python, with no date guard.
findings.end_goal: The handoff status should parse expires_after/valid_window, compare to now, and downgrade an expired advisory to status='final_handoff_expired' (confidence='low', advisory symbols treated as priors-needing-revalidation rather than active attention), so a stale external simulation cannot silently influence overnight candidate attention.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/research/mirofish_handoff.py:945-948,997-1006,1185-1193,1164; hardcoded window/biases at :607-625
findings.recommended_change: Add a date-aware staleness evaluation (reuse source_quality._parse_timestamp) and an 'expired' status branch; flag the hardcoded report-33 valid_window for externalization.

findings.title: n8n evaluation run-probe POSTs to /run and /execute, which can actually trigger a workflow execution despite 'non-mutating' claim
findings.whats_missing: The module docstring and probe() comment say 'non-mutating evaluation-run probing', but DEFAULT_PROBE_ENDPOINTS (n8n_evaluation_run_probe.py:26-31) issues POST to /workflows/{id}/test-runs, /test-runs/new, /run, and /execute. If the local n8n build supports any of those endpoints, the probe does not just detect availability — it starts an actual evaluation/workflow run (a side effect), and a 2xx is then classified 'api_trigger_available'. There is no dry-run/HEAD/OPTIONS pre-check and the workflow could be a live automation wrapper. This is the only orchestration module that issues POSTs to discover capability.
findings.end_goal: Capability discovery should be genuinely non-mutating: probe with OPTIONS/HEAD or a documented dry-run flag, or only POST against a dedicated disposable probe workflow; the packet should state explicitly when a probe actually executed a run vs merely detected the endpoint, so 'editor_required' vs 'api_trigger_available' cannot be reached by accidentally running a real workflow.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/orchestration/n8n_evaluation_run_probe.py:1-7,26-31,91-118,191-201
findings.recommended_change: Use non-mutating verbs for detection or restrict POST probes to a throwaway eval workflow id; annotate each probe with executed_a_run: bool.

findings.title: 4 allowlisted n8n jobs have no friendly automation label in the evaluation dataset (JOB_AUTOMATION_LABELS drift)
findings.whats_missing: JOB_AUTOMATION_LABELS (n8n_evaluations.py:45-67) is missing 4 of the 24 allowlisted jobs: n8n_evaluation_dataset, overnight_calibration_guard, preopen_validation_preview, research_automation_orchestration_plan. For those the evaluation dataset falls back to name.replace('_',' '), so eval rows for the calibration guard, pre-open validation preview, and the research orchestration plan lack a meaningful 'automation' grouping. There is no test asserting label coverage == allowlist, so this drift is silent and will recur whenever a job is added.
findings.end_goal: Every allowlisted job has an explicit human-readable automation label, and a test asserts JOB_AUTOMATION_LABELS keys are a superset of the allowlist so the eval dashboard always groups every automation correctly.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/orchestration/n8n_evaluations.py:45-67 vs config/n8n_tradingagents_allowlist.json (24 jobs); verified diff shows the 4 missing keys
findings.recommended_change: Add the 4 labels and a coverage test load_n8n_allowlist().keys() <= JOB_AUTOMATION_LABELS.keys().

findings.title: n8n evaluation dataset defines actual_* result columns but nothing in-repo ever populates or scores them
findings.whats_missing: DATASET_COLUMNS includes actual_http_status, actual_status, actual_json, actual_quality_score, actual_checked_at, actual_error (n8n_evaluations.py:37-43) and every row writes them as '' (lines 232-238, 268-272). There is no repo-side runner that executes the metric_rule, fills actuals, or computes pass/fail against expected_* — that work is entirely deferred to the n8n editor UI (the known 'n8n native-eval still requires the editor UI' weakness). So the dataset is a static fixture with no automated acceptance/scoring path, and metric_rule strings (e.g. 'compact_output_only_true_and_stdout_bounded') are never machine-evaluated.
findings.end_goal: A deterministic, repo-side evaluator that runs each allowlisted observer job, fills actual_* columns, evaluates the named metric_rule, and emits a pass/fail acceptance packet — so n8n native evals can be proven from the repo without the editor UI, closing the editor_required gap.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/orchestration/n8n_evaluations.py:37-43,232-238,268-272; metric_rule strings at SCENARIOS :69-133 have no evaluator

findings.title: model_route_telemetry_packet can never emit status='failed', but summary/error logic branches on 'failed'
findings.whats_missing: model_route_telemetry_packet (model_telemetry.py:29-35) maps route.status to only success/fallback/blocked — there is no path that yields 'failed'. Yet _errors_from_packets (line 247) and summarize_model_telemetry treat {'blocked','failed'} specially, and the operator summary distinguishes failed lanes. Because a route that errors at call time (vs being pre-blocked by policy) is still recorded as 'blocked' or 'success', a genuine runtime model failure (timeout, 5xx) is not distinguishable from a policy block in telemetry, weakening the upgrade/downgrade recommendation signal.
findings.end_goal: Telemetry should record 'failed' for runtime/call errors (error_summary present with a non-policy cause) distinctly from 'blocked' (policy/route gating), so blocked_route_summaries and model_upgrade_recommendation reflect real reliability rather than conflating configuration gaps with failures.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/research/model_telemetry.py:29-35,244-258; orchestrator passes error_summary=route.reason for non-selected routes (automation_orchestrator.py:235-242)

findings.title: deep_research_protocol is a static methodology note with no citation/source-quality enforcement on captured reports
findings.whats_missing: deep_research_protocol.py builds a single hardcoded methodology packet (capture steps, UI routes) pointing at a fixed markdown artifact dated 2026-06-02 (lines 106,202). It lists 'required_before_influence' (explicit source list / missing-source note / deterministic test) as prose, but there is no code that parses a captured Deep Research report, counts citations, checks source domains/quality, or enforces the 'critical implementation report with sources and open risks' contract before the advisory is allowed to influence anything. So depth/citation rigor and source quality for the external Deep Research lane are aspirational text, not validated.
findings.end_goal: A deep-research ingestion path that parses a captured report, extracts its citation list, scores source quality (reuse source_quality SOURCE_TRUST_PROFILES), counts independent corroborating sources, and produces a gated 'influence-eligible vs needs-more-sources' verdict — so a sourceless or thin Deep Research report cannot reach a promotion/methodology gate.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/research/deep_research_protocol.py:103-204 (entirely static); captured_report_date hardcoded :202

findings.title: Self-heal safe-command allowlist couples on exact command strings, brittle and partially duplicated
findings.whats_missing: execute_self_heal_plan resolves a command to run only if the exact command-key string is present in ALLOWED_SELF_HEAL_VERIFY_COMMANDS (self_heal.py:1024-1027), and that allowlist (lines 170-263) re-spells every command as both a string and an argv list. The night-shift-patrol and automation-health-audit commands are written out as raw strings in two places (SAFE_AUTOFIX_ACTIONS execute_commands and the allowlist) with no shared constant, so a single edit to one spelling silently turns a safe-autofix into 'verify_not_allowed'. This is correct fail-closed behavior but fragile, untested for drift, and easy to break.
findings.end_goal: Command definitions should be single-sourced (one constant per command holding both the canonical string and its argv), with a test asserting every execute_commands/verify_command referenced by SAFE_AUTOFIX_ACTIONS and LABEL_SAFE_AUTOFIX_ACTIONS exists in ALLOWED_SELF_HEAL_VERIFY_COMMANDS, so the safe plane can never be accidentally disabled by a string typo.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/orchestration/self_heal.py:50-128,170-263,1024-1027

findings.title: execute_self_heal_plan mutates the plan packet in memory but is not shown writing the executed result back to disk/latest
findings.whats_missing: execute_self_heal_plan (self_heal.py:994-1079) returns an updated packet with executed_count/verified_count/verify_failed_count and per-signal verify_results, but unlike write_self_heal_plan/write_self_heal_handoff there is no write_self_heal_execution function in this module that persists the executed packet and updates a latest pointer + signature state with the post-execution status. The n8n self_heal_execute_safe job summary (n8n_runner.py:478-493) expects executed_count/verified_count fields, implying the CLI writes them somewhere, but the module itself does not close the loop, making the safe-executor's verified/failed outcomes harder to audit and to feed back into the dedupe/signature ledger.
findings.end_goal: A persisted execution record (json + latest + signature-state update to 'verified'/'verify_failed') so the self-heal loop's outcomes are durable, deduped across runs, and visible to automation-health-audit timeliness checks.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/orchestration/self_heal.py:994-1079 (no writer); cf. write_self_heal_plan :1177-1208 which does persist and update state

findings.title: Several orchestration/research modules have no dedicated tests (run-probe, n8n_api_sync, model_telemetry, knowledge_graph, provider_fallbacks, control_plane_patrol)
findings.whats_missing: There is no tests/test_*.py covering n8n_evaluation_run_probe (editor_required vs api_trigger_available classification, missing_workflow), n8n_api_sync (key resolution / redaction), model_telemetry (status mapping, blocked-route summaries, upgrade recommendation thresholds), knowledge_graph (sensitive-text rejection, query), provider_fallbacks (quality ordering, depleted/disabled handling), or control_plane_patrol. The run-probe is the module that decides whether native n8n evals are triggerable at all, yet it is untested; only test_n8n_evaluations.py incidentally imports it.
findings.end_goal: Each of these modules has a focused unit test (happy path + at least the key edge cases: missing workflow, blocked route, depleted source, sensitive-text rejection), wired into CI, so the control-plane classification and routing logic are regression-protected.
findings.evidence: tests/ listing shows no test_n8n_evaluation_run_probe / test_n8n_api_sync / test_model_telemetry / test_knowledge_graph / test_provider_fallbacks / test_control_plane_patrol

findings.title: YouTube earnings-call relevance check only scans title + first 5000 chars and matches on generic terms (false accept/reject risk)
findings.whats_missing: _looks_like_earnings_call (youtube_transcript.py:171-173) lowercases title + transcript[:5000] and returns True if any of generic terms ('quarter','q1'..'q4','earnings') appear. A non-earnings finance video that merely mentions 'Q1' or 'quarter' passes; a genuine earnings call whose relevant phrasing appears after char 5000 (long intros/ads) is rejected. There is also no ticker/company-name confirmation, so a transcript for a different company can be accepted as the requested symbol's earnings call.
findings.end_goal: Relevance scoring should require an earnings-specific phrase AND a ticker/company-name match, scan the full (bounded) transcript or a sampled window, and downrank rather than hard-accept/reject borderline cases, so transcript evidence is correctly attributed to the requested symbol.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/research/youtube_transcript.py:171-173,230-231

findings.title: YouTube video discovery scrapes results HTML with a regex for videoId, fragile and unauthenticated
findings.whats_missing: _discover_youtube_video_urls (youtube_transcript.py:123-155) GETs the public YouTube results page with a spoofed Mozilla User-Agent and regex-extracts '"videoId":"(...11)"'. This is brittle (YouTube markup/consent-wall changes break it silently, returning no candidates), order-dependent (takes first N matches with no recency/relevance ranking), and has no caching, so every transcript attempt re-scrapes. There is no fallback discovery route (e.g. official transcript vendor, FMP transcript already wired elsewhere) when scraping returns zero IDs.
findings.end_goal: Discovery should rank candidates by upload recency/relevance, cache results, degrade to a structured gap packet on scrape failure, and prefer/fall back to the deterministic FMP earnings-call-transcript route (already imported in provider_orchestrator) before HTML scraping.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/research/youtube_transcript.py:123-155; FMP transcript route exists at provider_orchestrator.py:975-976

findings.title: provider_orchestrator.py is a 1213-line monolith mixing fetchers, sanitization, caching, and bundle assembly
findings.whats_missing: provider_orchestrator.py (1213 lines) imports ~20 dataflow modules and inlines broker-snapshot sanitization (_ACCOUNT_SUMMARY_FIELDS etc.), per-source fetcher dispatch (_fetcher_for_candidate, ~130 lines of if/elif), cache key/TTL logic, gap-packet construction, and bundle summary assembly in one file. The giant _fetcher_for_candidate if-chain is the central routing table and is hard to extend/test in isolation; the same forbidden_effects list is re-literal-ed in 4+ places across this and sibling modules.
findings.end_goal: Split into a fetcher registry (source_name+evidence_need -> callable) that can be unit-tested independently, a separate broker-snapshot sanitizer module, and a shared FORBIDDEN_EFFECTS constant, reducing the file size and making it possible to add a provider without editing a 130-line branch.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/research/provider_orchestrator.py:846-977 (_fetcher_for_candidate), :237-455 (broker sanitizer), forbidden_effects duplicated at :448-454,500-510,553-559

findings.title: FORBIDDEN_EFFECTS lists are copy-pasted across at least 7 modules with subtle differences
findings.whats_missing: Near-identical FORBIDDEN_EFFECTS tuples/lists are independently defined in youtube_transcript.py:36-46, twitter_mcp.py:19-29, deep_research_protocol.py:14-20, source_quality.py:66-72, self_heal.py:25-33, control_plane_patrol.py:32-37, and inline in provider_orchestrator.py. They diverge: self_heal adds send_email/modify_automation_status, control_plane_patrol uses edit_repo_files/mutate_goals, the dataflow ones add post/comment/vote/message. There is no single canonical safety-effects vocabulary, so a new forbidden effect must be added in many places and gaps are easy.
findings.end_goal: A single shared module defining the canonical forbidden-effect vocabulary (with named subsets, e.g. SOCIAL_FORBIDDEN, ORDER_FORBIDDEN, CONTROL_PLANE_FORBIDDEN) imported everywhere, so the live-safety contract is defined once and consistently enforced.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/research/youtube_transcript.py:36-46; twitter_mcp.py:19-29; deep_research_protocol.py:14-20; source_quality.py:66-72; orchestration/self_heal.py:25-33; orchestration/control_plane_patrol.py:32-37

findings.title: n8n_runner._summarize_stdout is a 600-line per-job-name if-chain with no schema coupling to the allowlist
findings.whats_missing: _summarize_stdout (n8n_runner.py:70-652) hardcodes a per-job-name parser for ~25 jobs in one giant if-chain referencing dozens of payload keys. There is no registry mapping job_name -> summarizer and no test that every allowlisted job has (or intentionally lacks) a summarizer; jobs like pre_open_context_refresh and context_snapshot have no branch and silently return None. Adding/renaming a job requires editing this function and the JOB_AUTOMATION_LABELS map and the allowlist independently, with no cross-check.
findings.end_goal: A job_name -> summarizer registry (or per-job summarizer functions) with a coverage test asserting each allowlisted compact-output job has a summarizer, so n8n observers always receive a bounded parsed_summary and drift between allowlist/labels/summarizers is caught.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/orchestration/n8n_runner.py:70-652; no branch for context_snapshot/pre_open_context_refresh

findings.title: n8n runner HTTP server has no auth, no body-size limit, and reads Content-Length-bounded body without guard
findings.whats_missing: _N8NHandler.do_POST (n8n_runner.py:802-817) reads int(Content-Length) and rfile.read(length) with no maximum, no auth token, and binds the ThreadingHTTPServer on 127.0.0.1 only by convention (serve default host is 127.0.0.1 but main exposes --host so it can be bound to 0.0.0.0). Any local process can POST arbitrary job names; safety relies entirely on the allowlist. A malicious/huge Content-Length could allocate unbounded memory, and there is no per-client rate limiting on a server that shells out to subprocess jobs.
findings.end_goal: The runner endpoint should require a shared-secret header, cap Content-Length to a small bound, refuse non-loopback binds (or require an explicit opt-in flag), and rate-limit job execution, so even a local compromise cannot spam job execution or OOM the runner.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/orchestration/n8n_runner.py:802-817,820-844 (--host exposed, no auth, unbounded read)

findings.title: There is no explicit 'quarantined' route state for the timed-out Mac helper; it cycles blocked<->selected based only on env presence
findings.whats_missing: The Mac Ollama lane only has states selected/blocked driven by env + (optional) health probe. There is no persistent quarantine concept: a Mac that repeatedly times out is re-probed and re-attempted every run with the same network_unreachable self-heal actions, and select_research_model_route can still mark it 'selected' (see mac-fallback-no-health-probe). The open item 'Mac-helper quarantine-or-repair + fallback routing correctness' is therefore not modeled — nothing records consecutive-failure counts to back off, quarantine, and route deterministically to Windows/deterministic until a repair is confirmed.
findings.end_goal: A durable Mac-lane health/quarantine record (consecutive_failures, quarantined_until, last_repair_verified) so that after N timeouts the lane is quarantined (status='quarantined', not retried until a repair probe passes) and the orchestrator deterministically uses Windows/deterministic fallback — making fallback routing correct and stopping repeated dead-host attempts.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/research/model_routing.py:360-490 (only selected/blocked); model_telemetry.py:69-99 classifies mac_host_unreachable but no persistence/backoff

findings.title: research quality gate counts blocked/gap packets toward source breadth and can flip to high quality without a real local worker
findings.whats_missing: _quality_gates (automation_orchestrator.py:143-183) computes source_breadth_ok = context_summary is None OR len(packet_refs) >= 3. packet_refs come from context_summary['packet_refs'] which includes gap/blocked packets unless filtered upstream; high_quality is then true if deterministic+judgment ok and (local_ok OR source_breadth_ok) and no blocked packets. Critically, when context_summary is None (include_research_context=False), source_breadth_ok is forced True, so research_quality_high_enough can be True with zero local workers and zero real evidence. The blockers loop (lines 288-296) also suppresses windows/mac blockers whenever at_least_one_local_worker_ready, which can be satisfied by the optimistic Mac selection.
findings.end_goal: Quality gating should treat absence of research context as low breadth (not auto-pass), exclude gap/blocked packets from packet_refs before counting breadth, and not mark a run high-quality on local-worker availability that was never health-verified — so 'research_quality_high_enough' reflects genuine, validated evidence depth.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/research/automation_orchestrator.py:143-183 (source_breadth_ok default True when context None), :286-296 (blocker suppression)

findings.title: Knowledge-graph query matches by naive lowercased JSON substring, causing false-positive symbol/theme matches
findings.whats_missing: GraphMemoryStore._query (knowledge_graph.py:105-121) serializes each record to JSON, lowercases it, and matches if value.lower() in text. Querying symbol 'A' (or any short ticker like 'ON','ALL','IT') matches almost every record because the substring appears in unrelated fields/labels; querying 'F' matches anything containing the letter f. There is no field-scoped match despite the field param ('symbol'/'theme') being passed, so query_symbol_context returns spurious refs and the graph-memory context is unreliable.
findings.end_goal: Queries should match against the structured node label/type fields (exact symbol equality, whole-word theme match) rather than whole-record substring, so graph-memory recall is precise and short tickers do not match everything.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/research/knowledge_graph.py:105-121 (substring over json.dumps), field arg unused in match

findings.title: Deterministic helper route is marked can_use_connectors=True while every model route is False, an under-documented authority asymmetry
findings.whats_missing: select_deterministic_helper_route (model_routing.py:493-512) sets can_use_connectors=True, whereas all LLM routes set can_use_connectors=False. The intent (deterministic packet helpers may call read-only connectors/crawlers; LLMs only see sanitized packets) matches the toolful_research_boundary note, but nothing enforces or tests that a route with can_use_connectors=True is restricted to read-only connectors. The flag grants the broadest connector capability to the one lane that is not an LLM, and there is no can_submit_orders/connector-scope assertion in tests.
findings.end_goal: The connector capability should be explicitly scoped (read_only_connectors vs none), documented at the field, and covered by a test asserting can_use_connectors implies read-only and never can_submit_orders, so the helper lane's broader access cannot silently widen.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/research/model_routing.py:493-512 (can_use_connectors=True) vs all model routes can_use_connectors=False

findings.title: MiroFish advisory gate thresholds are hardcoded placeholders explicitly flagged as needing calibration, with no calibration hook
findings.whats_missing: mirofish_gates.py uses ELEVATED=0.60 and DOMINANT=0.50 as module-level defaults; the docstring (lines 37,26-28) says they 'MUST be calibrated against real telemetry' and the report mandates real-market validation before acting. There is no calibration input, no config override, and no link from required_validations() outputs (phantom_liquidity, order_flow_toxicity, macro_attribution) to any module that actually computes those validations — so the gates remain advisory placeholders whose triggering thresholds were never tuned.
findings.end_goal: Gate thresholds should be sourced from a calibration config/telemetry fit (not literals), and the required_validations tasks should map to concrete validators so a triggered gate's prerequisite checks can actually be run before any downstream use.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/research/mirofish_gates.py:37-49,196-203; calibration caveat in module docstring

findings.title: self-heal graph_failure/schema safe actions request execute but only have verify_command=None or non-executable recommendations
findings.whats_missing: SAFE_AUTOFIX_ACTIONS['graph_failure'] (self_heal.py:110-114) sets verify_command=None and a recommended_action 'rerun_analysis_with_fallback_route_only_after_manual_review' but is still classified 'safe_autofix' (not escalate) when not order-adjacent. In execute_self_heal_plan, a safe_autofix signal with no execute_commands falls back to command_keys=[verify_command] = [None], and ALLOWED_SELF_HEAL_VERIFY_COMMANDS.get(str(None)) is None, so it is marked 'verify_not_allowed' rather than producing a clear 'needs manual review' outcome. graph_failure thus silently lands in verify_not_allowed instead of an explicit escalation, muddying the safe-plane boundary signal.
findings.end_goal: Actions whose recommended_action is manual-review-only (verify_command None and no execute_commands) should be classified as escalate/observe-only rather than safe_autofix, so they never enter the executor's command loop and produce a precise 'manual review required' status instead of 'verify_not_allowed'.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/orchestration/self_heal.py:110-114,754-803,1014-1027

findings.title: n8n run-probe sends payload=None to test-run endpoints, likely guaranteeing editor_required even when the API supports runs
findings.whats_missing: DEFAULT_PROBE_ENDPOINTS (n8n_evaluation_run_probe.py:26-31) sends payload=None for all four POSTs. n8n test-run / evaluation endpoints typically require a body (e.g. dataset id or run options); a bodyless POST will likely 4xx, so api_trigger_available will read False and the probe will almost always report status='editor_required' even when an API trigger is in fact available with the right body. The probe therefore cannot reliably distinguish 'API genuinely unsupported' from 'API supported but we sent the wrong/empty body'.
findings.end_goal: The probe should send the documented minimal valid body for each endpoint variant (and distinguish 405/404 'unsupported' from 400 'bad body'), so 'editor_required' means the API truly cannot trigger a run rather than that the probe under-specified the request.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/orchestration/n8n_evaluation_run_probe.py:26-31,191-201 (payload=None), 'supported' = 2xx only at :117

findings.title: A local deep-research harness skill exists but the deep_research_protocol packet still routes operators to the manual ChatGPT browser UI
findings.whats_missing: The environment exposes a 'deep-research' skill (fan-out web search, adversarial verification, cited report synthesis), but deep_research_protocol.py describes only the manual ChatGPT Deep Research browser route (login, model dropdown, DOM scraping, screenshots). There is no automated, repo-driven deep-research lane that produces a cited, verified report packet the calibration/promotion gates could consume without an operator clicking through a browser — leaving the highest-judgment research lane fully manual and unintegrated.
findings.end_goal: An automated deep-research lane (driven by the available harness) that emits a cited, source-quality-scored ResearchIntelligencePacket honoring the same forbidden_effects/required_before_influence contract, so phase-gate due diligence and methodology destructive reviews can run overnight without manual browser capture.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/research/deep_research_protocol.py:23-60,138-148 (manual browser capture only); deep-research skill available in environment

findings.title: Provider orchestrator allows stale-on-error for most sources without surfacing the staleness age in route attempts
findings.whats_missing: build_ticker_provider_research_packets passes allow_stale_on_error=candidate not in NO_STALE_CACHE_SOURCES (provider_orchestrator.py:1112), so on a fetch error most sources silently serve a possibly-old cached packet. _packet_attempt (lines 980-999) records cache_state but not the cache age or whether the served packet was stale-on-error vs a fresh hit, so the bundle summary cannot tell an operator that, e.g., fundamentals came from a 5-day-old error-fallback cache. _cache_ttl_seconds also buckets all non-quote/news needs to 24h regardless of source TTL profiles in source_quality.
findings.end_goal: Route attempts and the bundle summary should record cache age and a stale_on_error flag per packet, and cache TTLs should derive from the per-source ttl_hours in SOURCE_TRUST_PROFILES rather than a coarse 5m/30m/24h bucket, so the depth/freshness of each evidence packet is visible to calibration.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/research/provider_orchestrator.py:838-843 (coarse TTL), :1099-1118 (stale-on-error), :980-999 (no age/stale flag); source_quality ttl_hours unused here

findings.title: Calibration guard and influence weights are never enforced by the live gate (observer-only)
findings.whats_missing: build_overnight_calibration_guard produces guard_decision/can_increase_live_influence and agent_influence_weights produces bounded weights, but tradingagents/policy/live_gate.py contains zero references to calibration, influence, or brier (grep confirmed no matches). The only consumers are n8n_runner.py compact-context surfacing and CLI echo.
