A weak cohort (guard=tighten) therefore cannot actually block or down-weight any live influence; it is purely advisory display text.
findings.end_goal: evaluate_go_live_guard (or the unified live gate) reads the latest overnight_calibration guard packet and treats guard_decision in {tighten, collect_more} as a HARD gate input: when the mature cohort is weak, new-buy / influence-increase effects are rejected with a gate_trace entry citing the guard, fail-closed if the guard packet is missing or stale. The guard becomes a real constraint, not a rendered string.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/evals/overnight_calibration.py:126-153 _live_influence_policy; live_gate.py grep for 'influence|calibration|brier' => No matches found; only consumer is tradingagents/orchestration/n8n_runner.py:553-573
findings.recommended_change: Wire the latest-compact guard packet into evaluate_go_live_guard as a hard precondition for any live-influence escalation, fail-closed on missing/stale.

findings.title: 4582 forecasts, 0 resolved: no historical/backfill resolution loop
findings.whats_missing: All 4582 ledger rows have resolve_after in the future (earliest 2026-06-09, today 2026-06-07; 3130 rows resolve 2026-06-12). resolve_forecasts skips any forecast whose resolve_after > now, so nothing resolves until the wall clock passes each horizon. There is no command that resolves forecasts against actual historical price windows for forecasts whose created_at is already old enough — they only become eligible by waiting. Consequently rating_calibration.json shows resolved_count=0 and every state=insufficient_history, and influence weights are all 1.00.
findings.end_goal: A resolution loop that, on each run, resolves every forecast whose created_at + horizon has already elapsed (not just future-dated ones relative to append time) against real price history, so the ledger accumulates resolved outcomes, earned influence (Brier/accuracy/relative-return) is non-trivial, and rating shrinkage actually moves off the prior. Target: hundreds of resolved forecasts feeding non-default weights.
findings.evidence: results/agent_intelligence/ledger.jsonl wc=4582; grep -c '"resolved": true' => 0; resolve_after distribution all >= 2026-06-09; resolve_forecasts gate at agent_intelligence_ledger.py:797-799; rating_calibration.json resolved_count=0 throughout

findings.title: min_samples mismatch lets sparse calibration become live override eligible inconsistently
findings.whats_missing: _safe_calibrated_probability (agent_intelligence_ledger.py:173-189) gates overrides on resolved_count >= MIN_CALIBRATED_RATING_SAMPLES (=3) and state == 'calibrated_with_shrinkage'. But calibrate_rating_probabilities (replay_ablation.py:142-251) sets state='calibrated_with_shrinkage' at min_resolved=1, and the CLI decision-quality command also defaults min_resolved=1. So a rating with 1-2 resolved samples is marked calibrated_with_shrinkage in the packet, yet the loader rejects it via the 3-sample floor — two different sample floors (1 vs 3) coexist with no single source of truth, making behavior surprising and the 'safe' path silently dependent on which entrypoint wrote the packet.
findings.end_goal: A single shared minimum-resolved constant used by both the calibrator that sets the state and the loader that consumes it, so 'calibrated_with_shrinkage' implies it already meets the override sample floor; no possibility of a packet labelled calibrated but rejected by the consumer (or vice versa).
findings.evidence: agent_intelligence_ledger.py:50 MIN_CALIBRATED_RATING_SAMPLES=3 and :180; replay_ablation.py:147 default min_resolved=1 and :189 state assignment

findings.title: Walk-forward scoring ignores transaction costs, slippage, and fees
findings.whats_missing: build_walk_forward_replay_packet computes directional_accuracy, false_positive_rate, average_brier, relative_return, and action_relative_return purely from raw price deltas (replay_ablation.py:841-893). No commission, spread, slippage, or borrow cost is subtracted. The plan packet lists 'token_or_api_cost_per_useful_signal' and a 'same_cost_model_per_arm' control as required (replay_ablation.py:746-758) but no cost model is ever applied to the scored rows. A strategy that looks edge-positive gross can be negative net, so action_relative_return as a live-influence input is optimistic.
findings.end_goal: A configurable cost model (per-share/per-trade commission, half-spread slippage, optional borrow) subtracted in the action_relative_return and net-edge computation, with gross and net metrics both reported, so the guard's MIN_ACTION_RELATIVE_RETURN threshold is evaluated on after-cost returns.
findings.evidence: replay_ablation.py:294-302 _relative_action_return (no cost term); :878-893 metrics dict; required-but-unused cost strings at :749-758

findings.title: No statistical significance / confidence intervals on any calibration metric
findings.whats_missing: Directional accuracy 0.3143 and action-relative-return -1.66 are reported as point estimates with a binary sample_floor_met flag and a fixed minimum_decisions_per_arm (default 10). There is no confidence interval (Wilson/bootstrap), no standard error, no benchmark-vs-arm significance test, and no correction for the fact that overlapping 5-day windows across many symbols on the same dates are not independent. grep for wilson|bootstrap|p_value|confidence_interval|standard_error in evals => none. A guard could flip on noise.
findings.end_goal: Each arm metric carries a confidence interval and the arm-vs-baseline comparison carries a significance statistic (e.g. bootstrap over decisions or a paired test), with effective sample size discounting overlapping windows; the guard's decision uses lower-confidence-bound rather than raw point estimate so it does not tighten/loosen on statistical noise.
findings.evidence: replay_ablation.py:884-890 raw _rate point estimates; overnight_calibration.py:20-22 fixed thresholds; no significance helpers anywhere in tradingagents/evals/**

findings.title: Overlapping return windows treated as independent samples (look-ahead/double-count inflation)
findings.whats_missing: The fixture dedupes only on (symbol, as_of) (replay_ablation.py:556-570). Multiple symbols decided on the same date over the same 5-day forward window are highly correlated (driven by the same market move) yet each counts as an independent scored decision toward sample_floor_met and toward accuracy/Brier. There is no clustering by date, no block bootstrap, and no per-date single-vote reduction. This both inflates apparent sample size and biases the false-positive/accuracy rates in trending/choppy regimes.
findings.end_goal: Sample sufficiency and metric variance account for date-clustering of overlapping forward windows (cluster-robust counting or block resampling), so 30 same-day decisions are not treated as 30 independent observations.
findings.evidence: replay_ablation.py:556-570 dedupe on (symbol, final_as_of) only; :890 sample_floor_met = scored_count >= minimum_decisions_per_arm

findings.title: No per-regime / per-sector / per-setup stratified calibration scoring
findings.whats_missing: AgentForecast carries setup, regime, and ticker/sector intent (module docstring promises 'by setup, regime, symbol, sector, and evidence type'), but summarize_agent_scores buckets only by agent (agent_intelligence_ledger.py:856-924) and walk_forward metrics bucket only by arm. regime is almost always 'unknown' (CLI default), and there is no sector mapping at all. So you cannot tell whether an agent is good in risk_on but harmful in risk_off, which is exactly the cohort handling the calibration end-goal needs.
findings.end_goal: Scoring functions that produce per-(agent x regime), per-setup, and per-sector breakdowns with their own sample floors, surfaced in the summary and consumable by influence weighting, so influence can be earned conditionally (e.g. trust news_analyst only in event-driven regimes).
findings.evidence: agent_intelligence_ledger.py:3-5 docstring claims regime/sector/evidence scoring; summarize_agent_scores buckets by forecast.agent only at :859-895; regime default 'unknown' in cli/main.py:1489

findings.title: Analyst stance and probability derived from naive keyword counting
findings.whats_missing: _stance_from_text (agent_intelligence_ledger.py:244-252) counts ~7 hardcoded bullish vs bearish words and maps the count to a probability capped 0.52-0.68. Negation ('not bullish', 'no breakout'), sarcasm, and mixed theses are ignored; a report that says 'downside risk if momentum weakens' scores bearish on 'downside'/'weak momentum' regardless of conclusion. Probabilities are essentially fabricated (0.52 + 0.03*count) with no grounding, then fed into Brier scoring as if calibrated. This poisons the very calibration the ledger is supposed to measure.
findings.end_goal: Analyst direction/probability extracted from a structured rating or an explicit model-emitted probability field rather than keyword counts, or at minimum negation-aware sentiment, so the scored probability reflects the agent's actual stated conviction and Brier/calibration is meaningful.
findings.evidence: agent_intelligence_ledger.py:51-68 BULLISH/BEARISH_WORDS; :244-252 _stance_from_text; :553 used for all four analyst reports

findings.title: Resolution entry price uses first close in window, embedding intra-window look-ahead/timing assumption
findings.whats_missing: _ledger_price_lookup (cli/main.py:860-868) returns history.Close.iloc[0] as start and iloc[-1] as end for [created_date, resolve_after]. The forecast is generated overnight (created_at 08:12 UTC in sample), but the 'entry' is the close of the creation day — which already contains that full trading day's move the overnight analysis could not have acted on, and the 'exit' is the close of resolve_after. This is an inconsistent as-of: returns are measured from a price the strategy could not have transacted at. There is also no guarantee iloc[0] is the creation date (yfinance may start later).
findings.end_goal: Resolution measures returns over an explicit, executable window (e.g. next session open after the decision to the horizon close) consistent with how a live entry would actually fill, with the as-of price pinned to the decision time rather than the post-move same-day close.
findings.evidence: cli/main.py:860-868 iloc[0]/iloc[-1]; agent_intelligence_ledger.py:800-822 start_date=created_at.date, end_date=resolve_after.date

findings.title: Ledger horizon counts trading days but walk-forward horizon counts calendar days
findings.whats_missing: agent_intelligence_ledger._add_trading_days advances horizon_days skipping weekends (resolve_after = N trading days, ledger.py:128-135), but build_walk_forward_return_rows_from_overnight_packets sets end_date = as_of + timedelta(days=horizon) calendar days (replay_ablation.py:407-409). The same nominal horizon_days=5 therefore measures different windows in the two scoring paths (5 trading vs 5 calendar days), so the ledger's resolved outcomes and the walk-forward cohort's outcomes are not comparable, and neither path adjusts the calendar end to the next valid trading day.
findings.end_goal: A single shared horizon convention (trading-day or explicit session-aligned end date) used by both the ledger resolution and the walk-forward harness, so the two scoring systems measure the same window for the same forecast.
findings.evidence: agent_intelligence_ledger.py:128-135 _add_trading_days; replay_ablation.py:407-409 datetime.timedelta(days=horizon)

findings.title: summarize_agent_scores neutral_forecast_count branch is unreachable for resolved forecasts
findings.whats_missing: resolve_forecasts always sets outcome to a concrete bool (_outcome_for_direction returns bool, ledger.py:824). In summarize_agent_scores the branch elif forecast.outcome is False ... else (neutral, outcome None) at :883-888 can only fire for unresolved forecasts, but those are already caught by 'if not forecast.resolved' above. So neutral_forecast_count is permanently 0 and the 'neutral' outcome label is dead. A correctly-predicted neutral (small move) is counted as a 'win' indistinguishably from a directional hit, muddying accuracy.
findings.end_goal: Neutral-direction outcomes are tracked as a first-class category (correct-neutral vs missed-neutral) distinct from directional wins, and dead branches are removed; accuracy distinguishes directional skill from neutral-band luck.
findings.evidence: agent_intelligence_ledger.py:824 outcome always bool; :883-888 dead neutral branch; :892 if forecast.outcome counts neutral-true as win

findings.title: Influence-weight formula uses unjustified magic coefficients
findings.whats_missing: agent_influence_weights builds raw_weight = 1.00 + (accuracy-0.50)*0.80 + average_delta*1.00 + (0.25-average_brier)*0.80 then clamps to [0.50,1.50] (ledger.py:962-968). The coefficients 0.80/1.00/0.80, the 0.25 Brier reference, and the clamp bounds are undocumented magic numbers with no derivation, no unit consistency check (accuracy delta, score delta, and brier delta are summed in different units), and no test that the mapping is monotone/sane. min_resolved=3 is also a very low floor to start moving a live-influencing weight.
findings.end_goal: A documented, dimensionally-consistent influence mapping (e.g. driven purely by calibration-adjusted relative return with an explicit shrinkage toward 1.0 by sample size), with the coefficients justified in a docstring and covered by tests asserting monotonicity and the sample-shrinkage behavior, and a higher resolved floor before weights diverge from 1.0.
findings.evidence: agent_intelligence_ledger.py:933-968 magic coefficients and DEFAULT floors at :27-28; min_resolved default 3 at :934

findings.title: Benchmark-relative scoring hardcoded to SPY with no factor/sector benchmark
findings.whats_missing: All relative-return scoring is ticker vs a single benchmark (DEFAULT_BENCHMARK='SPY'). There is no sector ETF benchmark, no beta adjustment, and no factor-neutral excess return. A high-beta tech name beating SPY in a tech rally is scored as skill even though it merely tracked its sector. The preregistration end-goal ('detect positive benchmark-relative edge after costs') cannot be met with raw SPY-relative returns alone.
findings.end_goal: Configurable, per-symbol-appropriate benchmark (sector ETF and/or beta-adjusted SPY) so excess return isolates idiosyncratic skill rather than sector/beta exposure; the chosen benchmark is recorded per forecast and used consistently in resolution.
findings.evidence: agent_intelligence_ledger.py:26 DEFAULT_BENCHMARK='SPY'; :822 relative_return = actual - benchmark, single benchmark; replay_ablation.py:850 same

findings.title: MIN_ACTION_RELATIVE_RETURN=0 flags only strictly-negative returns; zero-edge passes
findings.whats_missing: _append_metric_flags fires negative_action_return only when action_return < 0 (overnight_calibration.py:86-88, MIN=0.0000). A cohort with exactly-zero or trivially-positive-but-below-cost action return is not flagged, and the directional-accuracy floor is 0.50 (coin-flip) — an arm at 0.50 accuracy and +0.0001 return passes 'monitor'. Given costs are not subtracted (see no-transaction-costs finding), 'not negative gross' is far from 'profitable net'. Thresholds are also module-level constants with no config or per-sleeve tuning.
findings.end_goal: Guard thresholds require a positive margin above an after-cost breakeven (and an accuracy floor meaningfully above 0.50 with statistical confidence), configurable per sleeve, so a coin-flip / zero-edge cohort cannot reach the 'monitor / can increase influence' state.
findings.evidence: overnight_calibration.py:20-22 thresholds; :86-94 flag logic uses strict < and 0.50 floor

findings.title: Guard never checks whether the TradingAgents overlay BEATS the deterministic baseline
findings.whats_missing: The guard evaluates the deterministic_sleeve and tradingagents_overlay arms independently for absolute red flags (overnight_calibration.py:243-262) but never compares them. The entire point of the ablation ('if an extra layer does not beat the baseline after costs and false positives, it does not earn influence', replay_ablation.py:767-771) is a relative test, yet the guard can return 'monitor / can increase live influence' even when the TradingAgents overlay is WORSE than the baseline, as long as both pass absolute floors. So the overlay can earn influence without demonstrating incremental edge.
findings.end_goal: The guard computes overlay-minus-baseline incremental action-relative-return (after costs, with significance) and refuses can_increase_live_influence unless the overlay statistically beats the baseline; a worse-than-baseline overlay forces tighten regardless of absolute floors.
findings.evidence: overnight_calibration.py:243-264 independent arm flags, no diff; replay_ablation.py:767-771 plan states the relative requirement it never enforces

findings.title: replay_ablation builds plan packets but no engine actually runs ablation arms
findings.whats_missing: build_replay_ablation_plan_packet (replay_ablation.py:674-780) and build_walk_forward_replay_packet only enumerate arms (official_context_overlay, news_social_crawler_overlay, deep_research_methodology_overlay, tradingagents_advisory_overlay) and score whatever overlay decisions a fixture happens to contain. The fixture only ever populates tradingagents_advisory_overlay (replay_ablation.py:576-584); the other four overlay arms are always 'unavailable'. There is no code that actually replays the graph with each overlay toggled on/off to generate those arm decisions, so the ablation comparison the system is built around cannot produce real numbers.
findings.end_goal: An ablation runner that re-executes decisions with each advisory overlay independently enabled over the fixed as-of cohort, populating each arm's decisions so the multi-arm comparison (and per-overlay earned influence) is real rather than perpetually 'unavailable'.
findings.evidence: replay_ablation.py:622-654 arms enumerated; :576-584 fixture only writes tradingagents_advisory_overlay; _walk_forward_arm_decision returns None for missing overlays at :326-331

findings.title: Resolution price lookup hits live yfinance with no caching, retry, or rate handling
findings.whats_missing: _ledger_price_lookup imports yfinance inline and calls .history per symbol/window per forecast (cli/main.py:860-868) with no cache, no batching, no retry/backoff, and no logging of which symbols failed. With 4582 forecasts this is thousands of sequential network calls; any single failure returns None and silently leaves a forecast unresolved with resolution_note 'price lookup unavailable' (ledger.py:804-810) that is never surfaced as a metric. There is no record of how many resolutions failed vs succeeded.
findings.end_goal: A cached, batched, retried price provider (or a pre-collected price-rows file like the walk-forward path already supports) with explicit success/failure counts surfaced in the resolve command's JSON output, so resolution is fast, deterministic in tests, and failures are visible.
findings.evidence: cli/main.py:860-868 inline yfinance per call; agent_intelligence_ledger.py:804-810 silent unresolved note; walk-forward already supports _static_price_lookup_from_rows at cli/main.py:871-886

findings.title: Resolve loads, resolves, and rewrites the entire 5.8MB ledger every run (no incremental/atomic write)
findings.whats_missing: agent-ledger-resolve loads all forecasts, resolves, then write_ledger rewrites the whole JSONL with a non-atomic write_text (agent_intelligence_ledger.py:845-853; cli/main.py:1434-1440). The ledger is already 5.8MB / 4582 rows and grows unbounded; every resolve re-serializes everything, and an interruption mid-write can corrupt the ledger (no temp-file+rename). load_ledger also rebuilds existing_ids by re-reading the full file on every append (ledger.py:748).
findings.end_goal: Atomic ledger writes (temp file + rename) and an incremental update path that only rewrites changed records (or an index of resolved ids), so resolution scales and a crash cannot truncate the ledger.
findings.evidence: agent_intelligence_ledger.py:845-853 write_ledger uses write_text; :741-757 append re-reads full file; ledger.jsonl 5,827,790 bytes

findings.title: forecast_id keyed on created_at second can collide / dedupe distinct forecasts
findings.whats_missing: _forecast_id hashes (source_packet_id, ticker, agent, forecast_type, created_at@seconds, horizon_days) (ledger.py:138-140, 376-383). created_at comes from packet generated_at, identical for every ticker in one overnight packet. Two forecasts from the same agent/forecast_type for the same ticker in the same packet (e.g. analyst report plus rating mapped to same forecast_type prefix) would collide and be silently deduped by append_forecasts (ledger.py:751-753). Conversely re-running with a regenerated packet changes packet_id and re-appends duplicates of the same underlying claim.
findings.end_goal: Forecast identity derived from stable decision content (claim hash + horizon + as-of date) rather than packet-run timestamp, so the same logical forecast dedupes across reruns while genuinely distinct forecasts never collide.
findings.evidence: agent_intelligence_ledger.py:138-140 and :376-383 id parts include source_packet_id and created_at; append dedupe at :751-753

findings.title: No CI workflow runs the eval test suite; correctness regressions undetected
findings.whats_missing: There are eval tests (test_agent_intelligence_ledger.py 11, test_overnight_calibration_guard.py only 3, test_replay_ablation_plan.py 16, plus execution_board/source_quality/process_review/real_simulation/automation_health/promotion/prereg/schemas) but the overnight_calibration guard — the live-influence gatekeeper — has only 3 tests, and there is no evidence of a CI workflow enforcing them on change. A dirty 105-modified-file WIP branch with only 2 commits in history means these calibration modules can change with no gate.
findings.end_goal: A CI job that runs the full evals test suite (and a coverage floor) on every change touching tradingagents/evals or policy, with the calibration guard's decision matrix (collect_more/monitor/tighten, baseline-beat requirement, fail-closed-missing) thoroughly covered.
findings.evidence: tests/ has 11 eval test files; grep test count test_overnight_calibration_guard.py => 3; repo is not a git repo per env, history described as 2 commits

findings.title: Sleeve promotion gates take preregistered/benchmark/alpha as free inputs, not derived from ledger/walk-forward evidence
findings.whats_missing: evaluate_sleeve_promotion (policy/promotion.py:53-104) checks gates like preregistered, ci_green, shadow_confirmed, benchmark_excess_return >= min, cost_adjusted_alpha >= min — but these are passed in as SleevePromotionEvidence fields by the caller with no link to the actual resolved ledger, walk-forward cohort, or calibration guard. Nothing forces benchmark_excess_return / recent_alpha to come from the real scored evidence, so a caller can assert promotion-worthy numbers that the calibration system has not validated. The defaults are also min=0 (promotion.py:29-31), i.e. any non-negative alpha passes.
findings.end_goal: Promotion evidence is populated directly from resolved-ledger / walk-forward cohort metrics (after costs, with significance) and is cross-checked against the calibration guard, so a sleeve cannot be promoted toward tiny-live unless the same evidence pipeline that powers the guard says it earned it; minimum thresholds default to a positive after-cost margin.
findings.evidence: policy/promotion.py:53-69 gates from caller-supplied evidence; :29-31 min_* default Decimal('0')

findings.title: process_review hardcodes required-doc paths and a single dated plan file
findings.whats_missing: build_process_review hardcodes REQUIRED_DOCS including a specific dated plan path docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-02-tradingagents-autonomous-revision.md (process_review.py:14-19) and a 50000-token hotspot magic threshold (:106). As plans are added/renamed this list silently rots; a missing-but-renamed doc reports as a finding forever, and the 50k threshold is undocumented. It also only flags, never weights findings by severity.
findings.end_goal: Required-doc set and token thresholds are config-driven (or discovered), the dated plan reference is generalized, and findings carry severity so the process review stays accurate as the repo evolves.
findings.evidence: process_review.py:14-19 REQUIRED_DOCS with dated path; :106 hardcoded 50000

findings.title: No surfaced metric for resolution coverage / staleness of the ledger itself
findings.whats_missing: write_summary records forecast_count, resolved_forecast_count, and per-agent stats (ledger.py:1010-1023) but nothing tracks how many DUE forecasts remain unresolved (created_at+horizon elapsed but resolution failed), how stale the oldest unresolved forecast is, or the price-lookup failure rate. The headline failure state of this very system (4582 forecasts, 0 resolved) is invisible from the summary — you only see it by inspecting the raw ledger. There is no alert when resolution coverage is ~0%.
findings.end_goal: The summary (and the calibration guard) report resolution_coverage = resolved/due, count of overdue-unresolved forecasts, and oldest-unresolved age, with a red flag when coverage is below a floor, so a stuck resolution loop is detected automatically rather than after manual ledger inspection.
findings.evidence: agent_intelligence_ledger.py:896-901 summary fields lack due/overdue/coverage; observed state ledger 4582 rows / 0 resolved not reflected in summary.json

findings.title: Anthropic client never sets max_tokens, so long analyst reports silently truncate
findings.whats_missing: No anthropic_max_tokens config key exists and the client only forwards max_tokens if the caller passes it (anthropic_client.py:9-12, default_config.py:104-117 has none); langchain_anthropic defaults ChatAnthropic max_tokens to ~1024, truncating multi-paragraph analyst/PM reports mid-sentence.
findings.end_goal: A provider-appropriate max_tokens default (e.g. 8192+) is set for Anthropic from config so deep-think reports and structured PM decisions are never cut off, with a config key anthropic_max_tokens documented in default_config.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/llm_clients/anthropic_client.py:9-12,57-64; default_config.py:104-117 (no max_tokens)

findings.title: No timeout or max_retries default for any LLM provider — overnight runs can hang indefinitely
findings.whats_missing: timeout/max_retries are in every client's passthrough tuple but are never set in default_config (grep shows zero matches in default_config.py), so an unattended overnight run that hits a stalled provider socket blocks forever with no bounded retry/backoff.
findings.end_goal: Config-driven default timeout (e.g. 120s) and max_retries (e.g. 3 with exponential backoff) applied uniformly across all provider clients so a hung provider fails fast and the pipeline either retries or fails closed rather than hanging the overnight job.
findings.evidence: default_config.py (no timeout/max_retries keys); openai_client.py:140-145, anthropic_client.py:9-12, google_client.py:36

findings.title: Concurrent analyst Send fan-out merges branch message scratchpads, risking cross-branch RemoveMessage collisions
findings.whats_missing: In the concurrency>1 path each Send branch starts with messages=[] but tool-bound analysts append many messages and their per-branch Msg Clear nodes emit RemoveMessage-by-id; at the batch-join the add_messages reducer merges all branches, so one branch's cleanup can target/skip ids that only exist after merge, leaving orphaned tool messages.
findings.end_goal: Parallel analyst branches use isolated sub-states (or report-only returns with no shared messages channel) so concurrent execution is provably equivalent to sequential output, verified by an integration test that runs concurrency=2 end-to-end and asserts clean message state.
findings.evidence: graph/setup.py:139-170; agent_states.py:47 (messages via MessagesState add_messages); market_analyst.py:92-95

findings.title: AgentState report/scalar keys use default last-write-wins reducer, unsafe under any future shared-key concurrent write
findings.whats_missing: market_report/sentiment_report/news_report/fundamentals_report and sender are plain Annotated[str,...] with no reducer; today each analyst writes a distinct key so it works, but the design is one refactor away from an InvalidUpdateError ('can receive only one value per step') if two concurrent branches ever write the same scalar.
findings.end_goal: Each concurrently-written state key carries an explicit reducer (or a documented invariant + test) so the parallel graph shape is robust to future analyst additions that share a key.
findings.evidence: agent_states.py:52-60; graph/setup.py:139-170

findings.title: Docs disagree on default analyst_concurrency_limit (2 vs reverted to 1), and parallel path is under-exercised
findings.whats_missing: PIPELINE_ARCHITECTURE_AUDIT.md:184 and IMPROVEMENT_PROGRAM.md:1883 claim overnight profiles default to concurrency=2, but reports/overnight_reliability/overnight-research-repair-20260607.md:46,82 says compact/market-news were reverted to 1; the live default in default_config.py:133 is 1, so the advertised parallelism is effectively off.
findings.end_goal: A single source of truth states the actual concurrency default, the docs are reconciled, and if 2 is intended it is enabled and covered by an end-to-end test rather than left disabled after a revert.
findings.evidence: docs/PIPELINE_ARCHITECTURE_AUDIT.md:184; reports/overnight_reliability/overnight-research-repair-20260607.md:46,82; default_config.py:133

findings.title: Graph layer has no token/cost accounting or budget enforcement
findings.whats_missing: trading_graph accepts callbacks but the graph itself never aggregates usage_metadata/prompt+completion tokens or estimated cost per run; there is no per-run token ledger or budget cap, so an overnight batch can silently burn unbounded spend and token-efficiency cannot be measured per node.
findings.end_goal: Per-run and per-node token/cost accounting is captured (via callback aggregation) and written alongside the state log, with an optional configurable per-run token/cost budget that fails closed when exceeded.
findings.evidence: trading_graph.py:62-66,408-410 (callbacks passed but no aggregation); only grep hit for 'token' in graph/ is unrelated

findings.title: Anthropic effort param silently dropped for unsupported models with no warning
findings.whats_missing: When a user configures anthropic_effort=high but selects Haiku (unsupported), _supports_effort returns False and the kwarg is dropped silently (anthropic_client.py:60-62) — the user believes high-effort reasoning is active when it is not.
findings.end_goal: A one-time warning is logged when a requested effort/reasoning level is dropped because the chosen model does not support it, so misconfiguration is visible.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/llm_clients/anthropic_client.py:25-28,60-62

findings.title: DeepSeek reasoning_content roundtrip zips outgoing payload messages against input messages, which can misalign
findings.whats_missing: _get_request_payload zips payload['messages'] with _input_to_messages(input_) positionally (openai_client.py:83-92), but langchain may inject/merge system messages or reorder, so the AIMessage carrying reasoning_content can be matched to the wrong payload dict, attaching reasoning to the wrong turn or skipping it.
findings.end_goal: Reasoning_content is re-attached by matching on message identity/role rather than positional zip, with a regression test covering a ChatPromptTemplate-driven multi-turn DeepSeek thinking call.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/llm_clients/openai_client.py:83-92,51-65

findings.title: normalize_content mutates the shared response object in place
findings.whats_missing: normalize_content reassigns response.content on the original object (base_client.py:21) rather than returning a copy; any callback/tracer that already captured the response sees its content change underneath it, and reasoning blocks are discarded irrecoverably.
findings.end_goal: Content normalization returns a normalized view without destructively mutating the provider's response, or explicitly documents and tests that mutation is intended and safe for all callback consumers.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/llm_clients/base_client.py:14-22

findings.title: clear_checkpoint hardcodes SqliteSaver table names and swallows schema errors
findings.whats_missing: clear_checkpoint deletes from hardcoded 'writes'/'checkpoints' tables and silently passes on OperationalError (checkpointer.py:84-88); a langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite version bump that renames tables (e.g. adds checkpoint_blobs) leaves stale rows behind with no error, so a 'cleared' run silently resumes from a stale checkpoint.
findings.end_goal: Checkpoint clearing uses the SqliteSaver's own delete API (or discovers tables dynamically) and logs rather than swallows unexpected schema errors, with a test pinning behavior across the pinned langgraph version.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/graph/checkpointer.py:76-90

findings.title: Checkpoint thread_id keys only on ticker+date, ignoring config/model/analyst-set changes
findings.whats_missing: thread_id hashes only ticker:date (checkpointer.py:28-30); if a run crashes, then the user changes models/selected_analysts/prompts and re-runs the same ticker+date, it resumes mid-graph against an incompatible node topology, producing corrupt or KeyError state.
findings.end_goal: thread_id incorporates a hash of the graph-shape-affecting config (selected analysts, provider/model, debate rounds) so a changed configuration starts fresh instead of resuming an incompatible checkpoint.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/graph/checkpointer.py:28-30; trading_graph.py:368-371

findings.title: Checkpointer compiled graph not reset and checkpoint not retried-safe on partial failure
findings.whats_missing: propagate enters the checkpointer context and recompiles self.graph, but if _resolve_pending_entries or state logging throws after invoke, clear_checkpoint may not run (it is only called on the success line 403-406 inside _run_graph), leaving a completed-but-unclearable checkpoint that wrongly resumes next time.
findings.end_goal: Checkpoint clearing happens in a finally/guaranteed path tied to successful graph completion (not interleaved with post-processing I/O), so a crash in logging never leaves a misleading resumable checkpoint.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/graph/trading_graph.py:351-357,402-406

findings.title: Hand-maintained model catalog lists speculative future models with no freshness/validation guard
findings.whats_missing: MODEL_OPTIONS hardcodes many not-yet-real or fast-moving IDs (gpt-5.5-pro, claude-opus-4-7, gemini-3.1-pro-preview, GLM-5.1, MiniMax-M2.7) with no last-verified date or CI check; validators.validate_model only warns, so a typo'd or retired ID passes through to the provider as a runtime 404.
findings.end_goal: The catalog carries a last-verified date and a CI/test (or optional live ping) that flags entries the provider no longer serves, so stale model IDs are caught before an overnight run fails on a 404.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/llm_clients/model_catalog.py:94-196; validators.py:12-25 (warn-only)

findings.title: Capability table only covers OpenAI-compatible providers; Anthropic/Google structured-output quirks are unmodeled
findings.whats_missing: get_capabilities is consulted only by NormalizedChatOpenAI; Anthropic and Google clients have no equivalent capability dispatch, so per-model structured-output method selection and tool_choice quirks for those providers are hardcoded in langchain defaults with no override path.
findings.end_goal: A unified capability model (or per-provider tables) covers all four first-class providers so structured-output method, tool_choice support, and reasoning quirks are declarative everywhere, not just for OpenAI-compatible models.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/llm_clients/capabilities.py:119-126; openai_client.py:35-48 (only consumer); anthropic_client.py / google_client.py (no capability use)

findings.title: Structured-output fallback catches bare Exception and degrades to free-text silently
findings.whats_missing: invoke_structured_or_freetext catches Exception and falls back to plain text on ANY error including transient network/timeout (structured.py:67-74); a flaky provider call silently produces an unstructured PM decision, which may then fail rating extraction or feed a lower-quality decision into the live-gated path with only a warning.
findings.end_goal: Transient errors are retried with backoff before the free-text fallback fires, and the fallback distinguishes schema/parse failures (legitimate downgrade) from infra failures (should retry/fail), with metrics on how often fallback triggers.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/agents/utils/structured.py:63-74

findings.title: should_continue_* index messages[-1] without guarding empty list
findings.whats_missing: should_continue_market/news/fundamentals do messages[-1].tool_calls (conditional_logic.py:16-46); if an analyst node ever returns with an empty messages channel (e.g. after aggressive cleanup or a provider returning no content), this raises IndexError/AttributeError and aborts the run.
findings.end_goal: Routing predicates defensively handle empty/None message lists and messages lacking tool_calls, routing to cleanup rather than crashing the graph.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/graph/conditional_logic.py:14-46

findings.title: Debate/risk round-count comments contradict the code (off-by-one documentation)
findings.whats_missing: should_continue_debate comments '3 rounds of back-and-forth' next to count >= 2*max_debate_rounds, and risk says '3 rounds' next to count >= 3*max_risk_discuss_rounds (conditional_logic.py:51-63); with default max=1 these actually allow 2 and 3 messages respectively, so the comments misstate behavior and invite mis-tuning.
findings.end_goal: Comments precisely describe the message/round math for the configured max so an operator tuning debate depth gets the count they expect.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/graph/conditional_logic.py:48-69

findings.title: Debate and risk routing depend on response prefix string matching ('Bull'/'Aggressive')
findings.whats_missing: should_continue_debate routes on current_response.startswith('Bull') and risk on latest_speaker.startswith('Aggressive'/'Conservative') (conditional_logic.py:55-69); if an agent prepends formatting, translates output (output_language config), or leaves the field empty, routing silently flips to the wrong speaker, breaking alternation.
findings.end_goal: Turn alternation is driven by an explicit structured turn/role field set by each node, not by prefix-matching free-text content, so non-English output_language or formatting changes cannot corrupt the debate order.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/graph/conditional_logic.py:55-69; default_config.py:128 (output_language)

findings.title: max_recur_limit not validated against debate/risk round counts
findings.whats_missing: recursion_limit is fixed at 100 (propagation.py:69) independent of max_debate_rounds/max_risk_discuss_rounds; a user raising rounds high (or enabling concurrency tool loops) can exceed the limit and get an opaque GraphRecursionError mid-run with no actionable message.
findings.end_goal: The recursion limit is computed from (or validated against) the configured round counts and analyst tool-loop budget so a high-rounds config either gets enough headroom or fails early with a clear message.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/graph/propagation.py:14,69; conditional_logic.py:9-12

findings.title: Gemini 2.5 thinking_level falls through to thinking_budget=0 (thinking disabled) for unexpected values
findings.whats_missing: For Gemini 2.5, only 'high' and 'minimal' are mapped; any other thinking_level (e.g. 'medium','low') falls to the else branch setting thinking_budget=0, which fully disables thinking on a deep-think model without warning (google_client.py:57-64).
findings.end_goal: Unrecognized thinking_level values for Gemini 2.5 map to a sensible non-zero budget (or dynamic -1) and warn, rather than silently disabling reasoning on the deep model.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/llm_clients/google_client.py:49-64

findings.title: Only OpenAI-compatible client raises on missing API key; Anthropic/Google fail late at first call
findings.whats_missing: OpenAIClient raises a clear ValueError when its provider key env is unset (openai_client.py:216-221), but AnthropicClient and GoogleClient never check api_key presence — they only fail deep inside the first network call, so an overnight run with a missing ANTHROPIC_API_KEY fails opaquely after setup rather than at construction.
findings.end_goal: All provider clients validate required credentials at get_llm() time with the same actionable error format (which env var to set), so credential gaps fail fast before the graph starts.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/llm_clients/openai_client.py:211-221; anthropic_client.py:49-64; google_client.py:40-43

findings.title: OpenAI-compatible client hardcodes api_key='ollama' for keyless providers
findings.whats_missing: When get_api_key_env returns None (ollama), the client passes the literal api_key='ollama' (openai_client.py:223); a remote OLLAMA_BASE_URL behind an auth proxy (now supported) would reject this, and the magic string is undocumented.
findings.end_goal: Keyless local providers either omit api_key or read an optional override env (e.g. OLLAMA_API_KEY) so remote/proxied Ollama endpoints can authenticate, with the placeholder documented.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/llm_clients/openai_client.py:209-223,166-179

findings.title: Debug-mode stream merge uses chunk.update which can produce a different final_state than invoke
findings.whats_missing: In debug mode final_state is built by final_state.update(chunk) over streamed value-mode chunks (trading_graph.py:382-385); with stream_mode='values' each chunk is a full snapshot so update mostly works, but partial/empty chunks or reducer-merged channels (messages) are overwritten rather than reduced, so debug runs can diverge from production invoke output the code claims to match.
findings.end_goal: Debug mode returns the same final state as invoke() by taking the last full 'values' snapshot (or using graph.invoke and streaming only for display), verified by a test asserting debug and non-debug final states are equal.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/graph/trading_graph.py:373-387

findings.title: Pending forecast resolution only runs for the ticker being analyzed, so most of the 4582 forecasts never resolve
findings.whats_missing: _resolve_pending_entries filters pending entries to the current ticker (trading_graph.py:288), so a forecast for AAPL only resolves the next time AAPL is run; with a broad universe most entries accumulate unresolved forever — directly matching the reported '0 of 4582 resolved' ledger problem.
findings.end_goal: A scheduled/standalone resolver sweeps ALL due pending entries (not just the current ticker) on each overnight run, batching yfinance calls, so the calibration ledger actually fills and walk-forward accuracy can be measured.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/graph/trading_graph.py:278-316 (line 288 same-ticker filter)

findings.title: _fetch_returns hardcodes a 5-day holding window and SPY-style benchmark with no per-decision horizon
findings.whats_missing: holding_days defaults to 5 everywhere (trading_graph.py:231) regardless of the decision's actual intended horizon; a Buy meant as a multi-week thesis is scored on a 5-day window, biasing the directional-accuracy/alpha metrics that drive the calibration guard.
findings.end_goal: Holding horizon is derived from the decision (or configurable per strategy) and stored with the forecast so outcome resolution scores each call over the horizon it was actually made for.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/graph/trading_graph.py:230-270

findings.title: with_structured_output path bypasses normalize_content / capability dispatch on non-OpenAI providers
findings.whats_missing: Anthropic/Google/Azure Normalized* subclasses override invoke() for normalization but do not override with_structured_output, so the structured runnable they build is the raw langchain one; any content-shape normalization or capability gating those providers need for structured calls is absent.
findings.end_goal: Structured-output construction is capability-aware and normalization-consistent across all providers (parallel to the OpenAI override), so typed PM/Trader decisions behave identically regardless of provider.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/llm_clients/anthropic_client.py:31-41; google_client.py:11-20; azure_client.py:26-31

findings.title: Entire graph/llm_clients hardening lives on an uncommitted 2-commit WIP branch
findings.whats_missing: All 17 graph/llm_clients source files are modified-uncommitted and the two new tests (test_graph_tool_routing.py, test_llm_client_config.py) are untracked on wip/submit-path-hardening-2026-06-05 with only 2 commits in history; a crash or stash loses the entire concurrency/capability/checkpoint rework (327 insertions in this subsystem alone).
findings.end_goal: The graph/llm_clients changes are committed in focused commits with the new tests tracked, on a branch ready for review/merge, so the work is durable and reviewable.
findings.evidence: git status: 17 M files under tradingagents/graph+llm_clients, 2 untracked tests; git log shows 2 commits, branch wip/submit-path-hardening-2026-06-05

findings.title: No CI workflow runs the graph/llm_clients test suite
findings.whats_missing: The subsystem has good unit tests (checkpoint resume, tool routing, fanout shape, client config) but they are untracked/uncommitted and there is no evidence of a CI workflow executing them, so regressions in routing/capabilities/checkpoint land silently.
findings.end_goal: A CI workflow runs the full graph and llm_clients test suite on every push, including the concurrency-shape and capability-dispatch tests, gating merges.
findings.evidence: tests/test_checkpoint_resume.py, test_graph_tool_routing.py (untracked), test_llm_client_config.py (untracked); no CI hits in repo for these

findings.title: Capability forward-compat patterns may over-match non-thinking variants
findings.whats_missing: _BY_PATTERN maps ^deepseek-v\d to _DEEPSEEK_THINKING and ^MiniMax-M\d to _MINIMAX_THINKING (capabilities.py:112-116), but a future non-thinking deepseek-v5-chat or MiniMax-M3-text would inherit thinking-only quirks (suppressed tool_choice, reasoning_split) it doesn't support, breaking structured output.
findings.end_goal: Patterns are scoped to the reasoning variants (or default to the safe non-thinking caps) so a new non-reasoning model in the same family doesn't inherit reasoning-only API restrictions.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/llm_clients/capabilities.py:110-116

findings.title: AnalystWallTimeTracker exists but is not wired into trading_graph's run loop
findings.whats_missing: analyst_execution.py defines AnalystWallTimeTracker and sync_analyst_tracker_from_chunk (lines 94-154) but trading_graph._run_graph never instantiates or feeds them, so the per-analyst wall-time observability they provide is dead code in the main path.
findings.end_goal: The run loop drives the wall-time tracker from streamed chunks and surfaces per-analyst timing in logs/observability, or the unused tracker is removed to avoid dead code.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/graph/analyst_execution.py:94-154; trading_graph.py:373-408 (no tracker use)

findings.title: Azure client passes reasoning_effort blindly to any deployment
findings.whats_missing: AzureOpenAIClient forwards reasoning_effort unconditionally (azure_client.py:8-11,86-88) with no per-deployment capability check; a non-reasoning Azure deployment (e.g. gpt-4.1) will 400 on the reasoning_effort param.
findings.end_goal: Azure reasoning_effort is gated by deployment/model capability (or caught and stripped on 400) so mixed reasoning/non-reasoning Azure deployments both work.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/llm_clients/azure_client.py:8-11,86-90

findings.title: cli/main.py is a 10,921-line monolith hosting ~90 commands and all order routing
findings.whats_missing: A single 443KB module defines 6 Typer apps, ~90 commands, and ~200 module-level helpers. Money-movement commands (alpaca submit, supervise-hourly), pure-analysis research producers, interactive analyze flow, and Rich display code all live in one file. Several command functions are individually huge (alpaca_supervise_hourly is ~525 lines 10210-10734; alpaca_plan_overnight ~415 lines with 26 options 9126-9540; alpaca_verify_overnight_system 9749-10210). This makes review of the live-trading path dangerous and merge-conflict-prone, and the file is part of the dirty WIP tree.
findings.end_goal: main.py decomposed into a thin entrypoint (app assembly + main()) plus command-group modules: cli/commands/alpaca.py, cli/commands/research.py, cli/commands/policy.py, cli/commands/integrations.py, cli/commands/paper_tournament.py, and cli/analyze/ (interactive runner + MessageBuffer + Rich display). Each command function stays well under ~80 lines by extracting orchestration into tradingagents/ service functions. main.py shrinks to assembly + shared CLI helpers only.
findings.evidence: cli/main.py wc -l = 10921; alpaca_supervise_hourly 10210-10734; alpaca_plan_overnight 9126-9540 (26 typer.Option params); single @app.command() analyze at 8276
findings.recommended_change: Split into a cli/commands package by Typer group; move heavy logic into tradingagents service modules; keep main.py as wiring.

findings.title: alpaca submit (documented live path) routes through hardcoded GOOGL/NVDA tickets and stale limit prices
findings.whats_missing: _ticket_orders() (3543-3581) hardcodes ticket 'googl-starter' GOOGL notional 450 limit 383.50 and 'nvda-pullback' NVDA notional 250 limit 212.25, with a third candidate auto-ranked from a fixed mega-cap list via yfinance (_rank_third_candidate 3527-3540). alpaca submit (8425) and alpaca preview (8386) both call this. The packet builder and code comments label the whole path 'legacy' (3741-3763, 8551, 8599, 8621), yet README lines 195-196 promote `tradingagents alpaca submit` as the live trading entry. A user running the documented command would submit buy orders for GOOGL/NVDA at multi-month-stale hardcoded limit prices.
findings.end_goal: alpaca submit either (a) is removed/hidden and replaced in docs by the supervise-hourly / preopen-validation flow that derives orders from packets, or (b) requires orders to be supplied from a validated plan packet (no hardcoded symbols/prices). README stops advertising the legacy command for live money. If retained, it is clearly marked deprecated in --help and refuses to run without an explicit --i-understand-legacy flag.
findings.evidence: cli/main.py:3549-3580 (_ticket_orders hardcoded GOOGL 383.50 / NVDA 212.25); 3527-3540 (_rank_third_candidate fixed universe); README.md:195-196
findings.recommended_change: Deprecate alpaca submit; source orders from plan packets; correct README live-trading section.

findings.title: Order-submitting commands (alpaca submit) lack the --json-output contract every other command exposes
findings.whats_missing: 71 commands take a --json-output flag, but alpaca submit (8425-8674) has none — it only console.prints lines and a packet path. The most important command for an n8n/automation control-plane to parse the result of a real submission cannot emit machine-readable output and instead requires re-reading the latest.json packet from disk. alpaca check (8296) also has no --json-output.
findings.end_goal: alpaca submit and alpaca check accept --json-output and emit the submit receipt packet (status/submitted/failed/issues/spend) to stdout, matching supervise-hourly. Every command that performs an action has a parseable JSON result so the control plane never has to scrape the filesystem.
findings.evidence: cli/main.py:8425-8437 (alpaca_submit signature has no json_output param); 8296-8320 (alpaca_check no json_output); 71 json_output occurrences elsewhere

findings.title: JSON output emitted three different ways (print / typer.echo / console.print) across commands
findings.whats_missing: JSON is printed via bare print() in some commands (integrations_doctor 744, policy_pullback_support 3521), typer.echo() in most (e.g. 801, 815, 1456), creating risk that Rich console wrapping/markup or stream buffering corrupts JSON in some paths but not others. There is no single helper that guarantees raw, unwrapped stdout for --json-output.
findings.end_goal: One emit_json(payload) helper used by every command, writing compact/indented JSON to stdout with no Rich markup interpretation; bare print() and console.print() are never used for --json-output. A test asserts json.loads() round-trips stdout for representative commands.
findings.evidence: cli/main.py:744 (print), 3521 (print), 801/815/1456 (typer.echo)

findings.title: get_ticker / get_analysis_date duplicated and divergent between utils.py and main.py
findings.whats_missing: cli/utils.py defines get_ticker (26-43) and get_analysis_date (70-100); cli/main.py redefines both (7648-7688) with different validation rules. utils.get_ticker calls normalize_ticker_symbol and exits on empty; main.get_ticker allows empty -> defaults to 'SPY', restricts charset to alnum+._-^, max 32. utils.get_analysis_date uses regex+strptime; main.get_analysis_date additionally rejects future dates. main.py does NOT import these from utils, so the module-level redefinitions silently win — the utils versions are partly dead and the two implementations can drift further. A reader cannot tell which validation actually runs.
findings.end_goal: A single canonical get_ticker and get_analysis_date in cli/utils.py with the union of the best validation (charset + non-future date), imported and used by main.py. No shadowing redefinitions; dead copies removed.
findings.evidence: cli/utils.py:26-43 and 70-100; cli/main.py:7648-7668 and 7671-7687 (redefinitions); main.py import block 36-52 does not import get_ticker/get_analysis_date

findings.title: User-supplied Decimal/price args converted with no try/except, raising raw InvalidOperation tracebacks
findings.whats_missing: Many commands take money/price/threshold values as str options and call Decimal(value) directly without catching decimal.InvalidOperation: agent-ledger-resolve/update/from-* (1343, 1391, 1438, 1503), policy pullback-support (3480-3485), alpaca pullback-support-paper (8714-8726), paper-tournament init (8948-8950). A typo like --alpha-threshold-pct 1.5x or --current-price abc produces an unhandled traceback instead of a clean typer.BadParameter. On a money-adjacent command this is poor UX and obscures the real problem in automation logs.
findings.end_goal: A shared _decimal_option(value, name) helper validates and converts, raising typer.BadParameter('--name must be a number') on failure. All raw Decimal(user_input) calls go through it; a test feeds a malformed value and asserts exit code 2 with a clean message.
findings.evidence: cli/main.py:1438, 1503, 3480-3485, 8714-8726, 8948-8950 (Decimal(...) on raw option strings, no guard)

findings.title: Categorical options (graph-profile, notification-policy, volume/gap/regime state) accept any string with no enum validation
findings.whats_missing: Options that have a fixed valid set are typed as free-form str: --overnight-graph-profile help says 'full, compact, market-news, or market-only' (9165-9169) but accepts anything; --notification-policy 'material-only/every-check/daily-digest/urgent-exceptions' (10224-10228) is unchecked; policy pullback-support --sell-volume-state/--gap-state/--regime-state/--sector-relative-strength (3464-3467) are unchecked strings. A misspelled value silently falls through to a default branch or a downstream behavior the operator didn't intend.
findings.end_goal: These become typer options backed by str Enums (or callback-validated choices) so invalid values are rejected at parse time with the allowed list shown in --help. Shell completion then offers the valid values.
findings.evidence: cli/main.py:9165-9169 (overnight_graph_profile), 10224-10228 (notification_policy), 3464-3467 (pullback categorical states)

findings.title: Primary `analyze` command is interactive-only — no flags for ticker/date/provider, blocking CI and automation
findings.whats_missing: analyze (8276-8293) exposes only --checkpoint and --clear-checkpoints and always calls run_analysis() -> get_user_selections() which blocks on questionary prompts (7471-7645). There is no way to run a deterministic analysis non-interactively (e.g. analyze --ticker AAPL --date 2026-06-07 --provider openai --depth medium), so the core research pipeline cannot be exercised in CI, smoke tests, or scripted overnight runs without driving a TTY.
findings.end_goal: analyze accepts optional --ticker/--date/--analysts/--provider/--quick-model/--deep-model/--depth/--output-language flags; when all required values are supplied it skips the interactive prompts; missing values still prompt. A CI smoke test invokes analyze fully non-interactively against a stub graph.
findings.evidence: cli/main.py:8277-8293 (analyze only has checkpoint flags); 7471-7645 get_user_selections all questionary-driven

findings.title: Interactive analyze path (run_analysis, get_user_selections, MessageBuffer, display) has zero CliRunner coverage
findings.whats_missing: test_alpaca_cli.py has 98 tests but none reference analyze, run_analysis, get_user_selections, or MessageBuffer (grep across tests/ returns nothing). The ~1,400-line interactive/display subsystem (MessageBuffer 7052-7240, run_analysis 7982-8273, update_display, classify_message_type, save_report_to_disk) is completely untested, including the chunk-merge and report-section finalization logic.
findings.end_goal: Unit tests for MessageBuffer (report completion counting, status transitions), classify_message_type, save_report_to_disk, and a CliRunner test that drives analyze non-interactively against a stubbed TradingAgentsGraph stream and asserts reports are written and final decision processed.
findings.evidence: grep of tests/ for analyze/run_analysis/get_user_selections returns no matches; MessageBuffer 7052-7240; run_analysis 7982-8273

findings.title: run_analysis crashes with KeyError if the graph stream ends without final_trade_decision
findings.whats_missing: After merging streamed chunks, run_analysis does graph.process_signal(final_state['final_trade_decision']) (8231) with direct subscript access. If the run is interrupted, a budget cap fires mid-pipeline, or the portfolio manager node never emits, final_state lacks that key and the program dies with a raw KeyError inside the Live display teardown, losing the partial reports the user could otherwise have saved.
findings.end_goal: run_analysis checks for final_trade_decision presence, and on absence prints a clear 'analysis ended before a final decision' message, still offers to save the partial reports it does have, and exits non-zero cleanly rather than tracebacking.
findings.evidence: cli/main.py:8228-8231 (final_state.update loop then final_state['final_trade_decision'] subscript)

findings.title: paper-tournament run submit loop lacks per-order try/except, crashing and losing ledger record on broker error
findings.whats_missing: alpaca paper-tournament run submits orders in a bare loop (9010-9018): paper_client.submit_order(order_payload) with no try/except. If any order raises, record_submitted_orders (9027) is never reached, so orders already submitted to the broker are not recorded in the ledger, and the user gets a raw traceback. This is inconsistent with supervise-hourly which wraps each submit in try/except and classifies the error (10521-10598).
findings.end_goal: The tournament submit loop wraps each submit_order in try/except using the same classify_alpaca_submit_error path, records every successful submit even when a later one fails, and writes a packet with failed-order evidence instead of crashing.
findings.evidence: cli/main.py:9008-9027 (loop with no try/except); contrast 10521-10598 supervise-hourly per-order guard

findings.title: alpaca_supervise_hourly is a single ~525-line function mixing broker reads, gating, submission, and packet assembly
findings.whats_missing: The most safety-critical command (it can submit live orders with --submit-actions) is one ~525-line function (10210-10734) interleaving: account/position/order reads, dynamic cap computation, candidate signal building, overnight/premarket/preopen validation, BOARD review gating, decision building, multiple sequential guardrail layers, the per-order submit loop with idempotency reconciliation, and evidence/packet assembly. Reviewing or modifying any one gate requires understanding the entire function; the gating sequence is hard to audit for fail-closed correctness.
findings.end_goal: Decomposed into named, individually testable steps — gather_supervisor_inputs(), build_supervisor_decision(), run_pre_submit_guards() (returns blocked decision or approval), submit_supervisor_actions() (the only place submit_order is called), assemble_supervisor_evidence(). The CLI command orchestrates these; each guard layer has a focused unit test proving it blocks.
findings.evidence: cli/main.py:10210-10734 (alpaca_supervise_hourly, ~525 lines, multiple inline replace()-based gates)

findings.title: MessageBuffer instantiated as a module-level global at import time
findings.whats_missing: message_buffer = MessageBuffer() at module scope (7238) means importing cli.main allocates and holds shared mutable display state, and run_analysis monkeypatches its methods (8071-8073) by reassigning instance attributes. This shared singleton makes the interactive flow non-reentrant and hard to test in isolation, and couples import side effects to display concerns.
findings.end_goal: MessageBuffer is created inside run_analysis (or an Analyze session object) and passed explicitly; no module-level mutable singleton; the save-decorator wiring lives on the instance the session owns.
findings.evidence: cli/main.py:7238 (message_buffer = MessageBuffer()); 8071-8073 (instance method reassignment)

findings.title: announcements.py uses getpass.getpass() as a 'Press Enter to continue' pause
findings.whats_missing: display_announcements calls getpass.getpass('Press Enter to continue...') (50) purely to pause for Enter. getpass is for hidden secret entry; using it here suppresses echo unnecessarily, behaves oddly when stdin is not a TTY (it warns/raises in some environments, e.g. piped automation), and is semantically misleading. fetch_announcements also has mutable-style defaults url=None/timeout=None resolved inside, and a broad bare except Exception that hides all errors silently.
findings.end_goal: Use input('Press Enter to continue...') (or typer.confirm) for the pause; guard for non-interactive stdin so automated/n8n invocations don't block or error. fetch_announcements narrows its except to network/JSON errors and logs at debug level.
findings.evidence: cli/announcements.py:50 (getpass.getpass as Enter pause); 24 (bare except Exception)

findings.title: Default Codex/MCP config path hardcodes Windows-only C:\cm
findings.whats_missing: _default_codex_config_path (559-561) returns Path(CODEX_HOME or 'C:\\cm')/config.toml. The fallback C:\cm is a non-standard, machine-specific Windows path that will silently resolve to a non-existent file on any other machine (and on Mac/Linux), making integrations doctor's MCP/Composio detection always report nothing without explanation. The Mac Ollama helper lane is a stated weak area, so cross-platform correctness here matters.
findings.end_goal: Fallback uses a platform-appropriate default (e.g. ~/.codex/config.toml) and integrations doctor reports clearly when the config path does not exist rather than treating absence as 'no MCP servers configured'.
findings.evidence: cli/main.py:559-561 (codex_home = ... or r'C:\cm')

findings.title: No consolidated CLI command reference/runbook for the ~90 commands
findings.whats_missing: There is no single document enumerating the ~90 commands across alpaca/research/policy/integrations/paper-tournament with purpose, key flags, JSON-output shape, and which ones can move money vs are analysis-only. README only shows a handful of examples (and promotes the legacy submit). Operators relying on overnight automation cannot discover commands like preopen-validation, verify-overnight-system, overnight-calibration-guard, agent-ledger-update, or n8n-sync-* without grepping main.py.
findings.end_goal: A docs/CLI_REFERENCE.md (generatable from Typer) listing every command grouped by app, marked analysis-only vs order-capable, with the canonical overnight runbook (plan-overnight -> preopen-validation -> supervise-hourly -> supervisor-daily-report) and each command's --json-output schema reference.
findings.evidence: README.md:183-227 only shows a few commands; ~90 commands exist (grep of @*_app.command in cli/main.py); no docs/CLI_REFERENCE.md present

findings.title: README live-trading examples promote the legacy hardcoded-ticket submit path
findings.whats_missing: README.md:195-196 instruct users to run `tradingagents alpaca submit --run-id ... --third-symbol MSFT --third-limit-price 500` as the live trading flow, with no warning that GOOGL/NVDA tickets and their limit prices are hardcoded in _ticket_orders and that the command is internally labeled 'legacy'. A user following the README would place real orders for stale hardcoded names/prices.
findings.end_goal: README live-trading section points to the packet-driven supervise-hourly/preopen-validation flow (already shown at 217-219) as the supported path; any mention of alpaca submit clearly labels it legacy/manual with the hardcoded-symbol caveat, or it is removed.
findings.evidence: README.md:195-196 vs cli/main.py:3549-3580 hardcoded orders and 'legacy' labels at 3741-3763

findings.title: integrations doctor reports MCP/Composio liveness as permanent 'not_run' placeholders
findings.whats_missing: build_integration_capability_audit hardcodes 'live_tool_check': 'not_run' (612) and 'active_account_check': 'not_run' (618) — the audit reports configured server/toolkit names and env presence but never actually probes whether the Docker MCP profile or Composio account works. These fields are effectively dead placeholders that always say not_run, giving false reassurance that something might later fill them.
findings.end_goal: Either implement an opt-in live probe (e.g. --probe that pings the configured MCP gateway / Composio account and records pass/fail), or remove the misleading not_run keys so the packet does not imply an unfinished check.
findings.evidence: cli/main.py:612 and 618 ('not_run' literals never updated)

findings.title: CLI has no --version flag and no main() entrypoint wrapper
findings.whats_missing: The root app (305-310) defines no --version callback, so operators cannot confirm which build is running in an overnight box (important given the dirty WIP tree). The module ends with `if __name__ == '__main__': app()` (10920-10921) and there is no main() function, so console_scripts entrypoints and tests must call app() directly; there is also no top-level exception boundary to redact/clean unexpected errors (only 3 ad-hoc uses of _compact_cli_error_reason).
findings.end_goal: Root app gains an eager --version callback printing package version + short git sha; a main() wrapper is the console-script entrypoint and installs a top-level handler that renders unexpected exceptions via _compact_cli_error_reason and returns a clean non-zero exit instead of a raw traceback.
findings.evidence: cli/main.py:305-310 (Typer app, no version_option/callback); 10920-10921 (bare app() call, no main()); _compact_cli_error_reason used only at 4601/6807/8943

findings.title: Thin one-line wrapper functions duplicate imported compact-payload helpers
findings.whats_missing: Several module-level helpers exist only to forward to an imported function with the same name, e.g. _compact_overnight_plan_payload (6855), _compact_premarket_brief_payload (6859), _compact_hourly_supervisor_payload (6863), _write_supervisor_daily_report_packet (6867), _compact_supervisor_daily_report_payload (6871) just call the imported compact_*/write_* functions. These indirection shims add noise, obscure call sites, and invite drift between the wrapper and the real implementation.
findings.end_goal: Call the imported functions directly at use sites (or import-alias them) and delete the pass-through wrappers; if a wrapper exists only to bind a default path, document that default explicitly.
findings.evidence: cli/main.py:6855-6873 (five one-line forwarding wrappers around imported helpers)

findings.title: OpenRouter model picker fetches full model list every run and silently shows only first 5 unsorted
findings.whats_missing: _fetch_openrouter_models (167-177) hits the network on every provider selection with a 10s timeout and no cache; select_openrouter_model (180-204) then shows models[:5] — the first five in API order, not the newest or most relevant, despite the prompt text claiming 'latest available' (181, 188). The 'newest/latest' claim is unsubstantiated and the slice may hide the model the user wants.
findings.end_goal: Model list is cached briefly (e.g. per-process / short TTL), sorted by a meaningful key (created date) so 'latest' is accurate, and the picker supports search/more-than-5 or always offers custom ID; prompt text matches actual ordering.
findings.evidence: cli/utils.py:167-204 (no cache, models[:5], 'latest available' label)

findings.title: StatsCallbackHandler increments llm_calls in both on_llm_start and on_chat_model_start
findings.whats_missing: Both on_llm_start (81-90) and on_chat_model_start (92-101) increment self.llm_calls and re-check the per-run budget. For chat models, LangChain fires on_chat_model_start; for completion LLMs, on_llm_start. A provider/integration that emits both callbacks for one invocation would double-count calls and could trip TRADINGAGENTS_MODEL_MAX_CALLS_PER_RUN at half the real count. There is no de-duplication by run_id/parent_run_id.
findings.end_goal: Call counting is keyed so a single model invocation increments exactly once regardless of which start callback fires (e.g. track run_id seen-set, or only count one of the two), with a unit test asserting one logical call == one increment across both callback shapes.
findings.evidence: cli/stats_handler.py:81-101 (both start callbacks do self.llm_calls += 1)

findings.title: Magic numbers and string literals scattered through CLI (client_order_id [:48], list limits, polling waits)
findings.whats_missing: Unnamed magic values appear in load-bearing spots: client_order_id truncation [:48] (10516), default supervisor packet limit=12 (_latest_supervisor_packets 3860), max_recent_fills=25 default (8327), volume window=20 (3916), terminate wait_seconds=5 (4374), _compact_cli_error_reason max_chars=320/80-char tool-arg limits. The 48-char Alpaca client_order_id cap in particular is a broker constraint encoded as a bare slice with no named constant or comment, risking silent ID collisions if the format changes.
findings.end_goal: Broker/format constraints (ALPACA_CLIENT_ORDER_ID_MAX_LEN=48, default packet history depth, polling timeouts) become named module constants with comments citing the source constraint; collision risk on truncated client_order_ids is covered by a test.
findings.evidence: cli/main.py:10516 ([:48] on client_order_id); 3860 (limit=12); 8327 (max_recent_fills 25); 4374 (wait_seconds 5)

findings.title: Broad `except Exception` blocks swallow errors without logging in several helpers
findings.whats_missing: Multiple helpers catch Exception and silently fall back without recording why: _account_circuit_breaker_values returns (None, None) on any parse error (476-477) — meaning a malformed account payload silently disables the daily-loss / drawdown circuit breaker inputs with no trace; _dynamic_live_cap_for_budget_mode buying_power parse falls back to 0 (446-447); paper-tournament run swallows the list_orders('all') failure (8996). On a money-movement path, silently neutering a circuit-breaker input is a safety-observability gap.
findings.end_goal: These except blocks log a structured warning (and surface into the packet evidence) so an operator/automation can see that a circuit-breaker input could not be computed; the supervisor packet records 'circuit_breaker_inputs_unavailable' rather than silently passing None.
findings.evidence: cli/main.py:476-477 (_account_circuit_breaker_values returns None,None on except); 446-447; 8996

findings.title: _default_run_id uses second-resolution timestamp evaluated at import time as a Typer default
findings.whats_missing: alpaca preview/submit and crawl-target use run_id default = _default_run_id() (8388, 8427, 771), but Typer evaluates option defaults at function-definition (import) time, so the default run_id is frozen to the timestamp when the module was imported, not when the command runs — every invocation in a long-lived process/REPL/test session reuses the same run_id. Run ids are also only second-resolution, so two runs in the same second collide. Collisions can cause idempotency/packet-naming clashes.
findings.end_goal: run_id defaults to None and is filled in at command execution with a fresh, collision-resistant id (timestamp + short random/uuid suffix), so each invocation gets a unique id regardless of import time.
findings.evidence: cli/main.py:485-486 (_default_run_id second-resolution); used as Option default at 8388, 8427, 771 (evaluated at import)

findings.title: Live submit path performs a synchronous yfinance network ranking with no timeout to pick a third order
findings.whats_missing: When --third-symbol/--third-limit-price are omitted, _ticket_orders calls _rank_third_candidate (3527-3540) which loops mega-cap symbols doing yf.Ticker(sym).history() inside the submit/preview path. yfinance is unauthenticated, rate-limited, and has no timeout here; a slow/blocked call stalls the order command, and on failure it raises typer.BadParameter aborting the whole submit even though the two primary orders are fully specified. Network-derived limit prices entering a live order path without freshness/sanity bounds is a money-safety concern.
findings.end_goal: Third-candidate selection is removed from the submit path entirely (orders come from a validated plan), or the third order is omitted (not the whole command aborted) when no symbol/price is supplied; any market-data fetch in an order path has an explicit timeout and price-sanity bounds.
findings.evidence: cli/main.py:3567-3569 (auto-rank when omitted) -> 3527-3540 (yfinance loop, no timeout, raises BadParameter)

findings.title: n8n native-evaluation lane still requires the editor UI; CLI only syncs the dataset and probes
findings.whats_missing: research n8n-sync-evaluation-table (2568) and n8n-evaluation-run-probe (2719) push the evaluation dataset and probe a built-in run, but per the stated weak area the native-eval still requires manually wiring evaluation nodes in the n8n editor UI. There is no CLI command that programmatically creates/attaches the native evaluation trigger/nodes to a workflow, so the 'self-checking via n8n' loop cannot be stood up headlessly.
findings.end_goal: A CLI command (e.g. research n8n-sync-evaluation-workflow) creates or patches the evaluation-enabled workflow (trigger + evaluation nodes referencing the synced Data Table) through the public API so the native-eval loop is reproducible from source control without the editor UI.
findings.evidence: cli/main.py:2568-2647 (sync table) and 2719+ (run probe) — no command that builds the evaluation node graph; task brief notes 'n8n native-eval still requires the editor UI'

findings.title: agent-ledger commands surface 0-resolved silently despite 4582 unresolved forecasts being a known blocker
findings.whats_missing: agent-ledger-resolve (1418) and agent-ledger-update (1463) compute newly_resolved_count and resolved_count but, on the human path, only print plain counts (1458-1460, 1575-1578). Given the stated state of 4582 forecasts / 0 resolved, the CLI gives no signal that resolution is failing (e.g. price_lookup returning nothing, all forecasts not yet mature). An operator running resolve sees 'Newly resolved: 0' with no diagnosis of why nothing resolved.
findings.end_goal: Resolve/update commands emit a resolution-health summary: how many forecasts are due-but-unresolved, how many failed price lookup, and the most common skip reason, so a human or automation can see whether the 0-resolved state is 'not yet mature' vs 'price lookup broken' and act.
findings.evidence: cli/main.py:1442-1460 (resolve prints only counts); 1530-1578 (update prints only counts); no per-skip-reason breakdown

findings.title: Result output directories are inconsistent string literals duplicated across dozens of commands
findings.whats_missing: Path('results/...') defaults are hardcoded inline across many commands with overlapping but inconsistent naming (results/hourly_supervisor, results/overnight_plans, results/premarket_briefs, results/research_evidence, results/n8n_evaluations, results/token_efficiency, results/agent_intelligence, results/policy/...). The same conceptual directory is repeated as a literal in every command that touches it, so a relocation requires editing dozens of sites and typos can silently split outputs across near-identical paths.
findings.end_goal: A single results-layout module/dataclass defines canonical output directories; commands reference RESULTS.hourly_supervisor etc. A test asserts no two commands disagree on a directory's name.
findings.evidence: cli/main.py: repeated Path('results/...') literals e.g. 8329, 8333, 10219-10253, 9135, 9605, 10863; same dirs re-typed per command

findings.title: setup_n8n.py ships a hardcoded n8n owner password
findings.whats_missing: OWNER_PASSWORD = "TradingAgents123!" and OWNER_EMAIL are hardcoded constants and printed to stdout (setup_n8n.py:13-14, 142-144); anyone with the repo gets working credentials and they are committed in plaintext.
findings.end_goal: Credentials are read from env vars / a prompted secret (e.g. N8N_OWNER_PASSWORD) with no default, never echoed to stdout, and the README documents the secret source; no usable password exists in source control.

findings.title: Three workflow generators disagree on jobs and only one is canonical
findings.whats_missing: n8n/generate-workflows.mjs (the source of the committed n8n/workflows/*.json) lists overnight planner jobs as [...,agent_ledger_update, agent_ledger_summary] and a Health+Self-Heal workflow [automation_health_audit, self_heal_plan], while generate_n8n_workflows.py and import_n8n_workflows.py use a different, older job set (e.g. overnight uses agent_ledger_summary only, a 'status dashboard/health check' workflow with process_review). The two Python generators write to /tmp (POSIX) and use typeVersion 4.1 with no timeout, diverging from the .mjs canonical (4.2, 120000ms timeout).
