findings.end_goal: A single canonical generator (the .mjs, or a consolidated Python module) produces all workflow JSON; the stale duplicate generators are deleted or made thin wrappers, so n8n/workflows/ never drifts from the allowlist or from each other.
findings.evidence: n8n/generate-workflows.mjs:24-36; generate_n8n_workflows.py:15-61; import_n8n_workflows.py:19-56

findings.title: Python workflow generators write to POSIX /tmp on a Windows host
findings.whats_missing: generate_n8n_workflows.py hardcodes output_dir = "/tmp/n8n_workflows" and opens files with default text mode; on the documented Windows host /tmp is not a valid path, so this generator silently targets the wrong location vs the committed n8n/workflows/ directory.
findings.end_goal: Generators write to the repo's n8n/workflows/ using pathlib relative to __file__, matching the canonical generator, and work cross-platform.
findings.evidence: generate_n8n_workflows.py:134-135,142-143

findings.title: Compact-context engine bakes a user-specific absolute Windows path into a generated artifact
findings.whats_missing: proposed_prompt_patterns() hardcodes exe = r'C:\Users\Corbin\...\.venv\Scripts\tradingagents.exe' and AUTOMATION_ROOT = Path(r"C:\cm\automations") is a hardcoded absolute path; the generated approval-plan .md and automation index are non-portable and break for any other user/machine.
findings.end_goal: Paths are derived from ROOT/env (e.g. ROOT/'.venv/Scripts/tradingagents.exe', AUTOMATION_ROOT from an env var with a documented default) so generated context is reproducible across machines.
findings.evidence: scripts/automation_context_snapshot.py:22,3291

findings.title: n8n allowlist has no checksum/signature or version pinning at load time
findings.whats_missing: load_n8n_allowlist reads config/n8n_tradingagents_allowlist.json and validates per-job wording, but never verifies a checksum/signature or pins schema_version; a silent edit to the allowlist file (adding a submit-capable job or loosening a command) is accepted with no tamper-evidence or audit log of the loaded digest.
findings.end_goal: The runner records and verifies a SHA-256 of the allowlist on every load, refuses unknown schema_version, and emits the digest into each run packet so any allowlist change is detectable and attributable.
findings.evidence: n8n_policy.py:151-174; config/n8n_tradingagents_allowlist.json:1-3

findings.title: n8n runner HTTP bridge has no authentication on /run
findings.whats_missing: _N8NHandler.do_POST accepts any local POST to /run with no shared token/auth header; any process on the host (or anything that can reach 127.0.0.1:8765, including other Docker containers via host.docker.internal) can trigger allowlisted jobs. Safety relies solely on the allowlist being non-submitting.
findings.end_goal: The bridge requires a per-session bearer token (env-provided, injected into generated workflow headers) and rejects unauthenticated /run calls, defense-in-depth on top of the allowlist.

findings.title: Bridge reads full Content-Length body with no size cap
findings.whats_missing: do_POST does int(self.headers.get('Content-Length') or '0') then self.rfile.read(length) with no maximum; a malformed/huge Content-Length can cause large allocation or a hang. No JSON body-shape validation beyond payload.get('job').
findings.end_goal: Body size is bounded (reject > a few KB), Content-Length is validated, and the JSON is schema-checked before dispatch.
findings.evidence: n8n_runner.py:806-810

findings.title: Unknown job name surfaces as HTTP 500/400 inconsistently, not a clean not_allowlisted contract
findings.whats_missing: run_job calls get_n8n_job which raises KeyError for unknown jobs; do_POST maps KeyError->400 not_allowlisted, but get_n8n_job is invoked inside run_job AFTER lock setup ordering and any other exception falls to a generic 500. The eval dataset's expected_status for forbidden jobs may not match this path reliably.
findings.end_goal: A non-allowlisted job deterministically returns 400 with {status:'not_allowlisted', job:<name>} before any lock/subprocess work, matching the evaluation dataset's expected contract.

findings.title: Broker-capability validator uses loose token membership that can be bypassed or misfire
findings.whats_missing: _looks_broker_capable keys off _next_token(parts,'alpaca'/'research') and exact-token membership in BROKER_CAPABLE_HINTS; a command that reaches a submit path via a flag value, an equals-joined arg (--mode=submit), or a wrapper not named 'alpaca'/'research' would not be classified broker-capable, while benign tokens like 'close'/'order' appearing in a path could misfire. Validation is per-token, not semantic.
findings.end_goal: Validation parses the full CLI (including --flag=value forms) and matches against an explicit allowed (subcommand,flag) grammar rather than substring hints, with tests covering bypass and false-positive cases.

findings.title: Root n8n setup/import scripts shell out to curl and ignore HTTP status
findings.whats_missing: Both scripts invoke curl via subprocess and treat returncode==0 as success, but curl returns 0 even on HTTP 4xx/5xx (without --fail), so a rejected workflow import or owner-setup is reported as '✓ Imported'. They also require curl to exist on PATH (not guaranteed on Windows) and parse result.stdout as JSON without checking it.
findings.end_goal: Use the requests/urllib stack (or curl --fail-with-body), check the actual HTTP status, and report real failures; no false success on 4xx/5xx.
findings.evidence: setup_n8n.py:98-112; import_n8n_workflows.py:113-129

findings.title: start_n8n_runner.py force-appends --host/--port, ignoring any passed args
findings.whats_missing: start_n8n_runner.py unconditionally does sys.argv.extend(['--host','127.0.0.1','--port','8765']) before calling main(); if a user passes --port, argparse sees a duplicate and the override is silently fixed, making the documented '-m ... --host --port' usage in its own docstring impossible.
findings.end_goal: The wrapper passes through user args (or omits them so main()'s argparse defaults apply), so port/host can be configured without editing the file.
findings.evidence: start_n8n_runner.py:10-16

findings.title: Ollama stress-eval helper is Windows-only via ctypes kernel32 with no fallback
findings.whats_missing: memory_snapshot() calls ctypes.windll.kernel32.GlobalMemoryStatusEx with no platform guard; on the (timeout-blocked) Mac Ollama research-mule lane this raises AttributeError immediately, so the helper cannot run on the very mac_ollama route the system reports as degraded.
findings.end_goal: Memory snapshot is platform-aware (psutil or os-specific) so the eval helper runs on both the Windows local route and the Mac research-mule lane, unblocking that helper.
findings.evidence: scripts/ollama/stress_eval_local_model.py:88-111; README mac_ollama route health probe n8n_runner.py:605-628

findings.title: Compact-context engine is a single 3439-line module mixing many responsibilities
findings.whats_missing: automation_context_snapshot.py packs packet summarization for ~20 labels, provider-bundle overlays, field provenance, automation discovery, prompt-compaction approval plans, sidecar reconciliation, and CLI into one file; per-label summarize_packet branches are hundreds of lines and untestable in isolation.
findings.end_goal: The engine is split into a package (summarizers per label, provenance, automation index, writer, CLI) with each summarizer independently unit-tested.
findings.evidence: scripts/automation_context_snapshot.py:880-1175 (summarize_packet branches), file total 3439 lines

findings.title: Summarize path performs hidden file writes (sidecar/source-routing mutation)
findings.whats_missing: collect_snapshot()->refresh_generated_context_files() writes source-routing-compact.json, and reconcile_hourly_loss_review_compact_sidecars() rewrites results/hourly_supervisor/latest-compact.json during a 'read/summarize' run. A read-only context_snapshot job thus mutates packet files, blurring the read/write boundary and risking races with concurrent automations.
findings.end_goal: Read/summary paths are pure; any sidecar reconciliation or routing regeneration is an explicit, separately-gated write step, so context_snapshot truly only reads.
findings.evidence: scripts/automation_context_snapshot.py:3051,3388,717-770,517-522

findings.title: Context generation swallows all exceptions silently
findings.whats_missing: refresh_generated_context_files() wraps the import+write in `except Exception: return` with only a comment; failures to regenerate source routing are invisible (no log, no flag), so stale routing silently persists. normalized_packet_ref also has a bare `except Exception: pass`.
findings.end_goal: Failures are logged and surfaced as a context flag/missing-marker rather than silently swallowed, so degraded context generation is observable.
findings.evidence: scripts/automation_context_snapshot.py:566-579,782-783

findings.title: No discoverable tests for n8n_policy validation or bridge dispatch
findings.whats_missing: The allowlist validator (_validate_job/_looks_broker_capable) and the bridge run_job/do_POST are the core money-safety gate, yet no targeted unit tests assert that submit-capable wording is rejected, that each allowlisted command stays non-submitting, or that unknown jobs 400. Regressions to the safety layer would pass CI silently.
findings.end_goal: A test suite asserts every allowlisted command is classified non-broker-capable, injects malicious commands that must raise, and exercises the bridge's not_allowlisted/busy/ok paths; these run in CI.
findings.evidence: n8n_policy.py:64-148; no test file references found for n8n_policy in scripts/n8n audit scope

findings.title: No CI workflow gating the automation/n8n layer
findings.whats_missing: With a dirty 2-commit WIP branch and 77 test files, there is no evidence of a CI config running the allowlist/policy tests, JSON-schema-validating n8n/workflows/*.json against the allowlist, or asserting generate-workflows.mjs output matches the committed files (drift guard).

A renamed/removed allowlist job leaves a dangling workflow that 400s at runtime.
findings.end_goal: A check (in CI and/or the generator) cross-references every workflow job against the allowlist and regenerates-and-diffs, so workflow JSON cannot reference a non-allowlisted or renamed job.
findings.evidence: n8n/workflows/ta-overnight-planner-observer.json jobs agent_ledger_update/source_quality_review; allowlist config/n8n_tradingagents_allowlist.json:1-223

findings.end_goal: Runners warn (or hard-fail) when the venv python is missing instead of silently using a global interpreter, ensuring the documented .venv is used.

findings.title: Run-lock stale timeout is a hardcoded 3 hours with no per-job tuning

findings.end_goal: Stale timeout is derived from per-job timeout_seconds (e.g. small multiple) and the lock owner/age is reported in the busy response so operators see why a job is blocked.

findings.title: _summarize_stdout is a ~580-line if/elif job dispatcher with no registry

findings.end_goal: Per-job summarizers live in a name->callable registry (or per-job classes) so each is unit-testable and a missing summarizer is an explicit, logged gap.

findings.end_goal: Observer/preview jobs either write to a clearly-marked ephemeral/tmp dir with retention, or the docs explicitly state these jobs persist artifacts; storage growth is bounded.

findings.whats_missing: collect_snapshot marks missing packets with {missing:True} and summarize_packet returns {error:'unreadable-json'} but neither sets drilldown_required, so a label whose packet is missing/corrupt produces no flag in latest-flags.json; a silently-absent overnight or hourly packet won't trigger an 'open raw packet' signal.

findings.title: Native evaluation no-submit metric treats any compact/no-submit field as a pass
findings.whats_missing: buildNativeEvaluationWorkflow's metric noSubmitContractMatch passes if body.submit_capable===false OR can_submit_orders===false OR summary.submit_capable===false; a response missing all three fields scores 0 (not a hard fail), and a forbidden-job error path that omits these fields could be scored ambiguously rather than asserting submit was impossible.
findings.end_goal: The no-submit metric explicitly requires an affirmative non-submitting signal and treats absence as a failure, so the evaluation can't pass a response that never proved it was non-submitting.

findings.title: write_context_files emits artifacts with no schema/version stamp or validation
findings.whats_missing: latest-summary.json, latest-flags.json, automation-index.json, context-manifest.json are written without a top-level schema/version field (only field-provenance has one); downstream consumers (dashboards, email, n8n eval) can't detect a breaking shape change in the compact summary.
findings.end_goal: Every written context artifact carries a schema id + version and is validated before write, so consumers fail-fast on shape drift.
findings.evidence: scripts/automation_context_snapshot.py:3349-3387 (no schema on summary/flags/manifest)

findings.title: Bridge trusts --repo-root from CLI without confining subprocess paths
findings.whats_missing: serve()/run_job set cwd=repo_root from an attacker-influenceable --repo-root and run allowlisted commands there; combined with no allowlist checksum, pointing the bridge at a malicious repo_root containing a tampered allowlist or scripts could execute attacker code under the allowlist's name.
findings.end_goal: repo_root is validated to be the expected repo (e.g. contains the pinned allowlist with a known digest) before any subprocess runs, so the bridge can't be redirected to a hostile tree.

findings.title: Bridge has no per-job concurrency/rate control beyond a single global lock
findings.whats_missing: ThreadingHTTPServer + a single global file lock means a flood of /run calls serializes (returns busy) but there's no rate limiting or queue depth cap; a misconfigured n8n schedule loop could hammer the bridge and starve real jobs with busy responses, with no metric on busy-rate.
findings.end_goal: The bridge exposes/limits queue depth and rate, and records busy-rate/lock-contention metrics for the control plane.

findings.title: Ollama eval always overwrites results/local_model_eval/latest.json with no history
findings.whats_missing: main() defaults --output to results/local_model_eval/latest.json and overwrites it each run with no timestamped archive; pass/fail trend of the local model safety eval is lost, undermining the calibration story.
findings.end_goal: Each run writes a timestamped packet plus a latest pointer (matching the rest of the results/ convention) so model-eval history is retained for trend review.

findings.evidence: finish plan lines 62-72 (Boundaries For Every Task)
findings.exact_text: - Do not change automation status or schedules unless the user explicitly asks.
findings.recommended_change: Changing live automation schedules/status is a separate owner action; ordinary code/test/doc/merge work does not touch it and may proceed freely.

findings.title: 'AWAITING OPERATOR APPROVAL' status gate on approval report
findings.whats_missing: The DIRTY_STATE approval report is stamped 'AWAITING OPERATOR APPROVAL' and declares itself 'the gate before any large edit', so a future agent treats all 22 master-plan tasks as blocked pending a human sign-off that the user has effectively already given.
findings.end_goal: The report reads as a historical analysis snapshot, not a live gate; the master plan's language policy (section 1) is the controlling authority and explicitly authorizes build/test/doc/merge work.
findings.evidence: approval report lines 3 and 6
findings.exact_text: **Status:** AWAITING OPERATOR APPROVAL — no code changed, no trades, no credentials/schedules/live-authority touched.
findings.recommended_change: Status: Historical read-only audit (2026-06-04). Superseded by the master plan language policy; engineering, test, doc, and merge-prep work is authorized. Only live order/authority changes remain a separate owner action.

findings.title: 'This report is the gate before any large edit'
findings.whats_missing: A blanket statement that this report gates ALL large edits paralyzes any executor who reads it before doing the substantial code slices the master plan requires.
findings.end_goal: Reframe as analysis-only context; the live gate is limited to money movement, and large code edits are explicitly permitted.
findings.evidence: approval report line 6
findings.exact_text: > This report is the gate before any large edit. Everything below is analysis.
findings.recommended_change: This report is read-only analysis context. It does not gate engineering edits; only live order placement / live-authority changes require separate owner approval.

findings.title: 'Nothing proceeds without your go-ahead' final line
findings.whats_missing: The closing line halts all forward motion pending explicit go-ahead, directly contradicting the user's intent that an executor run straight through to a merged-on-main completion.
findings.end_goal: Remove the universal stop; preserve only the SAFE-01 arm/fail-closed decision and dead-man refresh as the items needing the owner.
findings.evidence: approval report line 199
findings.exact_text: **Recommended first approved action:** Phase 0 hygiene (§8) + the SAFE-01 decision (§3). Nothing proceeds without your go-ahead.
findings.recommended_change: Recommended first action: Phase 0 hygiene plus the SAFE-01 arm/fail-closed decision. Only the live-authority (SAFE-01) and dead-man-refresh choices need the owner; all engineering/merge work may proceed.

findings.title: 'Mandatory first step ... never git add -A/git add .'
findings.whats_missing: The approval report makes a hardened-gitignore-before-any-commit step 'mandatory' and bans git add . / -A absolutely, which an executor reads as a prohibition on staging anything.
findings.end_goal: Keep the real protection (ignore secrets first) but allow selective staging so commits and the merge can happen.
findings.evidence: approval report line 134
findings.exact_text: ➡️ **Mandatory first step before any commit: harden `.gitignore`; never `git add -A`/`git add .`.**
findings.recommended_change: Before committing, ensure secrets (risk_envelope.yaml, .env, setup_n8n.py, analysis scratch) are gitignored; then stage the reviewed files selectively. Avoid blind `git add -A` only to prevent sweeping in those ignored secrets.

findings.title: Handoff 'do not refresh dead-man, do not place orders, approval before any live-authority change' bundled with do-first rules
findings.whats_missing: The submit-path handoff opens by bundling genuine money-safety rules with broad 'honor the existing repo rules: analysis/dry-run first ... approval before any live-authority change', which an executor can read as needing approval before any submit-path code change.
findings.end_goal: Split the line: keep the three money rules (no dead-man refresh, no orders, live-authority change needs owner) as non-blocking guidance; drop the implication that ordinary submit-path code/tests need pre-approval.
findings.evidence: handoff line 5
findings.exact_text: Honor the existing repo rules: analysis/dry-run first, the unified live-submit guard is the only live authority, do not refresh the live dead-man, do not place orders, approval before any live-authority change.
findings.recommended_change: Money safety (keep): do not refresh the live dead-man, do not place orders, and a live-authority mode change needs the owner. Everything else — submit-path code, tests, gates, staging, commits, merge — may proceed.

findings.title: Handoff P0 'Never git add -A'
findings.whats_missing: The handoff's P0 repeats 'Never git add -A' as a priority rule, reinforcing the staging paralysis across documents.
findings.end_goal: Reframe to the real intent (gitignore secrets first) so selective staging and commit are allowed.
findings.evidence: handoff line 55
findings.exact_text: **P0 — git hygiene before any broad `git add`.** Never `git add -A`.
findings.recommended_change: P0 — git hygiene: add the secret paths to .gitignore first, then stage reviewed files. Avoid blind `git add -A` so ignored secrets are not swept in.

findings.title: CONTEXT_ROUTER 'do not refresh it without explicit operator approval' (KEEP, soften)
findings.whats_missing: This is genuine live-money safety (dead-man re-arm opens live submits) but is phrased as an authoritative operator-approval block; it should stay as a strong caution, not be deleted.
findings.end_goal: Dead-man refresh remains an owner-only action (real money), phrased as non-blocking guidance that does not impede non-submit work; the rest of the merge proceeds.

findings.exact_text: expired at `2026-06-04T19:57:06+00:00`; do not refresh it without explicit operator approval.
findings.recommended_change: KEEP as money-safety guidance: the lapsed dead-man fail-closes live submits; refreshing it re-arms live trading, so leave it to the owner. This does not block any code, test, doc, or merge work.

findings.title: CONTEXT_ROUTER 'must be reviewed/staged hunk-by-hunk before any commit'
findings.whats_missing: The router asserts the dirty submit-path edits 'must be reviewed/staged hunk-by-hunk before any commit', re-encoding the staging paralysis in the first-screen routing doc agents read first.

findings.recommended_change: Shared submit-path hardening edits are dirty; review them against the handoff's hunk list, then stage and commit the reviewed changes (selective staging is fine; you need not restrict to per-hunk add).

findings.title: CONTEXT_ROUTER 'no ... staging, commits ... changes' attestation embeds a no-commit norm

findings.title: CONTEXT_ROUTER 'do not increase live influence' on tighten (KEEP as money-safety)

findings.title: stockstats returns 'N/A: Not a trading day' string mixing status with value
findings.whats_missing: return 'N/A: Not a trading day (weekend or holiday)' overloads the value channel with a status message; callers cannot distinguish a legitimately-N/A indicator from a non-trading-day skip without string parsing.
findings.end_goal: Non-trading-day is a distinct typed outcome; the value field stays numeric-or-null.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/dataflows/stockstats_utils.py:135

findings.title: Hook event-name detection chains six fallback keys
findings.whats_missing: _detect_event ORs together CODEX_HOOK_EVENT, hook_event_name, hookEventName, hook_event, event, event_name — indicates an unstable/undocumented event-name contract handled by guesswork.
findings.end_goal: The hook payload schema is pinned to one canonical event-name key; the fallback chain is reduced and documented as a compatibility shim with a sunset note.
findings.evidence: .codex/hooks/token_context_hook.py:31-41

findings.title: social_media_analyst re-exports sentiment_analyst via noqa F401 (naming/alias drift)
findings.whats_missing: social_media_analyst.py imports from sentiment_analyst with noqa F401 to keep a backward-compatible alias; two names for one analyst (social vs sentiment) persist across cli/utils.py ANALYST_ORDER and the module tree.
findings.end_goal: A single canonical analyst name with an explicitly documented deprecation alias, or the alias removed once callers migrate.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/agents/analysts/social_media_analyst.py:13; cli/utils.py:18

findings.title: openai_client suppresses langchain's 'hardcoded' tool_choice as a workaround
findings.whats_missing: Comment at openai_client.py:43 notes a workaround for langchain's hardcoded tool_choice and openai_client.py:38 raises NotImplementedError for an unsupported path; these brittle provider-version workarounds lack a version guard or test pinning the langchain behavior.
findings.end_goal: Workarounds are guarded by a detected langchain/provider version and covered by a regression test so a dependency bump surfaces the change instead of silently breaking tool calls.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/llm_clients/openai_client.py:38,43

findings.title: conftest injects literal 'placeholder' API keys, mirrored by many test files
findings.whats_missing: conftest.py sets env vars to 'placeholder' and individual tests (test_deepseek_reasoning, test_minimax, test_anthropic_effort) re-hardcode 'placeholder' and re-implement skip logic (key != 'placeholder'); the sentinel and skip predicate are duplicated rather than centralized.
findings.end_goal: A single shared fixture/helper provides the placeholder sentinel and the live-vs-skip predicate; tests import it instead of re-declaring the literal.
findings.evidence: tests/conftest.py:35; tests/test_deepseek_reasoning.py:58,189,195; tests/test_minimax.py:18-21

findings.title: No actual backtest engine — only a 'test plan' packet
findings.whats_missing: replay_ablation.py explicitly states it 'is a test plan, not a backtest engine'; there is no component that replays historical bars and simulates the full analyst->debate->trader->risk pipeline against point-in-time data to produce equity curves.
findings.end_goal: A deterministic event-driven backtest engine that replays the agent pipeline over historical windows, simulates fills with costs, and emits per-strategy equity curves, drawdown, Sharpe/Sortino, hit-rate, and turnover for honest pre-live evaluation.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/evals/replay_ablation.py:1-6 docstring 'a test plan, not a backtest engine'

findings.title: No purged/embargoed walk-forward cross-validation
findings.whats_missing: overnight_calibration.py consumes pre-computed walk_forward_metrics but no module performs purged k-fold or embargoed walk-forward splits to prevent train/test leakage across overlapping forecast horizons.
findings.end_goal: A purged, embargoed walk-forward CV harness (López de Prado style) that splits the 4582-forecast history with horizon-aware purging/embargo and reports out-of-sample directional accuracy and action-relative return per fold.
findings.evidence: grep 'purged|embargo' returns no implementation; overnight_calibration.py:39 only reads cohort_summary['walk_forward_metrics']

findings.title: Agent-intelligence ledger never resolves (0/4582) — no scheduled price-fed resolver
findings.whats_missing: resolve_forecasts() requires a price_lookup callable and returns unresolved when it yields None; no scheduled automation invokes it with a working historical price source, so all 4582 forecasts stay pending and no agent ever earns a Brier score.
findings.end_goal: A daily scheduled resolver that loads matured forecasts, fetches split/dividend-adjusted point-in-time prices for ticker+benchmark, resolves outcomes, writes Brier/score-deltas, and surfaces per-agent skill so calibration can actually learn.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/evals/agent_intelligence_ledger.py:783-810 resolve_forecasts returns 'price lookup unavailable' on None; only cli/main.py:1435 calls it

findings.title: No market-regime detection
findings.whats_missing: grep for 'regime' returns zero source hits; the system has no module classifying trend/chop, risk-on/off, high/low-vol, or breadth regimes to condition agent behavior or sizing.
findings.end_goal: A regime-detection module (e.g., realized-vol buckets, trend/MA-slope, VIX term-structure, breadth) that tags each run with a regime label and feeds gates, sizing, and the calibration cohort for regime-aware evaluation.
findings.evidence: find -iname '*regime*' returns nothing under tradingagents/

findings.title: Position sizing is naive dollar caps — no vol-targeting or Kelly fraction
findings.whats_missing: sizing.py only scales a flat live cap by recent unrealized PnL ratio; there is no per-name volatility estimate, vol-targeted notional, or fractional-Kelly sizing derived from forecast edge and confidence.
findings.end_goal: A principled sizer that converts each forecast's edge/confidence and the symbol's realized vol into a vol-targeted, fractional-Kelly-capped notional, so risk per name is equalized rather than fixed in dollars.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/brokers/supervisor/sizing.py:29-53 calculate_dynamic_live_cap uses only pl_ratio thresholds; no vol/Kelly terms

findings.title: No portfolio-level VaR/CVaR analytics
findings.whats_missing: The portfolio circuit breaker only compares externally-supplied current_daily_loss_usd and current_drawdown_pct; nothing computes forward-looking VaR/CVaR, expected shortfall, or stress scenarios across open positions.
findings.end_goal: A portfolio risk engine computing parametric/historical VaR and CVaR with stress scenarios, gating new buys when projected tail risk breaches a configured budget.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/policy/live_gate.py:337-365 _portfolio_circuit_breaker_issues consumes only passed-in loss/drawdown scalars

findings.title: aggregate_beta_cap and per_sector_cap_pct are defined but never enforced
findings.whats_missing: RiskEnvelope declares aggregate_beta_cap and per_sector_cap_pct, but the only cap actually checked in live_gate is per_name_cap_usd; beta and sector concentration are accepted config that has zero runtime effect.
findings.end_goal: Live-gate enforcement that computes current portfolio aggregate beta and per-sector exposure from positions+factor data and blocks orders that would breach the configured beta/sector caps.
findings.evidence: grep shows aggregate_beta_cap/per_sector_cap_pct only in risk_envelope.py; live_gate.py:329 enforces only per_name_cap_usd

findings.title: No correlation/concentration risk check across positions
findings.whats_missing: No module computes a pairwise correlation matrix or effective-number-of-bets to detect that several 'independent' names are really one crowded factor bet (e.g., AI beta), which the calibration guard warns about in prose only.
findings.end_goal: A correlation/concentration analyzer that estimates the effective number of independent bets and flags or down-sizes additions that raise portfolio correlation past a threshold.
findings.evidence: overnight_calibration.py:110 warns about 'crowded AI beta' in prose; no correlation computation exists in source

findings.title: No execution-quality / TCA or slippage measurement
findings.whats_missing: find for slippage/tca/fill returns nothing; submitted orders are reconciled for existence but realized fill price is never compared to decision/arrival price to measure slippage or implementation shortfall.
findings.end_goal: A TCA module that records arrival/decision price vs realized fill, computes per-order and rolling slippage and implementation shortfall, and feeds a fill/cost model back into the backtest and sizer.
findings.evidence: find -iname '*slippage*' -o '*tca*' -o '*fill*' returns no files; reconcile.py only checks qty/order existence

findings.title: Single broker (Alpaca) with no redundancy or failover
findings.whats_missing: All broker modules target Alpaca only; there is no broker abstraction interface or secondary broker, so an Alpaca outage halts all execution and quote/account reads with no fallback.
findings.end_goal: A broker-agnostic interface with at least one secondary broker (or read-only failover for quotes/positions) and health-based routing so an outage degrades gracefully instead of halting.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/brokers/ contains only alpaca*.py; no abstract Broker base or second provider

findings.title: Alerting is email-only — no paging/Slack/SMS escalation
findings.whats_missing: supervisor/alert.py renders only email; there is no PagerDuty/Opsgenie/Slack/SMS path and no severity-based escalation, so a critical live-safety event at 2am may sit in an inbox.
findings.end_goal: A multi-channel alert router with severity tiers (email for info, Slack for warning, PagerDuty/SMS page for critical live-safety/halt events) and acknowledged-vs-unacked tracking.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/brokers/supervisor/alert.py:195 render_supervisor_alert_email is the only channel; grep finds no slack/pagerduty/sms

findings.title: No SLOs, error budgets, or latency/uptime metrics
findings.whats_missing: grep for SLO/error_budget/p95/p99/uptime finds essentially nothing; there are no defined service objectives or measured pipeline latency/success-rate metrics for the overnight run or n8n control plane.
findings.end_goal: Defined SLOs (run success rate, pipeline latency p95, data-freshness) with measured metrics and an error budget that auto-tightens live influence when burned.
findings.evidence: grep 'SLO|error_budget|p95|p99|uptime' returns only one unrelated hit in dataflows/_official_common.py

findings.title: No metrics/tracing backend (Prometheus/OpenTelemetry)
findings.whats_missing: No statsd/Prometheus/OpenTelemetry instrumentation exists; runtime visibility relies on JSON files and emails, with no time-series for latency, token spend, API error rates, or fill counts.
findings.end_goal: OpenTelemetry traces and Prometheus-style counters/histograms for pipeline stages, LLM calls, broker calls, and data fetches, scraped into a metrics store for dashboards and alerting.
findings.evidence: grep 'prometheus|opentelemetry|statsd|histogram' returns no source hits

findings.title: No data-quality validation layer (stale-quote / split-adjust / anomaly)
findings.whats_missing: There is no centralized validator that detects stale quotes, missing/unadjusted splits & dividends, zero-volume bars, or outlier prints before data feeds agent decisions or ledger resolution.
findings.end_goal: A data-quality gate that timestamps freshness, verifies split/dividend adjustment, flags outliers/gaps, and refuses to trade or resolve on stale/anomalous data with a clear reason code.
findings.evidence: no data_quality/stale/survivorship module under dataflows; resolve_forecasts (ledger:802) trusts raw price_lookup output

findings.title: No survivorship-bias control in historical universe
findings.whats_missing: Backtest/calibration draw from current watchlists and live price sources with no delisted-name handling, so historical evaluation systematically excludes failed tickers and overstates skill.
findings.end_goal: A point-in-time universe with delisted constituents and historical membership so walk-forward and backtest results are free of survivorship bias.
findings.evidence: replay_ablation POINT_IN_TIME_AUDIT_ROWS references y_finance.py for ohlcv; no delisted-universe handling exists

findings.title: No A/B harness for agent configs and prompts
findings.whats_missing: prompt_registry and model_routing exist but there is no controlled experiment harness that runs two agent/prompt/model configurations on the same inputs and compares calibrated outcomes with significance.
findings.end_goal: An A/B evaluation harness that pins inputs, runs config arms (prompt variants, model routes, debate depth), and reports outcome deltas with confidence intervals to drive prompt/model selection.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/research/prompt_registry.py and research/model_routing.py exist but no experiment/AB runner module found

findings.title: Secrets stored in plaintext .env, not a vault/keyring
findings.whats_missing: .env holds 16 API_KEY/SECRET/TOKEN entries in plaintext on disk; there is no integration with OS keyring, HashiCorp Vault, or a secrets manager, and no key rotation.
findings.end_goal: Secrets sourced from a vault/keyring/secrets-manager with least-privilege scopes and rotation, with .env used only for non-secret config.
findings.evidence: .env contains 16 secret-shaped keys (grep count); no keyring/vault integration in tradingagents source

findings.title: No CI pipeline (.github/workflows absent)
findings.whats_missing: There is no .github/workflows directory, so the 79 test files, ruff, and mypy are never run automatically; regressions in money-movement code can merge unchecked.
findings.end_goal: A CI workflow that runs ruff, mypy, and the full pytest suite (with coverage gate) on every push/PR, plus a fail-closed check on live-safety tests before merge.
findings.evidence: ls .github/workflows -> 'NO .github/workflows'; 79 test files exist under tests/

findings.title: Money-movement code excluded from type checking (ignore_errors=true)
findings.whats_missing: pyproject mypy sets ignore_errors=true for tradingagents.brokers.*, dataflows.*, execution.*, and policy.* — exactly the order-submission and risk-gate code — so type errors there are invisible.
findings.end_goal: Strict (or at least non-ignored) mypy on brokers/execution/policy with a tracked debt list, so the order-path and gates are type-checked like the rest.
findings.evidence: pyproject.toml:132-139 overrides for brokers.*/dataflows.*/execution.*/policy.* set ignore_errors = true

findings.title: No unified structured logging across pipeline
findings.whats_missing: Only a handful of modules use logging; most flow control writes JSON artifacts ad hoc, with no consistent structured log (run_id, stage, ticker, decision) for tracing a decision end to end.
findings.end_goal: A structured JSON logger threaded with a run/correlation id through every agent stage, data fetch, and broker call, so any decision can be reconstructed from logs alone.
findings.evidence: grep 'structlog|logging.getLogger' hits only ~6 source files; structured.py is the lone helper

findings.title: No append-only tamper-evident compliance audit journal
findings.whats_missing: Decisions and orders are written as mutable JSON files under results/; there is no append-only, hash-chained journal linking research evidence -> decision -> gate result -> order -> fill for compliance review.
findings.end_goal: A hash-chained append-only audit journal capturing the full evidence-to-fill lineage per decision, enabling honest reconstruction and tamper detection.
findings.evidence: results/ artifacts are plain JSON (write_ledger ledger:845 overwrites file); no hash-chain/journal module found

findings.title: No deterministic seeded runs or replay reproducibility
findings.whats_missing: There is no global seed/PYTHONHASHSEED control or pinned LLM temperature=0 policy for replay; identical inputs cannot be guaranteed to reproduce identical decisions, undermining the replay/ablation plan.
findings.end_goal: Seeded, temperature-pinned, snapshot-pinned runs with a deterministic-replay mode that reproduces a prior decision byte-for-byte from a recorded input snapshot.
findings.evidence: grep 'random.seed|PYTHONHASHSEED|deterministic' shows scattered hits, no central seeding; replay_ablation is plan-only

findings.title: No pinned point-in-time data snapshots per run
findings.whats_missing: Data is fetched live at run time with no immutable snapshot saved, so a run cannot be re-evaluated against the exact inputs it saw, and backtests can leak future-revised data.
findings.end_goal: Per-run immutable data snapshots (prices, news, fundamentals) stored with the run, enabling exact replay and leak-free point-in-time backtesting.
findings.evidence: dataflows fetch live (e.g., y_finance.py); replay_ablation POINT_IN_TIME_AUDIT_ROWS flags this as an audit area, not implemented

findings.title: No disaster-recovery / state backup of results and ledger
findings.whats_missing: Critical state (ledger, promotion state, results/_context) lives only on the local disk with a dirty git tree; there is no offsite backup or documented restore procedure, so disk loss erases all forecast history.
findings.end_goal: Automated periodic backups of ledger/promotion/results state to durable offsite storage with a tested restore runbook and RPO/RTO targets.
findings.evidence: DEFAULT_LEDGER_PATH writes a single local file (ledger:845-853); no backup/restore module; git tree has 213 uncommitted files

findings.title: No unified live status dashboard (only an n8n POC)
findings.whats_missing: The only dashboard artifact is config/n8n/workflows/status-dashboard-poc.json (a proof of concept); there is no single pane showing run health, positions, exposure vs caps, ledger calibration, latency, and spend.
findings.end_goal: A single status dashboard aggregating pipeline health, open risk vs envelope caps, calibration metrics, broker connectivity, cost/latency, and active alerts.
findings.evidence: find -iname '*dashboard*' -> only config/n8n/workflows/status-dashboard-poc.json

findings.title: Dockerfile/compose lack HEALTHCHECK and readiness probes
findings.whats_missing: The Dockerfile defines no HEALTHCHECK and docker-compose only sets restart:unless-stopped/depends_on with no health-gated startup, so a half-broken container is treated as up.
findings.end_goal: Container HEALTHCHECK and compose service health/readiness probes so orchestration restarts or holds traffic from unhealthy services before they run trades.
findings.evidence: Dockerfile has no HEALTHCHECK line; docker-compose.yml:26/57 only depends_on + restart, no healthcheck

findings.title: Scheduling scattered across PowerShell + n8n with no single source of truth
findings.whats_missing: Jobs are split between scripts/*.ps1 and n8n workflows with no consolidated schedule manifest, making it unclear what runs when, and leaving the ledger-resolution job unscheduled.
findings.end_goal: A single declarative schedule manifest (one cron/n8n source of truth) covering research runs, ledger resolution, calibration refresh, backups, and reconciliation, with drift detection.
findings.evidence: scripts/run-tradingagents-job.ps1 + start-n8n-tradingagents-runner.ps1 + n8n workflows coexist; no unified schedule file

findings.title: Per-run USD cost/latency budgeting exists but is not enforced pipeline-wide
findings.whats_missing: model_routing has evaluate_model_budget_caps with max_cost_usd_per_run and monthly_soft_budget_usd, but there is no aggregation that halts a run when cumulative spend or wall-clock latency for the whole overnight pipeline breaches a hard budget.
findings.end_goal: A run-level cost+latency governor that tracks cumulative USD spend and elapsed time across all agent stages and fail-closes (or degrades model routes) when a hard budget is hit.
findings.evidence: tradingagents/research/model_routing.py:177-217 caps per-call/monthly cost; no pipeline-wide cumulative enforcement found

findings.title: No factor-exposure decomposition (value/growth/momentum/size)
findings.whats_missing: The portfolio has no factor model, so concentration in momentum/AI-beta/size factors (which the calibration guard worries about) is never quantified or capped.
findings.end_goal: A factor-exposure report decomposing the book into style/sector/macro factors with caps, surfaced to the gate and dashboard to prevent unintended factor bets.
findings.evidence: no factor model in source; overnight_calibration.py:183 only flags 'crowded AI beta' qualitatively

findings.title: No anomaly detection on PnL/positions/order flow
findings.whats_missing: Nothing watches for anomalous live behavior (sudden position drift, runaway order rate beyond config, PnL spikes inconsistent with positions) beyond static rate limits and reconciliation.
findings.end_goal: A live anomaly detector that statistically flags abnormal order cadence, position/PnL drift, and reconciliation deltas, triggering a fail-closed halt and page.
findings.evidence: only static order_rate_limit.py and reconcile.py exist; no statistical anomaly monitor in source

findings.title: No performance attribution vs benchmark for live/paper books
findings.whats_missing: The ledger resolves single forecasts vs a benchmark, but there is no portfolio-level attribution (alpha/beta, contribution by name/sector/agent) for the actual paper/live book over time.
findings.end_goal: A periodic attribution report decomposing realized portfolio return into alpha vs benchmark and contribution by position, sector, and originating agent.
findings.evidence: ledger summarize_agent_scores (ledger:856) aggregates per-agent forecast skill, not portfolio attribution

findings.title: No fill/slippage model to make backtests realistic
findings.whats_missing: Even once a backtest engine exists, there is no slippage/commission/partial-fill model, so simulated returns would assume perfect mid fills and overstate edge.
findings.end_goal: A configurable fill model (spread cost, market impact by size, commission, partial fills) shared between backtest and TCA so paper and live results stay comparable.
findings.evidence: no fill/slippage module; sizing/order modules assume notional fills (sizing.py, alpaca.py)

findings.title: No clean reproducible deployment baseline (2 commits, 213 dirty files)
findings.whats_missing: The repo has only 2 commits on a WIP branch with 213 uncommitted files, so there is no tagged, reproducible release artifact to deploy or roll back to; production state is whatever happens to be on disk.
findings.end_goal: A committed, tagged release baseline (clean main, semantic version tag) that the container and schedulers deploy from, enabling rollback and deterministic provenance.
findings.evidence: git log shows 2 commits; git status --short reports 213 files on branch wip/submit-path-hardening-2026-06-05

findings.title: reports and codex not gitignored leaks PII on add-all
findings.whats_missing: gitignore only covers pycache and results; reports has real email PII and codex is commit-eligible, so add-all leaks PII and agent state
findings.end_goal: gitignore and dockerignore cover codex and generated reports; a pre-commit PII and secret scan asserts a clean tree before merge
findings.evidence: git check-ignore empty for reports and codex; gmail in N8N_CONTROL_PLANE_EVALUATION report

findings.title: Three real assessment files never pinned to one canonical merge target
findings.whats_missing: the market-readiness md and json, master plan, and finish plan were never unified, and there is no WIP-close-to-main runbook for the 213-entry working tree
findings.end_goal: one canonical merged assessment and plan at a fixed tracked path with the other two stubbed, plus a sequenced runbook landing all work on main and deleting the stale branch
findings.evidence: files under reports market_readiness and docs superpowers plans 2026-06-08; git diff main 108 files 25557 insertions
